steps.title: Surveys — migration 9997_surveys_head_of_house.sql, RLS tests, domain and db wrappers
steps.goal: A second re-runnable migration `supabase/migrations/9997_surveys_head_of_house.sql` implements founder decision 8 on top of the survey schema already in `9999_init.sql`: the head of house (`household_role = 'head'`) with an account may answer `per_person` surveys for household members without accounts through a new client RPC `submit_survey_response_for(survey_id, person_id, answers)`, `list_survey_proxy_targets(survey_id)` tells a head whom they may answer for, `app.can_answer_for` and an extended `stamp_response_scope` (transaction-local `app.answer_for` setting) enforce the rule at the DB level, `survey_responses.answered_on_behalf` marks proxied rows, and the `survey_responses`/`survey_answers` update policies let the head edit those rows while the survey is open and `allow_edit`. A new RLS test file (`10_surveys_head_of_house.sql`) proves every positive and negative case, `09_grants.sql` includes the two RPCs, types are regenerated, and `@church/domain` (schemas, `validateSurveyAnswers`, status transitions, error keys) and `@church/db` (survey queries, RPC wrappers, query keys) are ready for the web (6.1b) and mobile (6.1c) steps. No UI; the founder gets a 'ready to paste' ledger row.

You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is step 6.1a "Surveys — migration 9997_surveys_head_of_house.sql, RLS tests, domain and db wrappers" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `docs/PLAN.md` §4 (Surveys tables, `stamp_response_scope`, `submit_survey_response`, the permission mapping "surveys = `announcements.create/edit/delete`", the migration skeleton (0)–(11)) and §13 founder answer 8, and `docs/DESIGN.md` §4.2 (Surveys table block), §4.4 (grant lists and RPC semantics), §5 (mapping table), §6 (the `surveys` / `survey_responses` policy rows), §11 Phase 3 and §12, plus `docs/MIGRATIONS.md`, `docs/RLS.md` and `supabase/README.md` before writing code. Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one.

## Goal
When you finish, a second re-runnable migration `supabase/migrations/9997_surveys_head_of_house.sql` implements founder decision 8 — "the HEAD OF HOUSE (`household_role = 'head'`, or an adult designated head when there is no father) may answer `per_person` surveys on behalf of household members without accounts" — on top of the survey schema that `9999_init.sql` already holds: two new client RPCs (`submit_survey_response_for`, `list_survey_proxy_targets`), one helper (`app.can_answer_for`), an extended `stamp_response_scope` trigger, one extra column (`survey_responses.answered_on_behalf`), the adjusted `ca_survey_responses_*` / `ca_survey_answers_*` policies and grants. A new RLS test file proves the rule positively and negatively, `09_grants.sql` still passes with the two new RPCs in the client set, generated types are regenerated, and `@church/domain` / `@church/db` expose typed schemas, error keys, query helpers and query keys that 6.1b (web builder/results/CSV) and 6.1c (mobile responder) consume. No UI in this step. The founder gets a "ready to paste" ledger row in HANDOFF.md.

## Inputs / prior state
- `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` (steps 1.2–1.4c; frozen if the HANDOFF ledger shows it pasted): tables `surveys` (`title, description, audience_group_id not null, response_mode default 'per_person', allow_edit default true, status default 'draft', opens_at, closes_at, push default true, created_by`; check `closes_at > opens_at` when both set), `survey_questions` (`survey_id, org_id, position, kind question_kind, prompt, options jsonb, required`; `unique(survey_id, position)`, `unique(id, survey_id)`), `survey_responses` (`survey_id, org_id, person_id null, household_id null, submitted_by_user_id, scope_key not null, submitted_at, updated_at`; `unique(survey_id, scope_key)`), `survey_answers` (`response_id fk cascade, question_id, survey_id, org_id, value jsonb`; composite FK `(question_id, survey_id) → survey_questions(id, survey_id)`; `unique(response_id, question_id)`). Enums `survey_status (draft, open, closed)`, `response_mode (per_person, per_household)`, `question_kind (short_text, long_text, single_choice, multi_choice, yes_no, number, date)`. No `anonymous` column (Phase 4).
- Trigger functions from 1.3a: `app.freeze_survey_shape` (raises `survey_shape_frozen` P0001 once `status <> 'draft'`), `app.stamp_response_scope` (before insert/update on `survey_responses`: overwrites `person_id`/`household_id`/`scope_key`/`submitted_by_user_id` from the caller — `app.my_person_id(org)` — and raises `no_person_linked` when null), `app.on_content_publish` (enqueues a `notifications` row of kind `survey` when `status = 'open'` and `push`), `app.cancel_notifications_on_delete`. Read their real bodies in the file before touching them — the exact scope-key format (`person:<uuid>` / `household:<uuid>` or whatever 1.3a chose) must be preserved.
- RPC from 1.3b: `submit_survey_response(survey_id uuid, answers jsonb) returns uuid` — `require_user`; `survey_not_open`; `survey_not_in_audience` (`app.user_in_group(audience_group_id)`); `answers` is `{question_id: value}` with keys belonging to the survey else `invalid_payload`; unique violation → `survey_already_responded` unless `allow_edit` (then update + replace answers); `survey_edit_not_allowed`. Its error keys live in the section (5c) comment block; 1.3b explicitly deferred decision 8 to this step.
- Policies from 1.4a: `surveys`/`survey_questions` select = member ∧ open ∧ in window ∧ in audience, or `announcements.create`; insert `announcements.create`; update `announcements.edit`; delete `announcements.delete`. `survey_responses` select = own (`person_id = app.my_person_id(org)` or `household_id = any(app.my_household_ids())`) or the three announcement permissions; insert member ∧ writable ∧ open/in window/in audience; update own ∧ open ∧ `allow_edit` (per_household → any adult via `my_household_ids`); no delete. `survey_answers` via `exists` on the visible/own response. Read the exact policy names in the file (`ca_survey_responses_select`, `ca_survey_responses_insert`, `ca_survey_responses_update`, `ca_survey_answers_*` — whatever 1.4a named them).
- Helpers: `app.my_person_id(org)`, `app.my_household_ids()`, `app.user_in_group(group)`, `app.person_in_group(person, group)`, `app.can_edit_household(hh)`, `app.require_user()`, `app.require_writable(org)`, `app.has_perm`, `app.is_super_admin()`. Head of house = `persons.household_role = 'head'`, at most one per household (partial unique index from orchestrator decision 6; the designation UI is 5.1a/5.2b and, if adopted, the atomic `set_head_of_house` RPC of proposed step 5.8).
- Tests: `supabase/tests/helpers.sql` (`app_test.login(uid)`, `login_anon()`, `logout()`, `assert_count`, `assert_raises`, `assert_denied`), `supabase/tests/rls/01…09` — `06_events_surveys.sql` already covers open/closed/window/audience/shape-freeze/`survey_already_responded`/`no_person_linked`/per-household double response; `09_grants.sql` asserts the exact client RPC set via `has_function_privilege`. `scripts/db/{local-up,apply-migrations,check-rerunnable,test,gen-types}.sh`. If `supabase/migrations/9998_join_codes.sql` (5.6) exists, `apply-migrations.sh` applies files highest-number-first — confirm by reading it.
- Packages: `packages/domain/src/schemas/surveys.ts` (1.6b: `surveySchema`, `surveyQuestionSchema`, `surveyAnswersSchema`, `submitSurveyResponseSchema`), `packages/domain/src/errors.ts` (1.6b: `toDomainError`, the key catalogue), `packages/domain/src/permissions.ts` (`canManageSurveys`), `packages/db/src/rpc.ts` (1.7a: `submitSurveyResponse(db, { survey_id, answers })`), `packages/db/src/queries/surveys.ts` (3.6a created it with only the getter the dispatcher needs), `packages/db/src/keys.ts`, `packages/db/src/database.types.ts` (generated), `packages/db/src/type-tests/enum-parity.test-d.ts`.
- Ledger: `HANDOFF.md` "Applied migrations" says which files the founder has pasted. 9997 was reserved for surveys by 3.5b/3.6a/5.8; if the ledger shows 9997 taken, use the next free lower number and record it.

## Build
1. **Migration `supabase/migrations/9997_surveys_head_of_house.sql`**, following the skeleton in PLAN §4 / `docs/MIGRATIONS.md` and the per-construct rules (policies/triggers `drop … if exists` then `create`; columns `add column if not exists`; functions `create or replace`; every function `security definer set search_path = ''`; schema-qualified everything; policy names `ca_`; no `force row level security`; no enum value additions — none are needed). Header comment: purpose, founder decision 8 quoted, "re-runnable; paste after 9999_init.sql (and 9998 if present)", and the list of objects it (re)defines. Sections:
   - (0) the same owner `rolbypassrls` assertion as 9999.
   - (3) `alter table public.survey_responses add column if not exists answered_on_behalf boolean not null default false;` — true when the response was submitted by someone other than the person it is for; lets results, CSV and the mobile list say "answered by head of house" without joining `persons.user_id`.
   - (5) `create or replace function app.can_answer_for(target_person uuid) returns boolean` (stable, definer): true iff the caller has a person in the same org as the target (`app.my_person_id(target.org_id)`), that caller person has `household_role = 'head'` and `household_id = target.household_id`, and the target has **no usable account** — `user_id is null`, OR the linked account is archived per orchestrator decision 15 (`profiles.archived_at is not null`, or whatever archival column/helper the G2/G3 fixers put into `9999_init.sql` — `grep -n archived_at supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql`; if no such column exists yet, skip this branch and say so in `docs/RLS.md`), OR the linked user has no `active` row in `org_memberships` for the survey's org — and additionally `deceased_on is null`, `congregation_status in ('member','attendee')` and is not the caller. The `detail` reason `person_has_account` is raised only when the account is usable (active membership, not archived). Record this reading ('a deactivated or disabled family member may be answered for by the head') in `docs/RLS.md` and under HANDOFF Decisions. Super admins do not get a bypass here (answering surveys is a member act).
   - (5) `create or replace function app.stamp_response_scope()` — keep 1.3a's behaviour for the normal path byte-for-byte and add the proxy path: when `current_setting('app.answer_for', true)` is a non-empty uuid, require `app.can_answer_for(that uuid)` (else raise `survey_proxy_not_allowed` with errcode `42501` and a `detail` naming the reason: `not_head_of_house` / `different_household` / `person_has_account` / `person_not_active`), require the survey's `response_mode = 'per_person'` (else `survey_not_per_person`, `22023`), then stamp `person_id = target`, `household_id = target.household_id`, `scope_key` in the same format 1.3a uses for a person scope, `submitted_by_user_id = auth.uid()`, `answered_on_behalf = true`. On UPDATE with the setting, the proxy path applies only when the existing row's `person_id` equals the target. On UPDATE **without** the setting: if `old.answered_on_behalf` is true, keep `old.person_id`, `old.household_id`, `old.scope_key` and `old.answered_on_behalf` unchanged (the update policy already proved `app.can_answer_for(old.person_id)`) and refresh only `submitted_by_user_id = auth.uid()` — never re-stamp a proxied row to the head's own person, which would silently re-attribute the child's answers or collide with the head's own `(survey_id, scope_key)` row; otherwise apply 1.3a's normal re-stamp and set `answered_on_behalf = false`. On INSERT without the setting always stamp the self path with `answered_on_behalf = false`. The setting is read with `current_setting(name, true)` and is only ever set transaction-locally (`set_config(…, …, true)`) by the RPC below; a direct table insert from PostgREST can never carry it, so client inserts stay self-only.
   - (5) `create or replace function public.submit_survey_response_for(survey_id uuid, person_id uuid, answers jsonb) returns uuid` (definer, `search_path = ''`): `perform app.require_user()`; load the survey (raise `survey_not_found`/`P0002` when missing — reuse an existing key if 1.3b has one); `app.require_writable(org_id)`; `app.can_answer_for(person_id)` else `survey_proxy_not_allowed` (42501); `response_mode = 'per_person'` else `survey_not_per_person` (22023); open + in window else `survey_not_open`; **the target person** in the audience via `app.person_in_group(person_id, audience_group_id)` else `survey_not_in_audience` (the head's own membership in the audience is irrelevant — a men's survey may be answered by a father for a son without an account); validate `answers` keys exactly as `submit_survey_response` does (factor the shared validation into `app.validate_survey_answers(survey_id, answers)` if 1.3b did not already, and have both RPCs call it — `create or replace` of `submit_survey_response` is allowed because the signature does not change); `perform set_config('app.answer_for', person_id::text, true)`; insert the response (the trigger stamps scope) mapping the `(survey_id, scope_key)` unique violation to `survey_already_responded` unless `allow_edit`, in which case update the existing row for that person and replace its answers (`survey_edit_not_allowed` when `allow_edit` is false); `perform set_config('app.answer_for', '', true)` in every exit path (use a nested block with `exception when others then … raise`); return the response id. Audit: if `app.audit_row` is trigger-only, do not add rows by hand — record in `docs/RLS.md` that proxy responses are identifiable by `answered_on_behalf` + `submitted_by_user_id`.
   - (5) `create or replace function public.list_survey_proxy_targets(survey_id uuid) returns jsonb` (definer): `require_user`; returns `[]` unless the caller's person is `head` of a household in the survey's org; otherwise a JSON array of `{ person_id, first_name, last_name, preferred_name, household_role, in_audience boolean, response_id uuid|null, submitted_at timestamptz|null }` for every household member for whom `app.can_answer_for(person_id)` is true, ordered by `household_role` then `last_name, first_name`. Reads `persons` directly inside the definer function (directory reads from clients must go through `directory_persons` — DESIGN §5/§6; the definer RPC reads `persons` only for the caller's own household, which `directory_persons` already shows them, and it is an RPC rather than a view because it also evaluates `app.can_answer_for` per row); it exposes only names and role of the caller's own household.
   - (7) `drop trigger if exists … ; create trigger` for `stamp_response_scope` on `survey_responses` only if 1.3a's trigger name must change — otherwise leave 9999's trigger in place (the function body was replaced in place).
   - (8) `drop policy if exists` + `create policy` for the `survey_responses` and `survey_answers` policies you must widen (re-create only those, with their 1.4a names): select — add the branch "the caller is head of a household and the response's `person_id` is a member of that household with `answered_on_behalf`" — in practice `household_id = any(app.my_household_ids())` from 1.4a already covers it; verify and keep as is if so; update — add `or (answered_on_behalf and app.can_answer_for(person_id))` alongside the existing own/adult branch, still ∧ survey open ∧ `allow_edit`; `survey_answers` select/insert/update mirror through the `exists` on the parent response. No delete policies. Every policy keeps the `app.org_writable` requirement on writes.
   - (9) `revoke execute on function public.submit_survey_response_for(uuid, uuid, jsonb), public.list_survey_proxy_targets(uuid), app.can_answer_for(uuid) from public;` then `grant execute … to authenticated` (and `app.can_answer_for` to `authenticated` because a policy calls it, like 1.4a did for the other `app.*` helpers referenced in policies). `service_role` gets nothing new.
   - Error catalogue: add to the comment block (or wherever 1.3b keeps the catalogue) `survey_proxy_not_allowed 42501`, `survey_not_per_person 22023`, plus `survey_not_found P0002` if new. Keep `raise … using errcode = …, message = '<key>', detail = '<reason>'` in the same style as 1.3b so `toDomainError` maps them.
2. **Apply and check locally** in the standing sequence; `apply-migrations.sh` twice must succeed with 9997 in place; `check-rerunnable.sh` must pass (it enforces the static rules on every migration file).
3. **RLS tests** — new file `supabase/tests/rls/10_surveys_head_of_house.sql` (same harness; `begin … rollback`): fixture = one org with a household of four persons — `head` with an account (`user_id` set, active membership), `spouse` with an account, `child` (age below `adult_min_age`, no account), `other` adult without an account — plus a second household whose `head` has an account, and — guarded by `if exists (select 1 from information_schema.columns where table_schema = 'public' and table_name = 'profiles' and column_name = 'archived_at')` so the file passes before and after the decision-15 columns land — a fifth member of the first household, `archived_kid`, linked to an account whose profile is archived (`archived_at = now()`, `archive_reason = 'user'`), and a sixth member `disabled_adult` whose only membership in the org is `disabled`; an `everyone` `per_person` open survey with two questions, a third `per_person` survey used only for the direct-insert re-stamp assertion, and a `men` survey; assert: head submits `submit_survey_response_for(survey, child, …)` → one `survey_responses` row with `person_id = child`, `household_id = the household`, `submitted_by_user_id = head`, `answered_on_behalf = true`, `scope_key` equal to what a self-submission for that person would produce; head sees that response and its answers (`assert_count`), spouse (same household) sees it too; the other household's head gets 0 rows; head for `spouse` (has an account) → `survey_proxy_not_allowed` with detail `person_has_account`; spouse (not head) for `child` → `survey_proxy_not_allowed` / `not_head_of_house`; other household's head for `child` → `different_household`; head for `child` on a `per_household` survey → `survey_not_per_person`; head for the `other` adult on the `men` survey when that person is female → `survey_not_in_audience`; second submission with `allow_edit = true` updates in place (still 1 row, answers replaced), with `allow_edit = false` → `survey_already_responded`; head updating the proxied row through a direct `update survey_responses` under RLS succeeds while open and `allow_edit`, and AFTER that update the row still has `person_id = child`, `answered_on_behalf = true`, the same `scope_key`, `submitted_by_user_id = head`, and the head's own self-response (submitted earlier in the test) is untouched — the trigger must not re-stamp a proxied row; the same direct update fails (0 rows) after `closed`; a direct `insert into survey_responses` by the head with `person_id = child` on the THIRD survey (run this BEFORE any self-submission by the head on that survey so the re-stamped row cannot collide on `(survey_id, scope_key)`) is re-stamped to the head's own person — assert the resulting row has `person_id = head` and `answered_on_behalf = false` — proving proxies only flow through the RPC; inside the `if exists` guard: head for `archived_kid` → allowed (row with `person_id = archived_kid`, `answered_on_behalf = true`) and head for `disabled_adult` → allowed, while `list_survey_proxy_targets` as head lists both; `list_survey_proxy_targets(survey)` as head → 2 entries (`child` with `response_id` set after the proxy, `other`), as spouse → `[]`, as the other household's head → its own household's members only; `anon` → 42501 on both RPCs; suspended org → `organization_suspended` from `submit_survey_response_for`. Update `09_grants.sql` so the intended client RPC set includes the two new functions and `authenticated` still cannot execute any `srv_*`. Extend `08_rerunnable.sql` only if it hard-codes object counts that 9997 changes (it should count after ALL migrations).
4. **Typegen**: `scripts/db/gen-types.sh` → `packages/db/src/database.types.ts` picks up the new column and the two RPCs; `enum-parity.test-d.ts` unchanged (no new enums).
5. **`@church/domain`**: `schemas/surveys.ts` — add `submitSurveyResponseForSchema` (`survey_id`, `person_id`, `answers: surveyAnswersSchema`), `surveyProxyTargetSchema` (the JSON shape above, `z.looseObject` like the other RPC results) and `surveyProxyTargetsSchema = z.array(...)`, `surveyResponseSchema` (row shape incl. `answered_on_behalf`), and a pure `validateSurveyAnswers(questions, answers)` → `{ ok: true } | { ok: false, errors: Record<question_id, string> }` enforcing `required`, `single_choice`/`multi_choice` values ∈ `options`, `yes_no` boolean, `number` finite, `date` `YYYY-MM-DD`, text length ≤ 2000 — the client-side mirror of what the RPC/DB accept (keep the DB as the authority; this exists so forms can show inline errors); `surveyStatusTransitions` = `{ draft: ['open'], open: ['closed'], closed: [] }` with `canTransitionSurvey(from, to)`, and `surveyStatusLabels: Record<survey_status, string>` = `{ draft: 'Draft', open: 'Open', closed: 'Closed' }` (6.1b and 6.1c import it — define it here, not in the apps). `errors.ts`: add `survey_proxy_not_allowed`, `survey_not_per_person`, `survey_not_found` with their SQLSTATEs and human messages (the proxy message uses the `detail` reason: "Only the head of house can answer for family members", "This person already has an account and answers for themselves", "This person is not in your household", "This person is not active in the directory"). Vitest cases for the validator (every kind, valid + invalid) and the transitions.
6. **`@church/db`**: `rpc.ts` — `submitSurveyResponseFor(db, { survey_id, person_id, answers })` → uuid, `listSurveyProxyTargets(db, { survey_id })` → parsed with `surveyProxyTargetsSchema`. `queries/surveys.ts` (extend 3.6a's getter additively): `listSurveys(db, orgId, { status? })` ordered `created_at desc`, `getSurvey(db, id)`, `listSurveyQuestions(db, surveyId)` ordered by `position`, `insertSurvey`, `updateSurvey`, `deleteSurvey`, `replaceSurveyQuestions(db, surveyId, questions[])` (delete-then-insert inside the draft state; the DB refuses after draft), `setSurveyStatus(db, id, status, { opens_at?, closes_at? })`, `listSurveyResponsesWithAnswers(db, surveyId)` (responses + nested answers; managers), `listOpenSurveysForMe(db, orgId)` (RLS does the audience/window filtering — a plain select ordered by `closes_at nulls last`), `getMyResponse(db, surveyId, { person_id?, household_id? })`, `countSurveyResponses`. `keys.ts`: `queryKeys.surveys.list(orgId)`, `.detail(id)`, `.questions(id)`, `.responses(id)`, `.myResponse(id, scopeId)`, `.proxyTargets(id)`. Unit tests with the mocked client pattern 1.7a uses.
7. **Docs**: `docs/RLS.md` — a "Surveys and head of house" subsection: the rule, the `app.answer_for` transaction setting, why proxies only flow through the RPC, the known consequence "if the head of house has no account but the spouse does, nobody can answer for the children until the household designates the account holder as head (5.1a/5.2b)", and the "Hidden household" consequence for survey managers who are not directory admins. `docs/MIGRATIONS.md` — add 9997 to the file list with its paste order. `supabase/README.md` — paste order now `9999 → (9998) → 9997`.

## Constraints
- Do not edit `9999_init.sql` if the HANDOFF ledger shows it pasted (frozen). If it is NOT yet pasted, still put this work in 9997 — the founder decided surveys are Phase 3 and the skeleton names this file. Never `supabase db push` / `db reset`; the founder pastes by hand.
- Signatures of existing RPCs are frozen (1.3b): do not add parameters to `submit_survey_response`; add the new RPC instead. Do not rename policies, triggers or error keys that `06_events_surveys.sql`, `@church/domain` or web/mobile already depend on.
- No UI, no `apps/web` or `apps/mobile` changes in this step (6.1b/6.1c). No anonymous mode, no Phase 4 columns.
- Pins unchanged (TypeScript ~5.9, Zod 4.5, supabase-js 2.112, Vitest 4). No new dependencies. No model identifiers, no secrets, no real email addresses anywhere.

## Verify
- `scripts/db/local-up.sh && scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh && scripts/db/test.sh` → all green, including the new `10_surveys_head_of_house.sql`, the extended `09_grants.sql` and the unchanged `06_events_surveys.sql`.
- `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "\df public.submit_survey_response_for" -c "\df public.list_survey_proxy_targets"` → both listed once, `security definer`; `select proconfig from pg_proc where proname in ('submit_survey_response_for','list_survey_proxy_targets','can_answer_for')` → every row contains `search_path=`.
- `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "select column_name from information_schema.columns where table_name = 'survey_responses' and column_name = 'answered_on_behalf'"` → 1 row.
- `bash scripts/db/gen-types.sh && git diff --stat packages/db/src/database.types.ts` → the file changed (new column + RPCs); `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → every task succeeds (domain validator tests, db query tests, enum parity).
- `grep -n "survey_proxy_not_allowed\|survey_not_per_person" packages/domain/src/errors.ts supabase/migrations/9997_surveys_head_of_house.sql` → present in both.

## Goal
When you finish, a church leader with `announcements.create` can build a survey at `/o/<slug>/surveys/new` (title, description, audience group, response mode per person / per household, window, allow edits, push), add and reorder questions of the seven kinds, open it (which enqueues a push of kind `survey` through the existing trigger and dispatcher), watch responses arrive at `/o/<slug>/surveys/<surveyId>` with per-question summaries and a response table that names people through the directory views, close it, and download a CSV. `announcements.edit` holders edit/open/close, `announcements.delete` holders delete. Members do not answer on the web (mobile, 6.1c); the response table already marks rows answered by a head of house on behalf of a family member. Playwright smoke covers the pages; the full E2E gets one survey scenario.

- Tick step 6.1b in `docs/TODO.md`; write `session_log.md`; commit `feat(web): surveys builder, open/close with push, results and CSV export`; push `main` (or the branch I named).

steps.title: Surveys (mobile) — responder, head-of-house 'answer for' flow, push target
steps.goal: Members answer surveys in the Anacast app: More → Surveys lists open surveys in their audience split into 'To answer' and 'Answered' (editable while open when `allow_edit`), `surveys/[id]` renders the seven question kinds with Paper controls, validates with `validateSurveyAnswers`, submits through `submit_survey_response` and maps every survey error key to member-facing copy (per-household double answer, closed, not addressed, no linked person, suspended org). The head of house sees an 'Answer for a family member' section fed by `list_survey_proxy_targets` and answers for household members without accounts through `submit_survey_response_for` on `surveys/[id]/for/[personId]` — founder decision 8 implemented end to end. Survey pushes (`data.url = /surveys/<id>`) navigate instead of being ignored, the Surveys notification switch is unhidden, and `expo-doctor` / `expo export` stay clean.
steps.prompt:
You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is step 6.1c "Surveys (mobile) — responder, head-of-house 'answer for' flow, push target" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `docs/PLAN.md` §4 (Surveys tables, `submit_survey_response`, permission mapping), §9 (mobile screen map, push `data.url` handling), §13 founder answer 8, and `docs/DESIGN.md` §5 (founder decision 8 delta at the end of §13), §6 (`surveys`/`survey_responses` policy rows), §10 (More tab entries "Surveys", stacks `surveys/*`, push handling), §11 Phase 3, plus `docs/RLS.md` "Surveys and head of house" (6.1a) and `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` before writing code. Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one.

## Goal
When you finish, a member opens More → Surveys (or taps a survey push) and sees the open surveys they belong to, answers each once (or edits their answer while the survey is open and `allow_edit` is on), gets a clear "already answered" state, and — when they are the head of house (`household_role = 'head'`) — sees an "Answer for a family member" section listing household members without accounts who are in the survey's audience, with an "Answered" mark after each is done. Per-household surveys tell a second adult that the household already answered. Survey pushes (`data.url = /surveys/<id>`) navigate to the survey; the Surveys switch in notification settings is no longer hidden. `npx expo-doctor` and `npx expo export --platform android` stay clean.

## Inputs / prior state
- DB (6.1a on top of 9999): `surveys` (`title, description, audience_group_id, response_mode per_person|per_household, allow_edit, status draft|open|closed, opens_at, closes_at, push`), `survey_questions` (`position, kind, prompt, options jsonb, required`), `survey_responses` (`person_id, household_id, submitted_by_user_id, scope_key, answered_on_behalf, submitted_at, updated_at`), `survey_answers` (`question_id, value jsonb`). RLS: a member selects `surveys`/`survey_questions` only while `open` ∧ inside the window ∧ in the audience, and `survey_responses` only for own person/household (so "did I answer?" is a plain select). RPCs: `submit_survey_response(survey_id, answers)` (self; errors `survey_not_open`, `survey_not_in_audience`, `survey_already_responded`, `survey_edit_not_allowed`, `invalid_payload`, `no_person_linked`, `organization_suspended`), `submit_survey_response_for(survey_id, person_id, answers)` (head of house for a household member without an account; `survey_proxy_not_allowed` with detail `not_head_of_house` / `different_household` / `person_has_account` / `person_not_active`, `survey_not_per_person`), `list_survey_proxy_targets(survey_id)` → `[{ person_id, first_name, last_name, preferred_name, household_role, in_audience, response_id, submitted_at }]` (empty unless the caller is head of house).
- Packages (6.1a): `@church/domain` `schemas/surveys.ts` (`surveySchema`, `surveyQuestionSchema`, `surveyAnswersSchema`, `submitSurveyResponseSchema`, `submitSurveyResponseForSchema`, `surveyProxyTargetsSchema`, `validateSurveyAnswers(questions, answers)`), `errors.ts` (`toDomainError`, messages for the survey keys), `urls.ts` `notificationTargetPath('survey', id)` = `/surveys/<id>`; `@church/db` `queries/surveys.ts` (`listOpenSurveysForMe(db, orgId)`, `getSurvey`, `listSurveyQuestions`, `getMyResponse(db, surveyId, { person_id?, household_id? })`), `rpc.ts` (`submitSurveyResponse`, `submitSurveyResponseFor`, `listSurveyProxyTargets`), `queryKeys.surveys.{list, detail, questions, myResponse, proxyTargets}`. Read the real signatures first; extend additively with tests if something is missing and record it.
- Mobile (G11/G12, read the code): `app/(app)/_layout.tsx` stack registration, `(tabs)/more.tsx` + `src/features/more/MoreMenu.tsx` (4.3 left `TODO(6.x)` comments where Surveys and Delete account rows go), `useActiveOrg()` → `{ org: { org_id, slug, name, status }, permissions, personId, householdId, orgs, switchOrg }` from `src/features/org/ActiveOrgProvider.tsx` (read it; the org id is `org.org_id`, nested — there is no top-level `orgId`), `useSession`, `src/lib/supabase.ts`, `src/lib/query-client.ts` (TanStack Query + kv persister; `staleTime` 5 min), `src/components/{Screen,LoadingState,ErrorState,EmptyState}.tsx`, React Native Paper theme (`src/theme.ts`), `src/features/push/useNotificationNavigation.ts` + `src/lib/deep-links.ts` `resolveNotificationTarget` (4.3 returns `{ kind: 'ignore', reason: 'not_built' }` for `surveys`; 5.3b switched `events` on), `src/features/push/NotificationSettings.tsx` (the `surveys` switch is hidden "until 6.1"), `src/features/household/{MyHousehold,HeadOfHouse,rules}.ts(x)` (5.2b: `canEditHousehold`, the head-of-house picker — reuse its person naming/format helpers from `src/features/directory/format.ts`), `src/features/events/*` (5.3b: the newest list/detail/submit pattern to copy).
- Founder decision 8 (quote it in the UI copy and in HANDOFF): "the HEAD OF HOUSE (`household_role = 'head'`, or an adult designated head when there is no father) may answer `per_person` surveys on behalf of household members without accounts."

## Build
1. **Hooks** `src/features/surveys/useSurveys.ts` (TanStack Query over the user client): `useOpenSurveys(orgId)` (`orgId` = `useActiveOrg().org.org_id`) → `listOpenSurveysForMe` (RLS filters to open/in-window/in-audience) + `listMyResponses(db, surveyIds: string[])` — add this helper additively to `packages/db/src/queries/surveys.ts` with a mocked-client test (one query on `survey_responses` filtered `survey_id in (...)`, explicit columns, own rows only by RLS; 6.1a's `getMyResponse` is single-survey and the Constraints forbid raw `from()` calls in the app) → `{ survey, myResponse }[]`; `useSurvey(id)` → `getSurvey` + `listSurveyQuestions` (the select policy returns nothing once the survey closes — treat "not found" as "closed or not available to you"); `useMyResponse(surveyId)` keyed by the scope the survey uses (`per_person` → `personId`, `per_household` → `householdId` from `useActiveOrg()`); `useProxyTargets(surveyId, enabled)` → `listSurveyProxyTargets` parsed with `surveyProxyTargetsSchema`, enabled only when the survey is `per_person` and `open`; mutations `useSubmitResponse()` (`submitSurveyResponse`) and `useSubmitResponseFor()` (`submitSurveyResponseFor`) invalidating `queryKeys.surveys.list`, `.myResponse`, `.proxyTargets`. Persisted cache holds no answers — answers can be personal: add the `queryKeys.surveys.myResponse` and `queryKeys.surveys.proxyTargets` prefixes to the deny list inside `shouldPersistQuery` in `packages/db/src/keys.ts` (additive, with a test — 4.1a's persister combines `shouldPersistQuery(queryKey)` with `meta.persist !== false`) AND set `meta: { persist: false }` on those queries (belt and braces, as 4.2a's signed-URL queries do).
2. **List** `app/(app)/surveys/index.tsx` → `src/features/surveys/SurveyList.tsx`: sections "To answer" (no response yet) and "Answered" (response exists; subtitle "You can change your answer until <closes_at>" when `allow_edit`, else "Answer submitted"); each row title, closes-at in the org timezone (`formatInstantInZone` equivalent already on mobile — reuse 4.2a's date helper), mode badge "Per family" for `per_household`; head-of-house rows also show "N of M family members answered" from `useProxyTargets` (only for `per_person`). Empty state "No open surveys right now". Pull-to-refresh. More tab row "Surveys" (`/surveys`) replaces the 4.3 placeholder, placed after Calendar/Documents per DESIGN §10 order.
3. **Responder** `app/(app)/surveys/[id].tsx` → `src/features/surveys/SurveyResponder.tsx` + `src/features/surveys/QuestionField.tsx` (one component per `question_kind` using Paper controls: `short_text` `TextInput`, `long_text` multiline, `single_choice` `RadioButton.Group`, `multi_choice` `Checkbox.Item` list, `yes_no` two `SegmentedButtons`, `number` numeric `TextInput` (`keyboardType="decimal-pad"`, parsed to a number), `date` masked `YYYY-MM-DD` `TextInput` (no new native module; use `@react-native-community/datetimepicker` only if 5.x already installed it via `npx expo install`)). Answer state as `Record<question_id, unknown>`; validation with `validateSurveyAnswers(questions, answers)` shown inline under each field; submit button disabled while invalid or org not writable (`status in ('suspended','cancelled')` → banner "Your church's account is suspended; surveys are read-only"). Header: description, window ("Closes <date>" or "Open until closed"), mode note ("One answer per family — anyone in your household can submit it; the last saved answer counts" for `per_household`, or "Your personal answer" for `per_person`). Existing response (`useMyResponse`) → prefill; if `allow_edit` false → read-only summary "Answer submitted on <date>"; if true → "Update answer". Error mapping through `toDomainError`: `survey_already_responded` (per_household second adult, or a race) → refetch and show "Your household has already answered this survey" with the read-only view; `survey_not_open` → "This survey has closed"; `survey_not_in_audience` → "This survey is not addressed to you"; `no_person_linked` → "Your account is not linked to a directory person yet — ask your church"; `organization_suspended` → the banner text. Success → `Snackbar` "Answer saved" and return to the list.
4. **Answer for a family member** (`src/features/surveys/AnswerForSection.tsx` rendered at the bottom of the responder when the survey is `per_person` and `useProxyTargets` returns ≥ 1 entry): heading "Answer for a family member", helper text "As head of house you can answer for family members who do not have their own account" (founder decision 8), one row per target (`preferredOrFirst last` via the directory format helper, role label, "Not in this survey's audience" greyed when `in_audience` is false, "Answered <date>" with an Edit affordance when `response_id` is set and `allow_edit`, else "Answer"). Tapping opens `app/(app)/surveys/[id]/for/[personId].tsx` → `src/features/surveys/ProxyResponder.tsx`, the same `QuestionField` form with a persistent chip "Answering for <name>", prefilled from that person's response when present (query `survey_responses` by `survey_id` + `person_id` — visible to the head by RLS), submitted through `useSubmitResponseFor`. Errors: `survey_proxy_not_allowed` → message by `detail` (`person_has_account` → "<name> has their own account now — they answer for themselves"; `not_head_of_house` → "Only the head of house can answer for family members"; `different_household`/`person_not_active` → the `@church/domain` message); `survey_not_per_person` → "Family-wide surveys are answered once per household". If the survey is `per_person` and the caller's own directory row (`directory_persons` where `id = personId` — the client cannot know whether the household's head has an account, because `directory_persons` exposes no `user_id` and `list_survey_proxy_targets` returns `[]` for every non-head without a reason) has `household_role <> 'head'`, show once (in the list header, dismissible via kv key `surveys_head_hint_dismissed`) the hint "Only the head of house can answer for family members without accounts. If your head of house has no account, your household can designate an adult who has one as head under My household" (5.2b's picker; DESIGN/HANDOFF known consequence).
5. **Push and deep links**: in `src/lib/deep-links.ts` switch `surveys` from `{ kind: 'ignore', reason: 'not_built' }` to navigate (`/surveys/<id>` after the 4.3 org switch); update its unit test. `src/features/push/NotificationSettings.tsx`: unhide the **Surveys** switch bound to `notification_preferences.surveys` (defaults true). `grep -rn "not_built" apps/mobile/src` must then return nothing. A cold-start push (`getLastNotificationResponseAsync`) uses the same path — verify 4.3's handler covers it.
6. **Navigation**: register `surveys/index`, `surveys/[id]`, `surveys/[id]/for/[personId]` in the `(app)` stack layout with titles ("Surveys", "Survey", "Answer for family member"). Deep link scheme `anacast://surveys/<id>` resolves through the existing `parseAppLink` if 4.1b supports arbitrary in-app paths; otherwise leave it and note it.
7. **Tests** (Vitest in `apps/mobile`, `src/**/*.test.ts`): answer-state helpers (`toAnswersPayload` dropping empty optional answers, number/date parsing), proxy error-message mapping by `detail`, section grouping in the list (to answer / answered / family progress), `resolveNotificationTarget` survey case. Keep components thin so logic lives in tested pure modules (`src/features/surveys/rules.ts`).
8. **Docs**: `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` — a "Device checklist: surveys" section holding the manual steps from Verify; `docs/MEDIA.md` untouched; HANDOFF mobile section lists the survey screens and the hooks.

## Constraints
- Native dependency versions come only from `npx expo install <pkg>`; this step should need no new native module (masked date field). No `react-hook-form` on mobile (G11 convention). No elevated keys; the mobile client only ever holds the publishable key.
- Reads of people only via `directory_persons` / `list_survey_proxy_targets`; never `select` on `persons`. Do not persist answers in the query cache. No anonymous surveys; no survey management on mobile (leaders use the web, 6.1b).
- Do not change `9999_init.sql` or `9997_surveys_head_of_house.sql`; if a DB change is unavoidable, write the next free descending number recorded in the HANDOFF ledger, re-runnable, and record it. Do not touch web code except `@church/domain`/`@church/db` additive helpers with tests.
- Expo 57 / RN 0.86.3 / React 19.2.3 exact; TanStack Query 5. No model identifiers, no secrets, no real email addresses.

## Verify
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → every task succeeds (mobile Vitest incl. the new survey rules and deep-link cases).
- In `apps/mobile`: `npx expo-doctor` → all checks pass; `npx expo export --platform android` → completes without errors.
- `grep -rn "not_built" apps/mobile/src` → no output; `grep -rn "from('persons')" apps/mobile/src` → no output.
- Device checklist against the hosted project once `9997_surveys_head_of_house.sql` is pasted (HANDOFF ledger) and a preview/dev-client build from 4.5 is installed (there is no local stack the app can sign in to — the local harness has no Auth/PostgREST — and a push needs the hosted project): create a household where the head has an account and a child does not; open a `per_person` survey on the web (6.1b) → the phone receives the push → tapping opens `/surveys/<id>` → answer → "Answer saved" → the survey moves to "Answered"; the "Answer for a family member" section lists the child → answer → "Answered" mark and the web results table shows the row with the head-of-house badge; sign in as the spouse → no "Answer for" section, the dismissible head-of-house hint appears once; a `per_household` survey answered by the head → the spouse sees "Your household has already answered"; close the survey on the web → it disappears from the list and a direct deep link shows "This survey has closed"; toggle the Surveys switch off in notification settings → `notification_preferences.surveys = false` in the DB. This list also goes into `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` (Build 8); if you cannot run it, write it into `session_log.md` for the founder.

## Finish
- `HANDOFF.md`: State — tick "Surveys (6.1c: mobile responder + head-of-house)"; feature table Surveys → Mobile UI "done"; mobile section — new screens (`surveys/index`, `surveys/[id]`, `surveys/[id]/for/[personId]`), hooks, the kv key `surveys_head_hint_dismissed`, the Surveys push switch; Decisions — founder decision 8 marked implemented with the known consequence (head without an account); "Deviations from plan" for anything that differed (for example if `parseAppLink` could not take `/surveys/<id>`).
- Tick step 6.1c in `docs/TODO.md`; write `session_log.md`; commit `feat(mobile): survey list and responder, head-of-house answer-for flow, survey push target`; push `main` (or the branch I named).
- If something in the plan proves impossible or wrong, do the closest correct thing, record it in HANDOFF.md under "Deviations from plan", and report it in your final message.
done_when: `apps/mobile/app/(app)/surveys/index.tsx`, `surveys/[id].tsx` and `surveys/[id]/for/[personId].tsx` exist, are registered in the `(app)` stack, and More → Surveys replaces the 4.3 placeholder row.

A member in the audience of an open `per_person` survey can submit an answer once, sees it under 'Answered', can edit it while `allow_edit` is on, and sees the read-only 'Answer submitted' state when it is off; a second adult on a `per_household` survey gets 'Your household has already answered this survey'.

A head of house (`household_role = 'head'` with an account) sees the 'Answer for a family member' section listing only household members without accounts (from `list_survey_proxy_targets`), can answer for one through `submit_survey_response_for`, and the target then shows 'Answered'; a spouse who is not head sees no section, and `survey_proxy_not_allowed` details map to distinct messages (covered by Vitest).

`src/lib/deep-links.ts` navigates survey pushes to `/surveys/<id>` (unit test updated), `grep -rn "not_built" apps/mobile/src` returns nothing, and the Surveys switch in notification settings writes `notification_preferences.surveys`.
`grep -rn "from('persons')" apps/mobile/src` returns nothing; survey answers are not written to the persisted query cache.

`pnpm turbo lint typecheck test`, `npx expo-doctor` and `npx expo export --platform android` are clean; `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` has the surveys device checklist; HANDOFF.md and docs/TODO.md are updated.
`listMyResponses(db, surveyIds)` exists in `@church/db` with a test and `shouldPersistQuery` denies the `queryKeys.surveys.myResponse`/`.proxyTargets` prefixes (tested).

Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one.

## Goal
When you finish, a church leader holding `org.settings` opens `/o/<slug>/audit` and sees, newest first, who changed what in their church: permission grants and revocations, membership status changes, invitation activity, settings edits, household privacy changes, person status/link changes, share-link creation and revocation, sermon deletions — each row naming the actor (or "System" for trigger/cron work), the table in plain words, the action, the affected row and a readable before/after diff. Filters for table, actor, action, date range (in the church's timezone) and row id live in the URL, pages load with a keyset cursor, and "Download CSV" exports the filtered result. The super admin has the same page across every church at `/admin/audit`, with a church filter and rows without a church (super-admin grants) labelled "Platform". Nothing in the UI can write to `audit_log`; the pages read through RLS with the user client only. `docs/RLS.md` documents what is audited and what is never rendered, and the Playwright suites cover both pages.

## Inputs / prior state
- Database (1.2–1.4c, `9999_init.sql`, frozen if the HANDOFF ledger shows it pasted — check): `audit_log (id bigint generated always as identity primary key, org_id uuid references organizations on delete cascade, actor_user_id uuid, table_name text not null, row_id uuid, action text not null, old_data jsonb, new_data jsonb, created_at timestamptz default now())` with index `(org_id, created_at desc)`. `app.audit_row()` (1.3a) writes `actor_user_id = auth.uid()` (null when a definer function or the cron ran without a user), `action = tg_op` (`INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`), `org_id` from the row (`id` for `organizations`, null for `super_admins`), and for `households`/`persons` only the privacy / status / link columns. RPCs add the synthetic actions `invitation_permissions_dropped` (1.3b `accept_invitation`) and `org_without_manager` (1.3b `srv_process_account_deletions`). Audited tables (DESIGN §4.2): `organizations`, `organization_settings`, `org_memberships`, `org_membership_permissions`, `households` (privacy columns), `persons` (status/link columns), `sermon_share_links`, `sermons` (delete only), `invitations`, `super_admins`. Policy (1.4a): the `ca_audit_log_select_*` policy 1.4a created for `org.settings` holders of the org or super admins (read its exact name in `9999_init.sql` section (8)); no insert/update/delete policies and `revoke insert, update, delete … from authenticated` — the table is append-only for triggers.
- `@church/db` (1.7a): `queries/audit.ts` was explicitly deferred to this step (1.7a's README and HANDOFF "Deviations from plan" say so) — create it. Existing helpers to reuse: `queries/memberships.ts` (`listMemberships(db, orgId)` and the two-query profile merge 2.2b/3.2 use; rows whose profile is not visible render "(profile not visible)"), `queries/organizations.ts` (`listOrganizations(db)`, `getOrganizationBySlug`), `queries/settings.ts` (`getSettings` for `timezone`), `keys.ts` (add `queryKeys.audit.list(orgId, filters)` additively with its uniqueness test). Every helper takes the client first and uses explicit column lists.
- `@church/domain` (1.6a/1.6b): `permissions.ts` (`PERMISSION_KEYS`, `PERMISSION_LABELS`, the three role groups), `schemas/enums.ts`, `errors.ts` (`permission_denied`, `not_found`, `invalid_payload`), `dates.ts`.
- Web (2.1–3.8, 5.x, 6.1b): `src/lib/auth/require-org.ts` (`requireOrgMember(slug)` → `OrgContext`; read the file for the org-id field name), `src/lib/auth/require-perm.ts` (`hasPerm`, `hasAnyPerm`, `requirePerm`), `src/lib/auth/require-super.ts` (`requireSuperAdmin()`), `src/lib/dates.ts` (`formatInstantInZone(iso, tz)`, `zonedLocalToInstant(datetimeLocal, tz)`, `instantToZonedLocal`, `todayInZone` — the ONLY date helpers; do not add another module), `src/features/org/nav.ts` (`NAV_ITEMS` with `requires` any-of), the `AdminShell` sidebar (2.2a) and its breadcrumb pattern, `src/features/orgs/StatusBadge.tsx`, the list-page house style of `src/features/announcements/AnnouncementsTable.tsx` (3.5a) and its `?show=` search-param filter, `src/lib/actions/result.ts` (`ActionResult`), `apps/web/e2e/smoke.spec.ts` and the env-gated full E2E from 3.7 (`pnpm --filter web test:e2e:full`), `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md` (3.8). 6.1b shipped a CSV export for survey results — find its writer with `git grep -n "text/csv" apps/web` and reuse it; if 6.1b inlined the CSV code, extract it to `src/lib/csv.ts` (`toCsv(rows: string[][]): string`, RFC 4180 quoting, cells starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` prefixed with `'` against spreadsheet formula injection) and re-point 6.1b's route at it.
- Routes that audit rows can link to (link only when the route exists in the repo at build time — check with `ls apps/web/app`): `/o/[orgSlug]/users/[membershipId]` (3.2), `/o/[orgSlug]/invitations` (3.2), `/o/[orgSlug]/sermons/[id]` (3.3a; share links live on it), `/o/[orgSlug]/settings` (3.1), the 5.1 directory household route (read HANDOFF for its exact shape — DESIGN §9 says `/directory/*`), `/admin/churches/[orgId]` (2.2a), `/admin/super-admins` (2.2b).
- Founder decisions that apply: decision 4 — "Permission mapping (docs/DESIGN.md §5 table) ships as the default": audit log viewing is `org.settings`; nothing else unlocks `/o/<slug>/audit`. Decision 1 and 2 — household privacy changes are audited (`hide_from_fellowship`, `hide_from_congregation`, `show_children_in_fellowship`, `privacy_confirmed_at`) and must be readable in the diff. Decision 7 — reading the audit log is not a write; the page works for `past_due` and `suspended` churches alike (no `requireWritable`).

## Build
1. **`@church/db` `packages/db/src/queries/audit.ts`** (user client; explicit columns `id, org_id, actor_user_id, table_name, row_id, action, old_data, new_data, created_at`): `listAuditLog(db, filters: AuditFilters): Promise<{ rows: AuditRow[]; nextCursor: string | null }>` where `AuditFilters = { orgId?: string | null; table?: string; actorUserId?: string | 'system'; action?: string; rowId?: string; from?: string; to?: string; cursor?: string; limit?: number }` — `orgId` undefined = no org filter (super admin page), `null` = platform rows (`org_id is null`); `'system'` → `actor_user_id is null`; `from`/`to` are ISO instants on `created_at`; order `created_at desc, id desc`; keyset cursor = base64url of `{ created_at, id }` decoded with a Zod schema (an invalid cursor → `invalid_payload`), applied as `(created_at, id) < (cursor.created_at, cursor.id)` using `.or()` with the two-clause expansion (`created_at.lt.X,and(created_at.eq.X,id.lt.Y)`); `limit` default 50, max 200; fetch `limit + 1` rows to compute `nextCursor`. `listAuditActors(db, orgId)` → distinct `actor_user_id` values for the org in the last 90 days merged with display names from the profiles two-query helper (`{ userId, displayName | null }`; null name → "(profile not visible)"). `countAuditSince(db, orgId, sinceIso)` (`{ count: 'exact', head: true }`) for a dashboard tile. Export `AUDITED_TABLES` — the ten table names above with labels ("Church", "Church settings", "Memberships", "Permissions", "Household privacy", "Person status & links", "Share links", "Sermon deletions", "Invitations", "Super admins") and `AUDIT_ACTIONS = ['INSERT','UPDATE','DELETE','invitation_permissions_dropped','org_without_manager']` with labels ("Created", "Changed", "Deleted", "Invitation permissions dropped", "Church left without a manager") — but derive both lists from the real triggers and `insert into public.audit_log` / synthetic-action sites in `9999_init.sql` (`grep -n audit_log supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql`) rather than trusting this paragraph: orchestrator decision 15 added account archive/restore/deletion-request RPCs (`deactivate_account`, `srv_archive_account`, `srv_restore_account`, the cancel path) that act on `profiles` / `account_deletion_requests`; if the G2/G3 fixers audit them, add that table and its actions with the labels "Account archived", "Account restored", "Deletion requested", "Deletion cancelled" and a `Platform`-scoped row link to the `/admin` users list (6.3a); if they did not audit archive/restore, record it under HANDOFF "Open questions" as a gap for the next migration. Vitest in `packages/db` with the mocked client: cursor encode/decode round trip, invalid cursor → `invalid_payload`, `limit + 1` fetch and `nextCursor` derivation, `orgId: null` → `is('org_id', null)`, `'system'` actor → `is('actor_user_id', null)`.
2. **Filter parsing** `apps/web/src/features/audit/filters.ts`: `parseAuditFilters(searchParams, { tz, allowOrg }): AuditFilters` — reads `table` (must be in `AUDITED_TABLES`), `actor` (uuid or `system`), `action` (in `AUDIT_ACTIONS`), `row` (uuid), `from`/`to` (`YYYY-MM-DD` in the org timezone → instants via `zonedLocalToInstant`, `to` = end of that day), `cursor`, and `org` (uuid or `platform`, only when `allowOrg`); unknown values are dropped, never thrown. `auditFiltersToSearchParams(filters)` for the reverse. Default date range: none on the org page; **last 7 days on `/admin/audit`** (there is no cross-org index — the default range bounds the scan; say so in a code comment and in `docs/RLS.md`). Table tests for every parameter, the timezone boundary (`from=2026-09-07` in `America/New_York` → `2026-09-07T04:00:00Z`) and the drop-not-throw rule.
3. **Diff rendering** `src/features/audit/diff.ts`: `diffAuditRow(row): AuditChange[]` where `AuditChange = { key, label, before: string | null, after: string | null }` — for `UPDATE` only keys whose JSON differs between `old_data` and `new_data`; for `INSERT` every key of `new_data`; for `DELETE` every key of `old_data`; for the two synthetic actions whatever the RPC stored. Format values with `formatAuditValue(key, value, tz)`: booleans → "Yes"/"No"; ISO timestamps (keys ending `_at`) → `formatInstantInZone`; `permission` / `permissions` arrays → `PERMISSION_LABELS`; uuids → shortened (`8 chars…`) with the full value in a `title`; nulls → "—"; objects → compact JSON. Column labels from a per-table map (`hide_from_fellowship` → "Hidden from fellowship", `congregation_status` → "Congregation status", `user_id` → "Linked account", `requires_password` → "Password required", …; unknown keys fall back to the column name). **Deny-list, defence in depth**: `NEVER_RENDER_KEYS = ['notes', 'birthdate', 'anniversary', 'password_hash', 'token_hash', 'token']` are dropped from every diff and from the Raw view even if a future trigger stores them (1.3a never does; 07's test asserts it). Special rendering: `org_membership_permissions` INSERT → "Granted <permission label>", DELETE → "Revoked <permission label>"; `invitations` → email + permission labels; `sermons` DELETE → title and media kind. Vitest: UPDATE keeps only changed keys, INSERT/DELETE sides, every deny-listed key is absent from the output of a row that contains them all, permission labels resolve, timestamps render in the given zone.
4. **Row links** `src/features/audit/links.ts`: `auditRowHref(row, { orgSlug, isSuperPage }): string | null` mapping `table_name` + ids to the routes listed under Inputs (`org_membership_permissions` uses `membership_id` from `new_data`/`old_data`; `sermon_share_links` uses `sermon_id`; `households`/`persons` link to the 5.1 directory route when present; `super_admins` → `/admin/super-admins`; `organizations`/`organization_settings` → `/o/<slug>/settings` on the org page, `/admin/churches/<orgId>` on the admin page); deleted rows return null. Unit-test the map; the test reads `apps/web/app` with `fs` to assert that every returned path prefix exists as a route directory (skip a mapping gracefully when 5.1's directory route is absent — say which in the test name).
5. **Components** `src/features/audit/`: `AuditFilters.tsx` (client; shadcn `Select` for table/action/actor/church, two date inputs, a row-id input, Apply → `router.replace` with the new search params, Clear; the actor list comes from `listAuditActors` plus "System"; the church select on the admin page from `listOrganizations` plus "Platform"); `AuditTable.tsx` (server-rendered rows: When (`formatInstantInZone` in the org tz — on the admin page use each row's church timezone from the organizations list, falling back to `DEFAULT_TIMEZONE`), Actor (display name → link to `/o/<slug>/users/<membershipId>` when the actor is a current member; "System" for null; "(profile not visible)" when unknown), Table label, Action label as a badge, Row (short id + link from `auditRowHref`), Summary (first change as "label: before → after", "+N more"); every row expands (`Collapsible`) into `AuditEntryDetail.tsx`: the full change list as a two-column before/after table, and a "Raw" toggle showing the deny-list-filtered `old_data`/`new_data` JSON); `LoadMore.tsx` (a link to the same URL with `cursor=nextCursor`; plain `<a>` so it works without JS); `AuditEmpty` states ("No audit entries match these filters" / "Nothing has been audited yet — permission, membership, privacy and sharing changes appear here").
6. **Pages**: `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/audit/page.tsx` — server component, `await params` and `await searchParams`, `requireOrgMember` → `requirePerm(ctx, 'org.settings')` (no `requireWritable`), `getSettings` for `timezone`, `parseAuditFilters(searchParams, { tz, allowOrg: false })` forced to `orgId = ctx org id`, `listAuditLog`, `listAuditActors`, render filters + table + load-more + "Download CSV" button (href `/o/<slug>/audit/export?<same params>`); heading text: "Every permission, membership, privacy, sharing and settings change in <church name>. Entries are written by the database and cannot be edited or deleted." `app/(super)/admin/audit/page.tsx` — `requireSuperAdmin()`, `parseAuditFilters(searchParams, { tz: DEFAULT_TIMEZONE, allowOrg: true })` with the 7-day default when no `from`/`to`, `listOrganizations` for the church select and per-row church name/timezone, actor names via the profile merge (super admins read every profile), rows with `org_id null` show "Platform"; same components; CSV button → `/admin/audit/export`. Add "Audit log" to `NAV_ITEMS` in `src/features/org/nav.ts` with `requires: ['org.settings']` (after Settings) and to the `AdminShell` sidebar; on `src/features/org/Dashboard.tsx` add a small "Changes in the last 7 days: N" tile (`countAuditSince`) linking to `/audit` for `org.settings` holders — additive, do not restyle the dashboard.
7. **CSV export** route handlers `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/audit/export/route.ts` and `app/(super)/admin/audit/export/route.ts` (`runtime = 'nodejs'`, `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`): same guards as the pages, same `parseAuditFilters`, iterate `listAuditLog` pages (limit 200) up to **10,000 rows** then stop and append a final line `# truncated at 10000 rows — narrow the date range`, columns `created_at_utc, created_at_local, actor, table, action, row_id, changes` (`changes` = `label: before → after` joined by `; ` from `diffAuditRow`, deny-list applied), `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="audit-<slug or all>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv"`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. Guards in the Route Handlers (`requirePerm`/`requireSuperAdmin` are written for pages and render or throw — do not call them here): org route `const ctx = await requireOrgMember(orgSlug); if (!hasPerm(ctx, 'org.settings')) return Response.json({ error: 'permission_denied' }, { status: 403 })` (use the permission helper 2.1b/3.1 exported — read `src/lib/auth/require-perm.ts` for its name); super route `const ctx = await getSuperAdminContext(); if (!ctx) return Response.json({ error: 'forbidden' }, { status: 403 })` (2.1b's null-returning variant). Anonymous callers are already redirected by `proxy.ts` because the routes sit under `(org)`/`(super)`.
8. **Tests and QA**: Vitest for `filters`, `diff`, `links`, the nav visibility change (`org.settings` → Audit log visible; a `users.create`-only leader → hidden), and a page-level test of the org page's guard with the mocked context (no `org.settings` → 403 via `requirePerm`; `suspended` org still renders). Playwright smoke (`apps/web/e2e/smoke.spec.ts`): anonymous `/o/any/audit`, `/o/any/audit/export`, `/admin/audit` → redirect to `/login?next=…`; with the smoke's mock session, if 3.7 provides one, the org page renders the filter form. Env-gated full E2E (`test:e2e:full`, 3.7's scenario file): after the existing "admin toggles permissions" step, open `/o/<slug>/audit?table=org_membership_permissions` → a row "Granted <label>" by the admin's display name appears; as the super admin open `/admin/audit?org=<orgId>&table=org_membership_permissions` → the same row; `/o/<slug>/audit` as the plain member → 403; as the provisioned church admin (not super) open `/admin/audit` → 403 (or the `requireSuperAdmin` redirect 2.1b chose — assert whichever it is) and `GET /admin/audit/export` → 403 JSON with no CSV body. Add a Vitest that every distinct `table_name`/`action` pair written by the SQL test fixtures (`grep -h "audit_log" supabase/tests/rls/*.sql` — 07's part (d) and 6.3a's `13_account_deletion.sql` if present) is contained in `AUDITED_TABLES`/`AUDIT_ACTIONS`, so a new audited action cannot be silently dropped by the filters.
9. **Docs**: `docs/RLS.md` — "Audit log" subsection: the ten audited tables and which columns of `households`/`persons` are captured, the synthetic actions, "never stores leader notes, birthdates or secrets" plus the UI deny-list, who can read (`org.settings` or super), the 7-day default and the missing cross-org index (a future `9996_*` migration may add `audit_log (created_at desc)` if `/admin/audit` becomes slow — do NOT add it now). `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md` — an "Audit log" click-through (toggle a permission → find it; change a household's privacy → find the before/after; download the CSV; plain member → 403). `docs/CHECKLIST_SECURITY.md` — tick "audit rows on permission/privacy changes" with the URL where the founder can see them.

## Constraints
- User client only: no `src/lib/supabase/service.ts` import anywhere under `src/features/audit/`, `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/audit` or `app/(super)/admin/audit` — RLS decides what a viewer sees, the page guard is the first line. No raw `supabase.from(...)` in components, pages or routes; every read goes through `@church/db` (add helpers additively, with tests).

- Keep 3.5a/3.6a/6.1b code intact apart from the CSV extraction (item 8 of Inputs) and the nav/dashboard additions. Do not touch `proxy.ts`, `next.config.ts`, CSP, the mobile app, `apps/web/vercel.json` or the cron. Do not build the notification status page or the scheduled-announcement polish — that is 6.2b.
- Versions: Next 16.3, React 19.2.3 exact, supabase-js 2.112, Zod 4.5, TypeScript ~5.9 (not 7), ESLint 9 (not 10), Tailwind 4, Vitest 4, Playwright 1.62. No new runtime dependency except shadcn components generated into `src/components/ui/*`.
- No model names, no secrets, `<slug>@example.test` addresses only in tests and fixtures.

The Vitest deny-list test proves `diffAuditRow` and the Raw view never emit `notes`, `birthdate`, `anniversary`, `password_hash`, `token_hash` or `token`, and `git grep` finds no `service.ts` import and no raw `from('audit_log')` under the audit feature.
`packages/db/src/queries/audit.ts` exists with `listAuditLog`, `listAuditActors`, `countAuditSince`, `AUDITED_TABLES`, `AUDIT_ACTIONS` and tests; `queryKeys.audit.list` is registered.
