steps.title: Scheduled announcements polish and notification delivery status pages
steps.goal: Scheduled announcements get a first-class Scheduled view with relative publish times, Reschedule and Publish now actions, and moving a publish time also moves the queued push (`notifications.scheduled_for`) through a sanctioned service-client Server Action after the user-client update; leaders with any `announcements.*` permission get `/o/[orgSlug]/notifications` (all four notification kinds, filters, counts, Retry) and a per-notification detail page listing recipient devices, Expo receipt outcomes and errors. Docs explain where to look when a push does not arrive; Vitest, Playwright smoke and the full E2E cover the new pages and the reschedule path.
steps.prompt:
You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is step 6.2b "Scheduled announcements polish and notification delivery status pages" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `docs/PLAN.md` §4 (Notifications tables; trigger functions `on_content_publish` and `cancel_notifications_on_delete`; server RPCs `srv_enqueue_due_notifications`, `srv_claim_notifications`), §7 (Push and Cron rows) and §8, and `docs/DESIGN.md` §1 item 6 ("Scheduled publishing is a `publish_at` column enforced in RLS, not a job"), §4.2 ("Notifications & devices"), §6 (policy rows for `notifications` — select for `announcements.*` managers, writes trigger/service only — and `notification_deliveries` — super only), §8 (Push fan-out and Enqueue rows), §9 and §11 Phase 3 ("scheduled announcements UI") before writing code. Also read the bodies of `srv_claim_notifications`, `srv_enqueue_due_notifications`, `app.on_content_publish` in `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql`, `apps/web/src/lib/push/{dispatch,refs,after-publish}.ts`, `apps/web/src/features/announcements/{push-actions,PushStatusBadge,AnnouncementsTable,actions}.tsx|ts` (3.5a/3.6a) and `apps/web/src/lib/cron/tick.ts` (3.6b). Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one.

## Goal
When you finish, scheduled announcements are a first-class thing on the web: `/o/<slug>/announcements` has a Scheduled view sorted by publish time with "publishes in 2 days (Wed, Sep 9, 09:00)" captions, and `announcements.edit` holders can **Reschedule** or **Publish now** from the row; moving a publish time also moves the queued push (`notifications.scheduled_for`) so an announcement pulled forward is pushed at its new time instead of the old one — the gap 3.5a/3.6a left open. Leaders holding any `announcements.*` permission get a delivery status page at `/o/<slug>/notifications` listing every push the church has queued, sent, failed or cancelled across announcements, bulletins, events and surveys, with kind/status/date filters, delivery counts, Retry, and a detail page per notification that shows which recipients' devices received a ticket, the Expo receipt outcome and the error text — the place to look when "my push did not arrive". Docs tell the founder where to look; Playwright covers the pages.

## Inputs / prior state
- Database (1.2–1.4c, frozen if pasted — check the ledger): `notifications (id, org_id, kind notification_kind, ref_id, audience_group_id, title, body, data, status notification_status, scheduled_for default now(), claimed_at, sent_at, attempts default 0, last_error, created_at, updated_at)` with indexes `(status, scheduled_for)` and `(kind, ref_id)`; statuses `queued, claimed, sent, failed, cancelled`; kinds `announcement, event, survey, bulletin`. `notification_deliveries (id, notification_id fk cascade, user_id fk auth.users, device_id fk push_devices set null, expo_ticket_id, receipt_status, error, created_at, updated_at)`; `push_devices (id, user_id, expo_push_token, platform push_platform, device_name, enabled, last_seen_at, …)`. RLS: `notifications` select for `announcements.*` holders, no write policies for `authenticated` (`revoke insert, update, delete`); `notification_deliveries` select super admin only. `srv_claim_notifications(max_rows)` claims `queued` rows with `scheduled_for <= now()` and `attempts < 5` — a queued row whose `scheduled_for` is in the future is untouched until that instant, which is why a moved `publish_at` needs the outbox row moved too. `app.on_content_publish` inserts one row per publish-worthy announcement (`scheduled_for = publish_at`); `app.cancel_notifications_on_delete` cancels on delete.
- 3.5a: `src/features/announcements/actions.ts` (`createAnnouncementAction`, `updateAnnouncementAction`, `deleteAnnouncementAction`), `announcement-state.ts` (`deriveAnnouncementState` → `scheduled | active | expired`), `AnnouncementsTable.tsx` with `?show=active|scheduled|expired|all` for managers, `AnnouncementForm.tsx` with the notice "Push already queued — a moved publish time is re-checked by the dispatcher before sending" (3.6a wording), `src/lib/dates.ts` (`formatInstantInZone`, `zonedLocalToInstant`, `instantToZonedLocal` — the only date helpers). 3.5b: `/o/[orgSlug]/bulletins` Push column reusing `PushStatusBadge`. 5.3a: `/o/[orgSlug]/events` (+ `/events/pending`); 6.1b: `/o/[orgSlug]/surveys/[surveyId]`.
- 3.6a: `src/lib/push/after-publish.ts` (`afterContentPublish({ orgId })` → `AfterPublishResult`), `src/lib/push/dispatch.ts` (`dispatchQueued`), `src/lib/push/refs.ts` (`loadNotificationRef` → `future` state reschedules a claimed row to the content's publish time), `src/features/announcements/push-actions.ts` (`retryPush(orgSlug, notificationId)` — permission follows the row's kind: `bulletins.upload` for bulletin rows, `announcements.edit` otherwise; `getDeliveryCounts(orgSlug, notificationIds)` — counts by `receipt_status` through the service client, org-checked), `PushStatusBadge.tsx` + `pushStatusLabel(status, row)`, `@church/db` service-only helpers `getNotificationById(svc, id)`, `resetNotificationForRetry(svc, id)`, `countDeliveriesByNotification(svc, ids)`, `listPendingReceipts`, `insertDeliveries`, plus user-client `listNotificationStatus(db, orgId, { kind? })` (1.7a/5.3a) in `queries/announcements.ts`. 3.6b: the service-client whitelist asserted by `git grep` (`src/lib/push/*`, `src/lib/cron/*`, `app/api/cron/tick/route.ts`, `src/features/announcements/push-actions.ts`) and `docs/ENV.md` "Push & maintenance job".
- `@church/domain`: `urls.ts` `notificationTargetPath(kind, refId)` (mobile deep-link paths — do not reuse for web links), `schemas/enums.ts` (`notificationKindSchema`, `notificationStatusSchema`), `errors.ts` (`permission_denied`, `not_found`, `invalid_payload`, `organization_suspended`). Guards: `src/lib/auth/require-org.ts` (`requireOrgMember` → `OrgContext`; read the org-id field name), `require-perm.ts` (`hasPerm`, `hasAnyPerm`, `requirePerm` any-of with an array, `requireWritable`), `src/features/org/nav.ts`, `src/lib/actions/result.ts`, `apps/web/e2e/*` (3.7).
- Founder decisions that apply: decision 7 — "only `suspended` blocks writes; `past_due` = banner only" (`requireWritable` before Reschedule / Publish now / Retry; the status pages are read-only and work for every status); decision 6 — bulletin pushes exist (`push_on_bulletin`), so the status page must show `bulletin` rows; decision 4 — the mapping ships as the default: the status pages are for `announcements.*` holders (mirrors the `notifications` select policy), Retry on bulletin rows stays with `bulletins.upload` (3.6a). Orchestrator decision 7 fixed the 3.5/3.6 ordering; this step only polishes what they built.

## Build
1. **Outbox helpers in `@church/db`** (`packages/db/src/queries/notifications.ts`, additive, tests with the mocked client): user-client `listNotifications(db, orgId, { kind?, status?, from?, to?, cursor?, limit = 50 })` → `{ rows, nextCursor }` ordered `scheduled_for desc, id desc` with the same base64url keyset cursor pattern 6.2a used for the audit log (put the cursor codec in `packages/db/src/cursor.ts` if 6.2a inlined it, and re-point 6.2a's `audit.ts` at it); `countNotificationsByStatus(db, orgId, sinceIso)` → `Record<notification_status, number>` (one grouped query or five head counts — keep it simple); service-only `rescheduleQueuedNotification(svc, { kind, refId, scheduledFor })` → number of rows updated (`update … set scheduled_for, updated_at = now() where kind = … and ref_id = … and status = 'queued'`; `claimed`/`sent`/`failed`/`cancelled` rows are never moved); service-only `listDeliveriesForNotification(svc, notificationId)` → rows `id, user_id, device_id, expo_ticket_id, receipt_status, error, created_at` embedded with `push_devices(platform, device_name, enabled)` through the real `device_id` FK (embedding is allowed only through FKs that exist in `9999_init.sql` — this one does). Add `queryKeys.notifications.list(orgId, filters)` and `.notifications.detail(id)` to `keys.ts` with the uniqueness test.
2. **Reschedule and Publish now** — `src/features/announcements/schedule-actions.ts` (`'use server'`; the second sanctioned service-client file in `src/features/announcements/` next to `push-actions.ts`): `rescheduleAnnouncementAction(orgSlug, id, publishAtLocal)` and `publishAnnouncementNowAction(orgSlug, id)`. Sequence for both: `requireOrgMember(orgSlug)` → `requirePerm(ctx, 'announcements.edit')` → `requireWritable(ctx)` → `getAnnouncement(db, id)` with the USER client (`not_found` when missing or not visible — the org check is the RLS-scoped read plus an explicit `row.org_id === ctx org id` comparison) → the row must still be scheduled (`deriveAnnouncementState(row) === 'scheduled'`; otherwise `invalid_payload` with the message "This announcement is already published") → new instant: `zonedLocalToInstant(publishAtLocal, tz)` validated as **at least one minute in the future** (`invalid_payload` "Pick a time in the future") for Reschedule, `now()` for Publish now → `updateAnnouncement(db, id, { publish_at })` — plus whatever actor column 3.5a's `updateAnnouncementAction` already sets, if any; `announcements` has no documented `updated_by` column (PLAN §4) — with the USER client (0 rows → "You no longer have permission to edit announcements") → ONLY THEN, with `createServiceSupabase()`, `rescheduleQueuedNotification(svc, { kind: 'announcement', refId: id, scheduledFor })` (0 rows moved is fine: push was off or the row already left `queued`) → for Publish now additionally `afterContentPublish({ orgId })` so the push goes out in the same request → `revalidatePath('/o/<slug>/announcements')`, `revalidatePath('/o/<slug>/notifications')` → `ActionResult` carrying `{ publishAt, pushMoved: boolean, dispatched }` for the toast ("Rescheduled — push moves with it" / "Rescheduled" / "Published — push sent to N devices" / "Published — push queued"). Then make the edit form consistent: in 3.5a's `updateAnnouncementAction`, after a successful update whose `publish_at` changed and whose new state is `scheduled`, call the same `rescheduleQueuedNotification` (factor a tiny `moveQueuedPush(svc, id, publishAt)` helper inside `schedule-actions.ts` and import it — do not duplicate the service call), and change the form notice to "Push notifications move with the publish time" (delete the 3.6a "re-checked by the dispatcher" sentence — `pushStatusLabel` keeps handling the `future` case for rows the cron rescheduled).
3. **Scheduled view polish** — `src/features/announcements/ScheduledAnnouncements.tsx` (server-rendered table used when `?show=scheduled`, and as a "Coming up" strip of at most 3 rows above the default `all` view when any scheduled rows exist): columns Publishes (`formatInstantInZone` + relative caption "in 2 days" computed server-side from `now` in the org zone — no client clock drift), Title, Audience, Push (`PushStatusBadge`: `queued` with a future `scheduled_for` now reads "Scheduled — sends at <time>" — extend `pushStatusLabel` additively), Actions: **Reschedule** (a `Popover` with a `datetime-local` input, minimum = next minute in the org tz, caption "Times are in <timezone>", Save → `rescheduleAnnouncementAction`), **Publish now** (`AlertDialog`: "Publish '<title>' now? Its push notification, if on, is sent immediately." → `publishAnnouncementNowAction`), Edit, Delete (existing). Sort ascending by `publish_at` (the soonest first) — the `all` view keeps 3.5a's `pinned desc, publish_at desc`. Empty state: "Nothing scheduled — pick 'Schedule for' when creating an announcement". `src/features/org/Dashboard.tsx`: turn the announcements tile into two lines "Active: N · Scheduled: M (next <date>)" for managers — additive; read counts through existing `@church/db` helpers (add a `countAnnouncementsByState` head-count helper additively if none fits).
4. **Delivery status list** `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/notifications/page.tsx` (server; `await params`/`searchParams`): `requireOrgMember` → `requirePerm(ctx, ['announcements.create', 'announcements.edit', 'announcements.delete'])` (any-of; mirrors the select policy — a `bulletins.upload`-only leader keeps seeing bulletin push status on `/bulletins`, 3.5b) → `getSettings` (timezone) → `parseNotificationFilters(searchParams, tz)` in `src/features/notifications/filters.ts` (`kind` ∈ the four kinds, `status` ∈ the five statuses, `from`/`to` dates in the org tz on `scheduled_for`, `cursor`; unknown values dropped) → `listNotifications` → `getDeliveryCounts(orgSlug, ids)` (3.6a, one call for the page) → `listAudienceGroups` for names. Render `src/features/notifications/NotificationsTable.tsx`: summary tiles for the last 7 days from `countNotificationsByStatus` ("Queued", "Sent", "Failed" — Failed links to `?status=failed`), filter bar (`NotificationFilters.tsx`, client, `router.replace`), rows: Kind badge, Title (link to the content when the route exists in the repo — `announcement` → `/o/<slug>/announcements/<ref_id>/edit`, `bulletin` → `/o/<slug>/bulletins`, `event` → `/o/<slug>/events`, `survey` → `/o/<slug>/surveys/<ref_id>`; check `ls apps/web/app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]` at build time and omit links whose route is absent — keep this map in `src/features/notifications/links.ts` with a unit test like 6.2a's), Audience (group name; "Everyone" for null), Scheduled for (`formatInstantInZone`), Status (`PushStatusBadge` with the counts; the failed label shows `last_error`), Attempts (`attempts`/5), Sent (`sent_at`), Actions: Retry (3.6a's `retryPush`, shown when `status = 'failed'` and the caller may retry that kind: `hasPerm(ctx, 'announcements.edit')` for non-bulletin rows, `hasPerm(ctx, 'bulletins.upload')` for bulletin rows), Details → `/o/<slug>/notifications/<id>`. Load more via cursor link. Empty state: "No push notifications yet — publishing an announcement, bulletin, approved event or opened survey queues one".
5. **Delivery detail** `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/notifications/[notificationId]/page.tsx`: same guard; the notification row through the USER client (`getNotificationForOrg(db, orgId, id)` — additive user-client helper selecting by `id` and `org_id`; `notFound()` when absent — RLS plus the explicit org filter); then `listDeliveriesAction(orgSlug, notificationId)` from `src/features/notifications/notification-actions.ts` (`'use server'`; the ONLY service-client file under `src/features/notifications/`): `requireOrgMember` → `requirePerm(any announcements.*)` → `getNotificationById(svc, id)` (3.6a) → refuse with `not_found` unless `row.org_id` equals the ctx org → `listDeliveriesForNotification(svc, id)` → resolve recipient display names from `profiles` by `user_id` through a new service-only helper `listProfileNames(svc: ServiceDbClient, userIds: string[])` (explicit columns `user_id, display_name`; add it to `packages/db/src/queries/profiles.ts` or the file the 2.2b/3.2 merge helper lives in, with a mocked-client test — the existing helper takes the user-scoped `DbClient` and the service client is branded `ServiceDbClient`, so reuse would not typecheck and casting is forbidden; names only, never emails) → return `{ targeted: distinct user count, devices: row count, ok, error, pending (receipt_status null), rows: [{ displayName, platform, deviceName, enabled, ticket: boolean, receiptStatus, error }] }`. Render `src/features/notifications/DeliveryDetail.tsx`: header (kind, title, body excerpt, audience, scheduled/sent times, status, attempts, `last_error`), the summary numbers with one-line explanations ("Pending — Expo has not reported a receipt yet; receipts are fetched by the maintenance job about 15 minutes after sending", "Error — see the row; `DeviceNotRegistered` means the app was uninstalled and the device was disabled"), and the per-device table. Zero deliveries for a `sent` row → "Sent — but nobody in the audience had a registered device". Retry button as in item 4. Explain in a muted footer that a notification lists devices, not people who read it — there is no read receipt.
6. **Navigation and cross-links**: `src/features/org/nav.ts` — add `{ href: 'notifications', label: 'Notifications', requires: ['announcements.create', 'announcements.edit', 'announcements.delete'] }` right after Announcements/Bulletins (before 6.2a's Audit log). `PushStatusBadge` gains an optional `detailHref` prop; 3.5a's announcements table, 3.5b's bulletins table, 5.3a's events list and 6.1b's survey page pass `/o/<slug>/notifications/<notificationId>` when they have the outbox row id (one-line changes; do not restyle those tables).
7. **Tests** (Vitest; mock `@church/db`, the guards, `createServiceSupabase` and `afterContentPublish`; never the network): `schedule-actions.test.ts` — without `announcements.edit` → `permission_denied` and the service client is never created; row of another org / missing → `not_found`; `active` row → `invalid_payload` "already published"; past instant → `invalid_payload`; suspended → `organization_suspended`; happy Reschedule → `updateAnnouncement` (user client) is called BEFORE `rescheduleQueuedNotification` (assert call order) with the same instant; happy Publish now → `afterContentPublish` called once and `pushMoved` reflects the helper's count; `updateAnnouncementAction` with an unchanged `publish_at` never touches the service client. `notification-actions.test.ts` — deliveries for another org's notification → `not_found` and `listDeliveriesForNotification` never called; without any `announcements.*` → `permission_denied`; the returned rows carry no email or token fields (assert the key set). `filters.test.ts`, `links.test.ts`, `pushStatusLabel` new "Scheduled — sends at" case, nav visibility (`announcements.delete`-only → Notifications visible; `bulletins.upload`-only → hidden), `packages/db` tests for every additive helper (including "rescheduleQueuedNotification only targets `status = 'queued'`" by asserting the `.eq('status','queued')` filter on the mocked builder). Playwright smoke: anonymous `/o/any/notifications` and `/o/any/notifications/<uuid>` → redirect to `/login?next=…`. Env-gated full E2E (3.7's file): after the scenario publishes its announcement, `/o/<slug>/notifications` lists it with kind "Announcement" and a Sent/Queued status, and its detail page opens; schedule an announcement 1 day ahead, Reschedule it to 2 minutes ahead → the detail page shows the new "Scheduled for" instant (proves `scheduled_for` moved).
8. **Docs**: `docs/ENV.md` "Push & maintenance job" — add "Where to look when a push did not arrive" (the `/o/<slug>/notifications` list → detail page; the meaning of Queued / Sending / Sent to N devices / Failed / Cancelled; receipts arrive ~15 minutes later; `DeviceNotRegistered` disables the device; Retry rules ≤ 5 attempts). `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md` — "Scheduled announcements" (schedule → Coming up strip → Reschedule → Publish now) and "Notification status" click-throughs. `docs/RLS.md` "Web guards" — one paragraph: the two files that may use the service client for the outbox and why (`notifications` has no write policies; `notification_deliveries` is super-only) and that both re-check the org id before returning anything.

## Constraints
- The service client (`createServiceSupabase()`) appears ONLY in `src/lib/push/*`, `src/lib/cron/*`, `app/api/cron/tick/route.ts`, `src/features/announcements/push-actions.ts` (3.6a), `src/features/announcements/schedule-actions.ts` and `src/features/notifications/notification-actions.ts` (this step) — extend 3.6b's `git grep` whitelist in `docs/RLS.md` accordingly. Every service read/write is preceded by the user-client permission check and followed by an explicit `org_id` comparison; `srv*`/service helpers require the `ServiceDbClient` brand — never cast.
- The user-client update of `announcements.publish_at` happens BEFORE the service-side outbox move, never the other way round (if the user update fails, nothing moves). Never move `claimed`/`sent`/`failed`/`cancelled` rows; never set `scheduled_for` in the past through Reschedule (Publish now uses `now()`).
- No migrations (`9999_init.sql` may be frozen); no changes to `srv_claim_notifications`, the dispatcher's claiming logic, `refs.ts`, the cron phases, `proxy.ts`, `next.config.ts`, CSP, `apps/web/vercel.json`, or the mobile app. No raw `supabase.from(...)` in components, pages or actions — helpers go in `@church/db` additively with tests. No `persons`/`households` reads — recipient names come from `profiles` only.
- Do not build the audit pages (6.2a), account deletion (6.3) or anything mobile. Keep 3.5a/3.5b/5.3a/6.1b tables intact except the one-line `detailHref` pass-through and the notice text.
- Versions: Next 16.3, React 19.2.3 exact, supabase-js 2.112, Zod 4.5, TypeScript ~5.9 (not 7), ESLint 9 (not 10), Tailwind 4, Vitest 4, Playwright 1.62. No new runtime dependency except shadcn components generated into `src/components/ui/*` (`popover`, `alert-dialog` if absent).
- No model names, no secrets; `<slug>@example.test` addresses only in tests.

## Verify
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → green, including `schedule-actions`, `notification-actions`, `filters`, `links`, `PushStatusBadge`, nav and the `packages/db` additive suites.
- Mock env (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://localhost:54321 NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=sb_publishable_ci_placeholder NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost:3000` exported): `pnpm --filter web build` → succeeds; the route list shows `/o/[orgSlug]/notifications` and `/o/[orgSlug]/notifications/[notificationId]`.

- `pnpm --filter web test:e2e:smoke` → green with the two new redirect assertions; with `E2E_*` set, `pnpm --filter web test:e2e:full` → the notification list/detail and reschedule assertions pass (otherwise leave the founder a note in `session_log.md`).

steps.title: Account deactivation and deletion (web): DB proof for both schema cases, `/account/*`, sign-in restore, super-admin restore in `/admin`, privacy and terms text
steps.goal: Orchestrator decision 15 is real on the web: any signed-in person can **Deactivate** their account at `/account` (archives it — reversible — and signs them out) or **Delete** it at `/account/delete` (the public deletion URL Google Play requires; archives immediately and schedules the real deletion 30 days out, `ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS = 30`), an archived person who signs in again is offered "Restore my account" or, during a pending deletion, "Keep my account", and the super admin restores archived accounts, cancels or starts deletion requests from `/admin/users`. The archival schema (`profiles.archived_at/archived_by/archive_reason`, `account_deletion_requests.scheduled_for`, `deactivate_account()`, `restore_my_account()`, `srv_archive_account`, `srv_restore_account`, the gated `srv_process_account_deletions()`) either already sits in the unpasted `9999_init.sql` (case A) or is shipped by this step as the next free `999x_*` migration (case B); a new SQL test `13_account_deletion.sql`, a cron unit test and a cron concurrency test prove archived users are non-members, that nothing is deleted before `scheduled_for`, and that restore brings memberships, permissions and directory visibility back. `/privacy` renders `docs/legal/privacy-policy.md` verbatim (decision 19, draft banner on) and `/terms` carries an agent-drafted terms of service; `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md` gains the deactivate/restore and cancel-deletion scripts. Mobile screens and the Play Data Safety worksheet follow in 6.3c.

This is step 6.3a "Account deactivation and deletion (web): DB proof for both schema cases, `/account/*`, sign-in restore, super-admin restore in `/admin`, privacy and terms text" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `docs/PLAN.md` §4 (`profiles`, `account_deletion_requests`, `request_account_deletion`, `srv_process_account_deletions`), §7 (Cron), §8 (`/privacy`, `/terms`, `(super)` `/admin/*`), §11 (Phase 3 line), `docs/DESIGN.md` §4.2, §4.4 (deletion RPCs), §5 ("Account deletion"), §6 (policy rows for `profiles` and `account_deletion_requests`), §8 (Single cron — "Idempotent under concurrency"), §11 Phase 3 and §13 risk 9, plus orchestrator decisions 15 and 19 in `Session log/003_2026-09-04/todo-drafts/orchestrator-decisions.md` and the placeholder policy `docs/legal/privacy-policy.md` before writing code. Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one (6.3c builds the mobile screens and the Play Data Safety worksheet).

## Goal
When you finish, decision 15 (founder, 2026-09-07) is implemented on the web: the self-service action is **Deactivate account** (archive, reversible, signs the user out, push devices deleted), while **Delete account** stays at `/account/delete` because Google Play requires a web deletion path — it archives the account immediately and schedules the real deletion `ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS` (30) days later unless the user (sign in → "Keep my account") or a super admin cancels. An archived user who signs in lands on `/account/restore` and can bring the account back with one click (recommended default the founder may veto), and the super admin has an Archived / Pending deletion list in `/admin/users` with Restore, Cancel deletion and Start deletion request. The DB side is proven for both schema cases by `supabase/tests/rls/13_account_deletion.sql`, the cron's final phase is proven to process only due rows and to be idempotent under concurrent invocation, `/privacy` shows the placeholder policy from `docs/legal/privacy-policy.md` verbatim under a draft banner (decision 19) and `/terms` a plain-English draft, and `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md` tells the founder how to try all of it on the hosted deployment.

## Inputs / prior state
- **Schema — two cases; decide which applies before writing anything.** Read the HANDOFF "Applied migrations" ledger. **Case A — `9999_init.sql` is NOT pasted anywhere:** the archival schema was added to 9999 by steps 1.2–1.4 (the global review's fixers): verify with `grep -n "archived_at\|archive_reason\|deactivate_account\|restore_my_account\|srv_archive_account\|srv_restore_account\|scheduled_for" supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` and read the real bodies; build only the UI, wrappers, tests, cron proof and docs on top, and do not duplicate any object. If the grep finds nothing, 9999 is unpasted but the fixers did not run — then add the objects below to `9999_init.sql` in their sections (tables (3), functions (5)–(6), policies (8), grants (9); still re-runnable per `docs/MIGRATIONS.md`) and record it under HANDOFF "Deviations from plan". **Case B — 9999 IS pasted:** ship the same objects in the next free descending migration named by the ledger (`9996_account_archival.sql` if free; 9998/9997 belong to join codes and surveys), re-runnable (`add column if not exists`, `create or replace function`, `drop policy if exists` + `create policy`), with its own paste to-do and a 'ready to paste' ledger row. The prompt below names the objects with decision 15's default names; in case A use the names the fixers actually chose (read them) and mention any difference in HANDOFF.
- The decision-15 objects (default names; the per-user table DESIGN §4.2 defines is `profiles`): columns `profiles.archived_at timestamptz`, `profiles.archived_by uuid` (null = self), `profiles.archive_reason text check (archive_reason in ('user','deletion_request','admin'))`; `account_deletion_requests (user_id pk, requested_at, scheduled_for timestamptz not null, processed_at)`; client RPC `request_account_deletion()` — `app.require_user()`, archives the caller now (`archived_at = now()`, `archive_reason = 'deletion_request'`), deletes the caller's `push_devices`, upserts the request row with `scheduled_for = requested_at + interval '30 days'`; client RPC `deactivate_account()` — same archive with reason `'user'`, no request row; client RPC `restore_my_account()` — for the caller's own row when `archive_reason in ('user','deletion_request')`: clears the three columns, deletes any unprocessed request row, and returns the restored memberships count; refuses `archive_reason = 'admin'` with `account_archived_by_admin` (42501) so an admin decision cannot be undone by the user; service RPCs `srv_archive_account(user_id, reason)` (reason `'deletion_request'` also upserts the request row with the same `scheduled_for`) and `srv_restore_account(user_id)` (clears the archive and deletes the pending request); `srv_process_account_deletions()` processes only rows with `processed_at is null and scheduled_for <= now()` — for each: `set local app.cascade = 'on'` (so `app.guard_last_org_manager` audits "org has no manager" instead of blocking), nulls `persons.user_id`, deletes memberships, `push_devices`, `notification_preferences`, deletes `auth.users` (cascades `profiles`), stamps `processed_at`, returns the count. Invariant: an archived user behaves like a disabled membership everywhere (non-member for the `app.*` helpers, no org reads, no push, absent from `srv_audience_user_ids`, hidden from `directory_persons`); `persons` rows stay. Policies: own-row select on both tables, writes only through the RPCs, `service_role` may update/delete. Grants: client RPCs to `authenticated`, `srv_*` to `service_role` only (`09_grants.sql` proves it).
- Cron (3.6b): `apps/web/app/api/cron/tick/route.ts` (Bearer `CRON_SECRET`, `runTick(...)`, JSON `{ ok, startedAt, durationMs, phases }`) and `apps/web/src/lib/cron/tick.ts` (`runTick(svc, { transport, now, deadlineMs })`, each phase wrapped in `phase(name, fn)` → `{ ok, ms, result | error }`, last phase calls `srv_process_account_deletions()`); its tests in `apps/web/src/lib/cron/*.test.ts`; 3.6a's `srv_claim_notifications` (`for update skip locked`).
- Web (2.1a/2.1b/2.2): guards `src/lib/auth/{context,require-user,require-super,require-org,require-perm,landing,paths}.ts` (`getAuthContext()`, `requireUser(nextPath?)`, `requireSuperAdmin()`, `landingFor(ctx)`), `src/lib/actions/result.ts`, `src/lib/supabase/errors.ts` (`toActionError`), `src/lib/supabase/{server,client,service}.ts` (`createServiceSupabase()` returns the branded `ServiceDbClient`), the `signOut` Server Action in `src/features/auth/*`, `apps/web/proxy.ts` (read the name of its protected-prefix list), the `(super)` shell and `/admin` navigation (2.2a/2.2b), the `(public)` privacy/terms placeholder pages (2.1a), 3.7a's Playwright smoke (`PROTECTED_PATHS`, `PUBLIC_PATHS`, `expectStrictHeaders`), 3.8's `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md` and `docs/CHECKLIST_SECURITY.md` (row "account deletion works"), `docs/RLS.md`'s service-client whitelist.
- Packages: `packages/db/src/rpc.ts` (1.7a wraps every public RPC — add the new ones additively), `packages/db/src/keys.ts`, `packages/domain/src/{errors,limits}.ts`, `docs/legal/privacy-policy.md` (decision 19: eleven `## n.` sections, `**Effective date:**` / `**Who we are:**` header lines, `<…>` placeholders, *For counsel* notes, a draft banner).

## Build
1. **Schema (case B only, or case A without fixer output)** — write the objects listed under Inputs exactly, every function `security definer set search_path = ''`, policy names `ca_account_deletion_requests_*` / `ca_profiles_*`, `revoke all on function … from public` then the grant per role, and extend the "drop all `ca_%` policies" block if the file has one. Make the `app.*` membership helpers (`app.member_org_ids()`-style, `app.is_org_member`, `app.person_in_kind`/`srv_audience_user_ids` — read their real names in 9999) exclude users whose `profiles.archived_at is not null`, and make `directory_persons` hide persons whose linked user is archived, if the fixers did not already. Case A with fixer output: nothing to write — verify by reading.
2. **DB proof** — `supabase/tests/rls/13_account_deletion.sql` (same harness as `01…10`: `begin … rollback`, `app_test.login(uid)`, `assert_count`, `assert_raises`, `assert_denied`). Fixture: org A with `mgr` (the only `users.edit_permissions` holder, linked person, a `push_devices` and a `notification_preferences` row), `member` (plain active member, linked person, a `push_devices` row) and `spouse` (same household); org B untouched. Assert, in order: (a) as `member`, `select deactivate_account()` → `profiles.archived_at` set, `archive_reason = 'user'`, `archived_by is null`, `push_devices` for `member` = 0, no `account_deletion_requests` row; as `member` (still logged in inside the transaction) `my_context()` shows no active org, a `select` on org A's `announcements` returns 0 rows, `srv_audience_user_ids` for org A's `everyone` group (as owner) excludes `member`, and as `spouse` `directory_persons` no longer lists `member`'s person (the `persons` row still exists); (b) `select restore_my_account()` as `member` → the three columns null, the membership active again with its permissions, `directory_persons` lists the person again; (c) as `member`, `select request_account_deletion()` → archived with `archive_reason = 'deletion_request'`, one request row with `user_id = member`, `processed_at is null`, `scheduled_for` between `requested_at + interval '29 days'` and `+ interval '31 days'`; calling it again leaves one row (upsert — assert what the body does to `scheduled_for` and comment it); `member` selects exactly 1 row and `spouse` selects 0 of it (own-only policy); `member` cannot `update`/`delete` the row directly (0 rows or 42501); `anon` → 42501 on all three client RPCs; as owner `select srv_process_account_deletions()` → **0** (nothing is due) and `auth.users` still has `member`; (d) as `member`, `select restore_my_account()` → request row gone, account restored (the "Keep my account" path); (e) super-admin path as owner: `srv_archive_account(member, 'admin')` → archived with reason `admin` and `archived_by` = the acting id the RPC records; as `member` `restore_my_account()` → `account_archived_by_admin` (42501); `srv_restore_account(member)` → restored; (f) `srv_archive_account(member, 'deletion_request')` → request row with `scheduled_for` 30 days out; as owner `update public.account_deletion_requests set scheduled_for = now() - interval '1 day' where user_id = member` (the test's stand-in for waiting 30 days), then as `mgr` `request_account_deletion()` and the same backdating for `mgr`; `srv_process_account_deletions()` → returns 2; afterwards `auth.users` has neither id, `persons.user_id` is null for both (persons rows remain), `org_memberships`/`org_membership_permissions`/`push_devices`/`notification_preferences` for both are gone, both requests have `processed_at not null`, and `audit_log` holds the "org has no manager" row for org A; a second call returns 0; (g) idempotency under concurrency (DESIGN §8/§11): assert via `pg_get_functiondef` that `srv_process_account_deletions` claims rows with `skip locked` or a single `update … where processed_at is null and scheduled_for <= now() … returning` (assert the form the body uses; if neither, fix it in case B / A-without-fixers, else record a deviation), and the same `skip locked` assertion for `srv_claim_notifications` (3.6a's guarantee). Add the file to `scripts/db/test.sh` only if it enumerates files by name (it should glob).
3. **Cron proof** — in `apps/web/src/lib/cron/tick.test.ts` (or 3.6b's file) assert the final phase calls `srv_process_account_deletions` on the service client once per tick and reports its integer result in `phases[]` (0 when nothing is due). New `apps/web/src/lib/cron/tick.concurrency.test.ts`: run `runTick` twice concurrently (`Promise.all`) against a mocked service client whose `srv_claim_notifications` hands each queued row to exactly one caller and whose `srv_process_account_deletions` returns 1 then 0; assert every notification is dispatched once and the `processed` counts sum to 1. No change to the phase order.
4. **`@church/domain` + `@church/db`** — `packages/domain/src/limits.ts`: `export const ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS = 30` with a JSDoc ("recommended default, founder may change; must equal the interval in `request_account_deletion` / `srv_archive_account`") and a Vitest that reads the migration file that defines the RPC (`9999_init.sql` or the case-B file) with `node:fs` and asserts `interval '30 days'` (built from the constant) appears in it; `errors.ts`: `account_archived_by_admin` (42501) with the message "An administrator deactivated this account; ask your church office to restore it". `packages/db/src/rpc.ts`: `requestAccountDeletion(db)`, `deactivateAccount(db)`, `restoreMyAccount(db)` (add what is missing); `packages/db/src/queries/account.ts`: `getMyAccountState(db)` → `{ archivedAt, archiveReason, deletionScheduledFor }` from the caller's own `profiles` row (explicit columns `archived_at, archive_reason`) and own `account_deletion_requests` row (if the fixers added these fields to `my_context()`, read them from there instead and say so); service-only `listArchivedAccounts(svc: ServiceDbClient, { filter: 'archived' | 'pending_deletion' | 'all' })` joining `profiles` (`user_id, display_name, email, archived_at, archive_reason, archived_by`) with `account_deletion_requests` (`scheduled_for, processed_at`); `keys.ts`: `queryKeys.account.state()`. Mocked-client tests as in 1.7a.
5. **Web `/account`, `/account/deactivate`, `/account/delete`, `/account/restore`** — new route group `apps/web/app/(account)/` with `layout.tsx` (minimal shell, no org nav); `account/page.tsx` ("Your account": signed-in email, the churches from `my_context()` with membership status, links to `/auth/reset`, "Sign out", and a **Deactivate account** and a **Delete account** card, each with its decision-15 sentence and a button to its page); `account/deactivate/page.tsx` and `account/delete/page.tsx` — all call `requireUser('/account/…')`. Add `/account` to `proxy.ts`'s protected prefixes so anonymous requests redirect to `/login?next=%2Faccount%2Fdelete` (Google's reviewers open the URL logged out — the redirect is the documented behaviour). Copy lives in ONE module `src/features/account/deletion-copy.ts` (6.3c mirrors it byte for byte): `ACCOUNT_ACTION_COPY = { deactivate: "Deactivate account — hides you from your church and signs you out; your data is kept so an administrator can restore you later", delete: "Delete account — permanently deletes your account and data after 30 days unless you cancel" }` (decision 15, verbatim) and `DELETION_POLICY_COPY` = the two "Deactivate your account" / "Delete your account" bullet texts copied word for word from section 5 of `docs/legal/privacy-policy.md` (decision 19 keeps that section in sync with decision 15; 6.6's `legal.test.ts` compares these strings with the rendered policy), plus `whatTheChurchKeeps` ("Directory entries your church created about you are the church's records; ask your church's directory administrators to remove or correct them") and `DELETE_CONFIRMATION_WORD = 'DELETE'`. `src/features/account/{DeactivateAccountForm,DeleteAccountForm,RestoreAccountPanel}.tsx` + `actions.ts` (`'use server'`, user client only): `deactivateAccountAction()` → confirm checkbox "I understand I will be signed out and hidden from my church until my account is restored" → `deactivateAccount(db)` → existing `signOut` logic → redirect to `/account/deactivated` (static `(public)` page: "Your account is deactivated. Sign in again and choose Restore my account, or ask your church office."); `requestAccountDeletionAction()` → requires the typed word `DELETE` and the checkbox "I understand my church keeps its directory entry" → `requestAccountDeletion(db)` → sign out → redirect to `/account/deleted` (static `(public)` page: "Your deletion request was received and your account is deactivated. It will be permanently deleted on <date = now + ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS>, unless you sign in before then and choose Keep my account."); `restoreMyAccountAction()` → `restoreMyAccount(db)` → redirect to `landingFor(ctx)`; errors through `toActionError` (`account_archived_by_admin` → admin message + Sign out). `/account/delete` for a user whose deletion is already pending shows "A deletion request is pending since <requested_at>; your account will be deleted on <scheduled_for>" with a **Keep my account** button (same `restoreMyAccountAction`). Never use the service client under `(account)`.
6. **Sign-in detection (web)** — in `getAuthContext()`/`landingFor(ctx)` (2.1b) read `getMyAccountState` once per request (or the `my_context()` fields) and, when `archivedAt` is set, route every authenticated landing (`/login` success, `/auth/callback`, `/`, `/o/*`, `/admin`) to `/account/restore`; `account/restore/page.tsx` shows, by `archiveReason`: `'user'` → "Restore my account"; `'deletion_request'` → "Keep my account" with the scheduled date and the warning that restoring cancels the deletion; `'admin'` → the admin message + Sign out (no restore button). `proxy.ts` changes only by the `/account` prefix (it must not query the DB). Unit-test `landingFor` for the three reasons.

## Goal
When you finish, a member can deactivate or delete their account from the phone with exactly the web's wording, understands the difference (Deactivate — reversible, an administrator can restore; Delete — permanent after 30 days unless cancelled), is signed out with the push device removed, and — if they sign in again while archived — sees the Restore screen and can come back with one tap (or "Keep my account" during a pending deletion). Google's reviewers find the in-app deletion path under More → Delete account and on the no-church screen. `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` answers the Play Console Data safety form from the real schema, including the account-deletion URL `https://<DOMAIN>/account/delete`, and `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` carries the device checklist the founder runs in 4.5-style builds.

Keep the check cheap (one query, no persist) and unit-test the decision as a pure function `routeForAccountState({ archivedAt, archiveReason, hasActiveOrg })` → `'restore' | 'no-church' | 'app'`.
5. **Entry points** — `MoreMenu.tsx`: a "Your account" section under the existing privacy/terms links with two rows — "Deactivate account" (secondary style, subtitle from `ACCOUNT_ACTION_COPY.deactivate` after the dash) and "Delete account" (destructive style, subtitle from `ACCOUNT_ACTION_COPY.delete` after the dash) — replacing 4.3's `TODO(6.x)` comment; `app/(auth)/no-church.tsx`: a small "Delete my account" text link below its explanation; all three `router.push('/account/…')`. 6. **`docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md`** — the Play Console "Data safety" worksheet, filled in from the schema: a table per Play category (Personal info: name, email, phone, address, other — birthdate, marital status, photos; Photos; Messages — none; App activity — survey responses; in-app search history/other content none; App info and performance — crash logs "none until step 6.3b enables error reporting; then diagnostics, optional"; Device or other IDs — Expo push token/device id) with columns Collected? / Shared? / Optional or required / Purpose(s) / Ephemeral? / Encrypted in transit (yes) / Deletion request mechanism (yes — URL). Then the form's direct questions with the answers: "Does your app collect or share any of the required user data types?" yes; "Is all of the user data collected by your app encrypted in transit?" yes; "Do you provide a way for users to request that their data is deleted?" yes — account deletion URL `https://<DOMAIN>/account/delete` (redirects a signed-out visitor to sign-in — expected) and in-app path More → Delete account; the "Account deletion" App content page answer must describe **both** paths and the window in decision 15's words: deactivation (temporary, reversible — Google says this alone does NOT satisfy the requirement, which is why Delete exists) and deletion (account archived immediately, all account data permanently deleted 30 days after the request unless cancelled; directory entries the church created are the church's records — "some data is retained: church directory entries, survey answers without the account attached"); "Data deletion: are there any other data deletion methods?" contact the church office / `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` for directory entries; privacy policy URL `https://<DOMAIN>/privacy`; "Independent security review" no; target audience adults (no child accounts); "Families policy" not enrolled; the app contains no ads and no analytics SDK (4.4). Add "How this was derived" (pointing at the tables, `9999_init.sql` and decision 15) and "Re-check when" (Sentry enabled in 6.3b; a new table with personal data; the grace period changes). Link it from `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` and the README docs index.

README route list: the three mobile account routes.

## Constraints
- User session only — never a service key in the app; deletion is executed only by the web cron. Mobile native modules unchanged (no `expo install` needed); Expo 57 / RN 0.86.3 / React 19.2.3 exact; no new dependencies; versions of native packages only via `npx expo install` if ever needed.
- Strings must match the web module byte for byte (the test in Build 1 enforces it); do not paraphrase decision 15's two sentences. No real email, entity, price or address — placeholders only (`<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`, `<DOMAIN>`). No analytics or tracking SDK (the worksheet says "none").
- Do not restyle More, no-church or sign-in; add rows, links and the archived-user redirect only. No web code changes except the README/docs lines named above. No model identifiers, no secrets.

## Verify

- Device checklist against the hosted project with a 4.5 preview/dev-client build (the local harness has no Auth/PostgREST, so the app cannot sign in locally): run the `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` "Device checklist: account" section from Build 7. If you cannot run it, write it into `session_log.md` for the founder.

- Tick step 6.3c in `docs/TODO.md`; write `session_log.md`; commit `feat(mobile): account deactivate/delete/restore screens and Play Data Safety worksheet`; push `main` (or the branch I named).
- If something in the plan proves impossible or wrong, do the closest correct thing, record it in HANDOFF.md under "Deviations from plan", and report it in your final message.

## Goal

## Build
1. **Web Sentry SDK** — run `npm view @sentry/nextjs version peerDependencies`, check the peer range supports `next@16`, and install that exact version — `pnpm --filter web add @sentry/nextjs@<exact version>` (the standing orders pin every dependency exactly; record the pin under HANDOFF version pins). If the peer range does not include Next 16, stop, record it in HANDOFF, and implement only the DSN-less `captureException` shim below. Env (`src/lib/env.ts` + `apps/web/.env.example` + `docs/ENV.md`): `SENTRY_DSN` (server; optional), `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` (browser; optional — usually the same value), `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` (build-time source-map upload; optional; Vercel server env only), `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT` (default `process.env.VERCEL_ENV ?? 'development'`). Files: `apps/web/sentry.server.config.ts`, `apps/web/sentry.edge.config.ts`, `apps/web/instrumentation-client.ts` (Next 16 convention) and `apps/web/instrumentation.ts` (`register()` imports the server/edge config by `process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME`; `export const onRequestError = Sentry.captureRequestError`). Every init is guarded: `if (!dsn) return;`. Options in all three: `dsn`, `environment`, `release: process.env.VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA`, `sendDefaultPii: false`, `tracesSampleRate: 0.05` server / `0` client, no Replay, no profiling, `beforeSend` from `src/lib/monitoring/scrub.ts` (pure, unit-tested): delete `event.user.email`/`ip_address`/`username`, delete `request.cookies`, drop `authorization`/`cookie`/`x-cron-secret` headers, redact email-shaped strings and `sb_secret_…`/`sb_publishable_…`/`eyJ…` tokens in `message`, `exception.values[].value` and breadcrumb messages with a fixed regex set; keep `user.id` (a uuid) and tags. `next.config.ts`: wrap with `withSentryConfig(config, { org, project, authToken, silent: true, widenClientFileUpload: true, disableLogger: true })` only when `SENTRY_DSN || NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` is set; otherwise export the plain config so the mock-env build is byte-for-byte the same as before. CSP: extend 2.1a's builder so `connect-src` also lists the DSN's origin (parse `new URL(dsn).origin`) when `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` is set — unit test both branches; do not add `unsafe-*`, do not use the tunnel route (it would widen the matcher in `proxy.ts`).
2. **Web capture points** — `src/lib/monitoring/index.ts`: `isMonitoringEnabled()`, `captureException(err, { tags?, extra? })` (no-op without DSN; never throws), `withMonitoring(name, fn)` wrapper. Use it in exactly these places, additively: `runTick`'s `phase()` — on failure `captureException(error, { tags: { area: 'cron', phase: name } })`; `dispatchQueued`/`processReceipts` — per-notification failures that are not `DeviceNotRegistered` (tag `area: 'push'`); `app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts` — the 500 path (tag `area: 'stripe'`, extra `eventType`, never the payload); `toActionError` — only when the error is NOT a mapped domain error (SQLSTATE known to `errors.ts`) and not a Next redirect/notFound (`isRedirectError`), tag `area: 'action'`; `app/global-error.tsx` and `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/error.tsx`-style boundaries → `Sentry.captureException` in a `useEffect` (create `app/global-error.tsx` if 2.1a did not). Set `Sentry.setUser({ id })` in `getAuthContext()` when enabled — id only.
3. **Mobile Sentry SDK** — from `apps/mobile`: `npx expo install @sentry/react-native` (version from `expo install` only). `src/lib/monitoring.ts`: `initMonitoring()` — reads `EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` through `publicEnv()` (add it as optional), returns without side effects when empty; otherwise `Sentry.init({ dsn, environment: Updates.channel ?? 'development' (or `__DEV__ ? 'development' : 'production'` if expo-updates is not installed — do not install it), release from `expo-constants` version, sendDefaultPii: false, enableNativeCrashHandling: true, tracesSampleRate: 0, beforeSend: scrub })`; the scrub is a copy of the web regex set in `src/lib/monitoring-scrub.ts` (pure, unit-tested; do not import web code); `captureException(err, ctx)` and `setMonitoringUser(id | null)` helpers. Call `initMonitoring()` at the top of `app/_layout.tsx` before providers, wrap the root layout with `Sentry.wrap` only when enabled (export `Sentry.wrap(Root)` vs `Root` through a tiny `withMonitoring(Component)` so the disabled path has no Sentry reference at runtime), call `setMonitoringUser(session?.user.id ?? null)` from `SessionProvider` on session change, and clear it in `signOutEverywhere()` via the existing `registerBeforeSignOut` hook. `app.config.ts`: add the plugin `['@sentry/react-native/expo', { organization: process.env.SENTRY_ORG, project: process.env.SENTRY_PROJECT }]` ONLY when `SENTRY_ORG && SENTRY_PROJECT && SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` are all present (source maps upload during EAS builds), so `expo-doctor`/`expo export` without them are unchanged; document the three as EAS secrets in `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md`. 4. **`docs/MONITORING.md`** — sections: What is monitored (the capture points above, the tags `area`/`phase`, what is scrubbed, what is never sent — emails, tokens, cookies, request bodies, directory data); Turning it on (founder click-path: sentry.io → Create project → platform Next.js → copy DSN → Vercel → Settings → Environment Variables → `SENTRY_DSN`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` (Production + Preview), `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` (server only) → redeploy; second project platform React Native → `EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` as an EAS environment variable plus the three build secrets → next `eas build`); Alerts (Sentry → Alerts → "issues" rule: new issue in `cron` or `stripe` area → email `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` — placeholder); Where to look when something is wrong (Vercel → Deployments → Functions logs; Vercel → Settings → Cron Jobs → last runs and the JSON phase report; Supabase → Reports and Logs → Postgres/Auth; Supabase Free plan pause after 7 idle days → Restore; Expo → Builds; the org `/o/<slug>/notifications` page (6.2b) for stuck `queued` pushes; `/admin/audit` (6.2a)); Manual health check (`curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET" https://<VERCEL_URL>/api/cron/tick | jq '.ok, [.phases[] | {name, ok, ms}]'` — expected every `ok: true`); Cost/plan notes (Sentry free tier limits; sampling values above). Link it from README's docs index and from `docs/DEPLOY.md`.
5. **Security audit script** — `supabase/tests/security/audit.sql` + `scripts/db/security-audit.sh` (runs it with `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$DATABASE_URL"`; prints one line per check `PASS|FAIL <id> <description> [<offenders>]` using `do $$ … raise notice` blocks or a temp table + final `select`; exits non-zero when any FAIL). Checks (ids stable so the checklist can cite them): `SEC-01` every table in `public` has `relrowsecurity = true` and none has `relforcerowsecurity`; `SEC-02` every policy on `public.*`/`storage.objects` is named `ca_%`; `SEC-03` `anon` has no `execute` on any function in `public` and `app` (`has_function_privilege('anon', oid, 'execute')`) and no table privileges beyond what `09_grants.sql` allows (list the exceptions 1.4b documented, e.g. none); `SEC-07` every row in `storage.buckets` has `public = false` and the `sermon-media` `file_size_limit` ≤ 52428800 while HANDOFF says Free (print the value); `SEC-08` `storage.objects` has no `update`/`delete` policy whose roles include `authenticated`; `SEC-09` column-level: `has_column_privilege('authenticated', 'public.persons', 'birthdate', 'select')` and `has_column_privilege('authenticated', 'public.households', 'anniversary', 'select')` are both false while `select` on `persons.first_name` is true (the grant exists at all) — PLAN §5 / DESIGN §1 item 3 exclude exactly `persons.birthdate` and `households.anniversary`; `persons.user_id` and the household privacy flags are readable base columns (visibility is handled by the `directory_*` views); print any further column `9999_init.sql` section (9) / `docs/RLS.md` revoked but assert only these two — cite the list, do not extend it; `SEC-10` `private` schema: no privileges for `anon`/`authenticated`/`service_role` on `private.*`; `SEC-11` `audit_log` has no insert/update/delete policy for `authenticated`; `SEC-12` `account_deletion_requests` has no `insert`/`update`/`delete` policy whose roles include `authenticated` (requests are created by `request_account_deletion()` and cancelled through the definer RPC decision 15 introduced — read `docs/RLS.md`; if 1.4b chose an own-row cancel policy instead, the check asserts that policy's `using` clause is exactly `user_id = auth.uid()` and nothing wider), `anon` has nothing, `service_role` may update/delete; `SEC-13` archived accounts are non-members (orchestrator decision 15): inside the audit transaction insert a fixture user with `profiles.archived_at` set (or whatever archival column the fixers chose — read `docs/RLS.md`; if the column does not exist, print `SKIP SEC-13` and treat it as PASS), give it an `active` membership, and assert that the `app.*` membership helpers (`app.is_org_member` / `app.my_org_ids`-style — names from `docs/RLS.md`) return false/empty for it, that `srv_audience_user_ids` for the org's `everyone` group excludes it, that `directory_persons` hides its person, and that `select count(*) from public.push_devices where user_id = …` is 0; roll everything back. Wire `scripts/db/security-audit.sh` into `.github/workflows/ci.yml` after `test.sh` (same non-blocking mode 1.1 chose, or blocking if 3.7a made the DB job blocking — match it) and into `docs/MIGRATIONS.md`'s verification sequence.
6. **Checklist run-through** — rewrite `docs/CHECKLIST_SECURITY.md` so each row has: item, why, how to check (command with `SEC-nn` or dashboard click-path), expected, and a new "Run-through <date> (local)" column filled by actually running everything you can now: the audit script rows, `scripts/db/test.sh` (grant matrix), the smoke suite (`noindex`/no-referrer on `/s/*`, CSP + HSTS on `/privacy`, no secret in HTML), `grep -rn "SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY" apps/web/src apps/mobile/src` → only `src/lib/env.ts`/`service.ts` on the web and nothing in mobile, `grep -rn "createServiceSupabase\|service.ts" apps/web/app apps/web/src` → only Route Handlers/Server Actions listed by name (share unlock, cron, webhook, createUserDirect, 6.3a's `(super)` account-archival actions, push dispatch, and 6.2b's reschedule/deliveries actions only if 6.2b has run — `docs/RLS.md`'s service-client whitelist is the authority; check it before calling any hit unexpected) — list every hit and mark any unexpected one as a finding to fix in this step. Rows only a hosted dashboard can prove (secret key only in Vercel server env, custom SMTP configured, Stripe webhook secret set and signature verified with a test event, buckets private on the hosted project, OTP template, Site URL/redirect list, Supabase "Enforce SSL", Vercel deployment protection off for `/api/stripe/webhook` and `/api/cron/tick`) go into a "Founder run-through" section with a click-path each and an empty "date / result" column plus the one-line `helper` command where one exists (e.g. `curl -sI https://<VERCEL_URL>/s/unknown | grep -i x-robots-tag`). Add the two new rows "error reporting scrubs PII (unit test `scrub.test.ts`)" and "error reporting is off without a DSN (build/export unchanged)", a row "archived accounts are non-members (SEC-13)", a row "cron idempotent under concurrency (6.3a's `tick.concurrency.test.ts` and the `skip locked` assertions in `13_account_deletion.sql`)", and rename the inherited DESIGN §12 row "account deletion works" to "account deactivation, restore and 30-day deletion work" citing `supabase/tests/rls/13_account_deletion.sql` (6.3a) and the acceptance curl from `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md`. Record every FAIL you found and fixed in HANDOFF "Deviations from plan" and in the row itself.
7. **Tests** — web: `scrub.test.ts` (emails, `sb_secret_`, JWT-looking strings, cookies/headers removed; uuids and tags kept), `csp.test.ts` extension (with/without DSN), `monitoring.test.ts` (no DSN → `captureException` no-op and `isMonitoringEnabled() === false`; with DSN → `Sentry.captureException` called with tags — mock `@sentry/nextjs`), cron test extension (a throwing phase is reported with `{ area: 'cron', phase }`); mobile: `monitoring-scrub.test.ts`, `monitoring.test.ts` (init skipped without DSN; `withMonitoring` returns the component untouched), `ErrorBoundary.test.tsx` if the mobile Vitest setup renders components (else a pure test of its `getDerivedStateFromError`/reset logic). Playwright smoke: with the mock env (no DSN) the HTML of `/`, `/login`, `/privacy` contains no `sentry` script or `ingest.sentry.io` reference and the CSP `connect-src` has no Sentry origin; add a second smoke config case only if 3.7a's harness supports per-test env — otherwise assert the CSP branch in the unit test only and say so.

## Constraints
- Error reporting is opt-in by env: with no DSN the web build output, the CSP, the mobile export and every test must be identical to before. Never enable Sentry in Playwright or CI mock env. No Session Replay, no profiling, no performance tracing on the client, no `sendDefaultPii`. Never capture domain errors (`errors.ts` keys), redirects, or 4xx auth failures — those are expected behaviour.
- No analytics or tracking SDK (4.4). No `tunnelRoute`. `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` is server/build-only and never `NEXT_PUBLIC_`/`EXPO_PUBLIC_`. No secret, DSN, email or model identifier in code, docs or tests — placeholders (`<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`, `<VERCEL_URL>`, `<DOMAIN>`).

No planned migration; the audit script only reads catalogs. If an audit check FAILS because of a real grant/policy bug: when the HANDOFF ledger shows `9999_init.sql` pasted, fix it in the next free descending migration named in the ledger (re-runnable per `docs/MIGRATIONS.md`); when 9999 is not pasted yet it is not frozen — fix it in `9999_init.sql` itself (still re-runnable) and re-run the standing DB sequence. Record the fix either way — do not silently relax the check.
- Do not restructure `next.config.ts`, `proxy.ts`, `app/_layout.tsx` beyond the guarded additions above.

## Verify

- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → green (new scrub/monitoring/CSP/cron/mobile tests); `pnpm --filter web build` with the mock env (no DSN) → same route list as 6.3a and no Sentry webpack output; `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN=https://examplePublicKey@o0.ingest.sentry.io/0 SENTRY_DSN=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN pnpm --filter web build` → succeeds (source-map upload skipped without `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, no error) and `curl -sI` of `/privacy` on `pnpm --filter web start` shows `connect-src` containing `https://o0.ingest.sentry.io`.
- `pnpm --filter web test:e2e:smoke` → green (no-Sentry assertions).
- `pnpm --filter mobile exec expo-doctor` and `npx expo export --platform android` (no DSN, no `SENTRY_*`) → clean; `grep -n "sentry" apps/mobile/app.config.ts` → the plugin is inside the `if (SENTRY_ORG && SENTRY_PROJECT && SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN)` branch.
- `grep -c "PASS\|FAIL" docs/CHECKLIST_SECURITY.md` → ≥ 12 (the run-through column is filled); `grep -n "SEC-0[1-9]\|SEC-1[0-2]" docs/CHECKLIST_SECURITY.md supabase/tests/security/audit.sql` → every id in both.
- Manual (optional, needs a throwaway Sentry project): set the DSN locally, throw inside a Server Action, confirm the event arrives with `user.id` only and no cookies.

## Finish
- `HANDOFF.md`: State — tick "Monitoring + security checklist run-through (6.3b)"; env var section — add `SENTRY_DSN`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`, `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` (all optional, off by default); founder to-dos — "create two Sentry projects and set the env vars (docs/MONITORING.md)", "do the Founder run-through section of docs/CHECKLIST_SECURITY.md on the hosted project and record the date"; Decisions — "error reporting opt-in by DSN, PII scrubbed, no analytics"; "Deviations from plan" for every audit FAIL fixed, any `@sentry/nextjs` peer-range problem, and any capture point you could not add.
- Tick step 6.3b in `docs/TODO.md`; write `session_log.md`; commit `feat: error monitoring behind env (web + mobile), monitoring runbook, security audit script and checklist run-through`; push `main` (or the branch I named).
- If something in the plan proves impossible or wrong, do the closest correct thing, record it in HANDOFF.md under "Deviations from plan", and report it in your final message.
