steps.goal: Anacast runs on iPhones through TestFlight. The agent makes the Expo project iOS-ready without a Mac (`ios.bundleIdentifier` confirmed, `ios.config.usesNonExemptEncryption: false`, iOS purpose strings for photos/camera, `UIBackgroundModes` audio proven from a prebuild, iOS branches of the bulletin PDF opener and push registration verified by unit tests, Universal Links route `/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` behind `APPLE_TEAM_ID`, `submit.production.ios` in `eas.json`, `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md` derived from `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md`, an iOS section in `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md`, CI exporting the iOS bundle); the founder enrols in the Apple Developer Program, lets `npx eas-cli build -p ios --profile production` register the bundle id and create the distribution certificate, provisioning profile and APNs push key, creates the app in App Store Connect with the privacy-policy URL from 6.6 and the App Privacy answers, submits with `npx eas-cli submit -p ios --profile production --latest`, installs from TestFlight and runs the device checklist (OTP sign-in, push, background audio with lock-screen controls, YouTube WebView, bulletin PDF, Deactivate/Delete rows); the agent's second pass fixes what the iPhone shows and records the TestFlight ledger in HANDOFF.md.
steps.prompt:
You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is step 6.4 "iOS: Apple Developer account, bundle id, APNs key, `eas build -p ios`, TestFlight; agent fixes iOS-only issues" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `docs/PLAN.md` §9 (mobile screen map, `app.config.ts`, `eas.json`) and §11 (Phase 3 line), `docs/DESIGN.md` §7 ("Android PDF … iOS renders natively (Phase 3)"), §10 (Playback, Push, EAS paragraph — "iOS fields present but untested until Phase 3"), §11 Phase 3 acceptance ("TestFlight build"), §13 risks 5, 9 and 10, `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md`, `docs/MEDIA.md`, `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` and `HANDOFF.md` ("Mobile (Phase 1)", "Google Play" if 6.5 ran, "Legal") before writing code. Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one.

## Goal
Two agent passes around the founder's checklist. First pass (Build 1–8): make the project build and behave correctly on iOS without a Mac — configuration, iOS branches that Phase 1 left "untested until Phase 3", the App Store privacy worksheet and docs — so the founder's `npx eas-cli build -p ios --profile production` succeeds on the first try. Second pass (Build 9): triage the TestFlight device results and Apple's emails the founder pastes, fix iOS-only bugs (PDF viewer, background audio and lock-screen controls, push permission flow, safe areas, keyboard) and fill the HANDOFF TestFlight ledger. Nothing in this step changes Android behaviour.

## Inputs / prior state
- 4.1a: `apps/mobile/app.config.ts` — `ios: { bundleIdentifier: 'com.anacast.app', supportsTablet: false }` with the comment "present but untested until Phase 3 (step 6.4)"; `scheme: 'anacast'`; plugins `expo-router`, `expo-notifications` (icon/colour), `expo-secure-store`, `expo-video` (`supportsBackgroundPlayback`), `['expo-audio', { recordAudioAndroid: false, enableBackgroundPlayback: true }]` (the plugin writes `UIBackgroundModes: ['audio']` — no manual `infoPlist` line), `expo-sqlite`, `expo-web-browser`, `expo-build-properties`; `newArchEnabled: true`; `extra.eas.projectId: process.env.EAS_PROJECT_ID`. `eas.json`: `build.production` (`autoIncrement: true`, `environment: 'production'`), and from 6.5 `cli.appVersionSource: 'remote'`, `submit.production.android`, and a `submit.production.ios: {}` placeholder (if 6.5 has not run, add `cli.appVersionSource: 'remote'` yourself and say so).
- 4.2a: `src/features/bulletins/openBulletinFile.ts` (`openBulletinFile`, `pickOpener`) — Android opens PDFs via `expo-intent-launcher`; the iOS branch was left as `expo-sharing` `shareAsync(localUri)` or `WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync(signedUrl)` with the comment "Phase 3 (6.4) verifies". 4.2b: `players/Audio.tsx` (`expo-audio`, `setAudioModeAsync({ shouldPlayInBackground: true, playsInSilentMode: true, interruptionMode: 'doNotMix', shouldRouteThroughEarpiece: false })`, lock-screen controls "pending expo-audio API" if the installed version lacked them), `players/Video.tsx` (`expo-video`), the hosted-YouTube `react-native-webview` player, `players/External.tsx`. 4.3: `src/lib/push-capability.ts` (`pushCapability` → `ok | emulator | expo_go | missing_project_id | unsupported_platform`; `'ios'` must yield `ok` on a device), `registerForPush(deps, …)` with `ensureAndroidChannel()` guarded by `Platform.OS === 'android'`, `push_devices.platform` ∈ `android | ios`, `installPushSignOutCleanup`. 5.2b (if built): `expo-image-picker` / `expo-image-manipulator` for directory photos. 6.3a: `app/account/delete.tsx`, Deactivate/Delete rows on More (decision 15). 6.3b: `@sentry/react-native` behind `EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` (iOS builds need no extra config while the DSN is unset).
- Web: 5.7 (if built) serves `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` for Android App Links; `apps/web/next.config.ts` security headers (2.1a); `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`.
- 6.6: live `https://<DOMAIN>/privacy` and `/terms`, `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` with final URLs; 6.5 (if run): `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` "Google Play" section and the reviewer test-account convention (demo church + password account).

## Build
1. **`app.config.ts` iOS block.** Keep `ios.bundleIdentifier` = `android.package` = `com.anacast.app` (orchestrator decision 18, confirmed lowercase; immutable once App Store Connect has the record). Add `ios.config: { usesNonExemptEncryption: false }` (the app uses only HTTPS/TLS → exempt; this answers App Store Connect's export-compliance question in every build and skips the "Missing Compliance" prompt in TestFlight). Do not write `UIBackgroundModes` into `ios.infoPlist` by hand — the `expo-audio` plugin owns it (Build 5 proves it). Store assets from the brand palette (orchestrator decision 17 — the token file `apps/mobile/src/theme.ts` is the single source: `ink` Prussian Blue `#00072d`, `primaryDark` Deep Navy `#001c55`, `primary` Imperial Blue `#0a2472`, `accent` Bright Marine `#0e6ba8`, `tint` Icy Blue `#a6e1fa`): Apple requires an opaque 1024×1024 PNG without alpha, so generate `assets/icon-ios.png` by flattening `assets/icon.png` (6.5's palette icon if it ran, else the current icon) onto `theme.colors.ink` with a small Node script that uses only dependencies already installed in the workspace (`sharp` if present, else `pngjs`; if neither exists, write an SVG at `assets/icon-ios.svg` from the palette and put the exact export instructions for the founder into `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md`), set `ios.icon` to it, and confirm `splash.backgroundColor` and `android.adaptiveIcon.backgroundColor` read the token values (`ink` and `primary`). List under a new "Assets" section of `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md` the screenshot sets App Store Connect requires (6.7" and 6.5" iPhone, at least 3 each) and which screens to capture (Home, Sermon playing, Announcement, Bulletin, Directory, Survey — whichever exist), all in the app's real theme. Ensure `ios.buildNumber` is absent (remote versioning bumps it). If `expo-image-picker` is installed (5.2b), give its plugin entry purpose strings: `['expo-image-picker', { photosPermission: 'Anacast uses your photo library so you can choose a household or profile photo for your church directory.', cameraPermission: 'Anacast uses the camera so you can take a directory photo.' }]` — Apple rejects generic or missing `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription` / `NSCameraUsageDescription`. `expo-notifications` needs no purpose string on iOS.
2. **`eas.json`.** `build.production.ios` needs nothing beyond the defaults (store distribution, `autoIncrement` with remote versioning); add `build.preview.ios: { simulator: false, distribution: 'internal' }` ONLY as documentation of the ad-hoc alternative in `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` — the founder uses TestFlight, which needs no device UDIDs. Leave `submit.production.ios` as an empty object (no `ascAppId`, no `appleId`) and document that `eas submit -p ios` resolves the app from the bundle id after the founder logs in or uploads an App Store Connect API key through `npx eas-cli credentials -p ios`; never commit `appleId`, `ascAppId` or a key path. Add `AuthKey_*.p8` and `*.p8` to `apps/mobile/.gitignore` and the root `.gitignore`.
3. **iOS push path.** Read 4.3's `registerForPush` and `pushCapability` and add unit tests (`src/lib/push-capability.test.ts` — extend, do not duplicate) proving: `Platform.OS === 'ios'` on a physical device with a project id → `ok`; the Android channel step is skipped on iOS; `getPermissionsAsync` returning `status: 'undetermined'` → `requestPermissionsAsync` is called with `{ ios: { allowAlert: true, allowBadge: false, allowSound: true } }`; `status: 'denied'` → no token call, the explainer shows the "Open Settings" hint (use `Linking.openSettings()`); the `push_devices` row is upserted with `platform: 'ios'` and `device_name` from `expo-device` (`Device.modelName`). iOS shows notifications in the foreground only if the handler says so — confirm 4.3's `setNotificationHandler` returns `shouldShowBanner: true, shouldShowList: true, shouldPlaySound: true` (or the older `shouldShowAlert` if that is what the installed typings expose). The Expo push service needs the APNs key the founder uploads in the checklist (D) — nothing in code.
4. **Bulletin PDF and images on iOS.** In `openBulletinFile.ts` settle the iOS branch: PDFs → `WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync(signedUrl, { presentationStyle: 'pageSheet' })` (SFSafariViewController renders PDFs natively with share/print — this is DESIGN §7's "iOS renders natively"; no `react-native-pdf`), and a secondary "Share" action → download to `FileSystem.cacheDirectory` (already implemented for Android) then `Sharing.shareAsync(localUri, { UTI: 'com.adobe.pdf', mimeType: 'application/pdf' })` so the founder can save to Files. Images keep the inline `expo-image` view on both platforms. Keep 4.2a's pure `pickOpener(mimeType, platform)` and its return set `'intent' | 'inline_image' | 'share' | 'browser'` (do not change the signature or 4.2a's tests); settle the iOS branch so `ios × pdf` → `browser` (the page-sheet Safari view) with `share` as the secondary action, and extend its tests for `ios` × `pdf|jpeg|png` and `android` × the same. Remove the "Phase 3 (6.4) verifies" comment.
5. **Background audio and lock-screen controls — prove the config.** Run `cd apps/mobile && EAS_PROJECT_ID=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 npx expo prebuild --platform ios --no-install --clean` (works on Linux: it only generates the `ios/` folder from templates; it needs network for the template tarball). Assert with `grep -A3 UIBackgroundModes ios/Anacast/Info.plist` that `<string>audio</string>` is present, that `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription` / `NSCameraUsageDescription` exist when `expo-image-picker` is installed, that `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption` is `false`, and that `CFBundleIdentifier` resolves to the bundle id. Then delete `ios/` (and `android/` if generated) — prebuild output is never committed; confirm `.gitignore` lists `/ios` and `/android` under `apps/mobile`. Mirror checklist items 14–20 including 19b–19e (surveys, events, Universal Link, deactivate/restore) in the `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` iOS device list. Put the exact grep commands into `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` "iOS" so the founder or a later agent can repeat the check. In `players/Audio.tsx`: if the installed `expo-audio` exposes lock-screen/Now Playing metadata (check the package's typings for a `setActiveForLockScreen`-style or `updateNowPlaying`/`metadata` API — the name varies by version), set title = sermon title, artist = speaker, so the iOS lock screen and Control Center show the sermon; if there is no such API in the installed version, keep background playback (already enabled) and record "lock-screen metadata pending expo-audio API" under Deviations. Do not add `react-native-track-player` or any other native package for this.
6. **Universal Links (optional, mirrors 5.7's Android App Links).** Add `ios.associatedDomains: ['applinks:<host of EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL>']` computed in `app.config.ts` from `process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL` (skip the field when the variable is unset so `expo config` stays clean in CI), and on the web `apps/web/app/.well-known/apple-app-site-association/route.ts` (Node runtime) that returns `{"applinks":{"details":[{"appIDs":["<APPLE_TEAM_ID>.<bundle id>"],"components":[{"/":"/invite/*"},{"/":"/s/*"}]}]}}` with `Content-Type: application/json`, no redirect, no `.json` extension, reading `APPLE_TEAM_ID` (new server env var; document in `docs/ENV.md` and `.env.example`; return 404 when unset so nothing breaks before the founder has a Team ID). Reuse 5.7's bundle-id source if it exported one; otherwise hard-code the bundle id in ONE constant `IOS_BUNDLE_ID` in `apps/web/src/lib/mobile-app.ts` next to 5.7's Android constant (or create the file). 4.1b's `parseAppLink` already handles `https://<host>/invite/<token>`; add a test that an `https` universal link resolves like the `anacast://` scheme link. If 5.7 was not built, still add the route — it is independent.
7. **`docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md`.** Derive from `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` the App Store Connect "App Privacy" answers: data types collected (Contact Info: name, email, phone, physical address; Identifiers: user id, device push token; User Content: photos, survey responses, other — announcements/events submitted; Usage data: none; Diagnostics: crash data only when 6.3b's error reporting is enabled), for each: linked to the user's identity (yes for account holders), used for tracking (No — no ads, no analytics SDK), purposes ("App Functionality"); the privacy-policy URL `https://<DOMAIN>/privacy`; the "Account deletion" review note quoting decision 15 ("Delete account" archives now and permanently deletes after 30 days unless cancelled; "Deactivate" is separate) — Apple's guideline 5.1.1(v) requires the in-app deletion path 6.3a built; the age rating answers (no objectionable content; "Unrestricted Web Access" No; frequent/intense: none → 4+); App Review information (demo church + password account, same convention as 6.5; note "sign in with the password, ignore the one-time code"); export compliance (exempt, `usesNonExemptEncryption: false`). Keep a "Sign in with Apple" line: not required — the app offers only email OTP/password, no third-party or social login (guideline 4.8 applies only when a third-party login is offered).
8. **Docs and CI.** `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` gains an "iOS (step 6.4)" section that mirrors the founder checklist (enrolment, EAS-managed credentials, App Store Connect app, environment variables already set for `production`, build, submit, TestFlight internal group, device checklist, the prebuild grep check, troubleshooting: "No profiles for 'com.anacast.app' were found" → run `eas credentials -p ios` and let EAS create them; "Missing Compliance" → `usesNonExemptEncryption`; "ITMS-90683 missing purpose string" → plugin purpose strings; "Push token failed: APNs" → the push key is missing in EAS credentials for the production profile; "build number already used" → remote versioning). Replace the "iOS untested until Phase 3" paragraph. `docs/MEDIA.md`: add the iOS column (audio background + lock screen, video fullscreen/PiP, YouTube WebView inline — no background, external opens Safari view controller, PDF via Safari view controller + Share). `docs/ENV.md`: `APPLE_TEAM_ID`. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: add `pnpm --filter mobile exec expo export --platform ios` next to the Android export (JS bundle only, no Xcode; mock env). HANDOFF: an "iOS / TestFlight" block (Team ID — not secret, bundle id, ASC app id, ledger: build number, EAS build id, TestFlight date, tester count, device/iOS version results) and the founder to-dos in checklist order. Commit and push the first pass, then hand over.
9. **Second pass — TestFlight results (run when the founder pastes them).** Triage like 4.5's helper: build failures (`npx eas-cli build:view <id>` excerpt) → credentials (founder: `eas credentials -p ios`), CocoaPods/native errors (usually a version mismatch → `npx expo install --fix`, never a manual pin), or config; device failures → the layer that owns them (push permission prompt never shown → capability/handler; no lock-screen controls → Build 5's deviation; PDF opens blank → signed URL expired, re-mint (4.2a's `remint()`), or the `pageSheet` presentation; keyboard hides the OTP field → `KeyboardAvoidingView` with `behavior: 'padding'` on iOS in the auth screens; content under the notch/home indicator → `SafeAreaView` edges from `react-native-safe-area-context` (already a dependency of expo-router) in the affected screen; tab bar overlapped → expo-router `Tabs` `tabBarStyle` safe-area inset). Apple emails: "ITMS-9xxxx" codes → look up the fix, usually a config change here; Beta App Review rejection (only for external testers) → the reviewer account or the privacy URL. Add a regression test where a unit test can catch the bug; record every fix under HANDOFF "Deviations from plan" and in the TestFlight ledger for the build that carries it.

## Constraints
- No Mac is assumed anywhere: builds run on EAS, `expo prebuild --no-install` is used only to inspect the generated `Info.plist` and its output is deleted, never committed. Do not add native modules; native versions only via `npx expo install`; no `react-native-pdf`, `react-native-track-player`, `expo-av`.
- Never commit or paste an APNs key (`.p8`), App Store Connect API key, distribution certificate, provisioning profile, Apple ID password or app-specific password; EAS holds them. `prompt_history.txt` is committed verbatim.
- Do not change `android.package`, the Android PDF path, the push dispatcher on the web, migrations (never `supabase db push`), or Phase 1/2 screens beyond the iOS-specific fixes named above. Keep every change guarded by `Platform.OS === 'ios'` where it would otherwise alter Android.
- `ios.bundleIdentifier` becomes immutable once App Store Connect has the record — read HANDOFF first; if the founder already created the ASC app with a different id, use that one and record the deviation.
- Do not build a "Sign in with Apple" flow; do not add In-App Purchase (churches pay on the web through Stripe — Apple's guideline 3.1.3(b) treats a multi-tenant organisational subscription bought outside the app by the organisation as acceptable; the app must not link to the Stripe checkout — confirm no mobile screen links to `/settings/billing` or `/api/billing/*`, and record the guideline reference in `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md` "Review notes").

## Verify
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → green (new tests: `pickOpener` iOS/Android matrix, iOS push capability/permission paths, universal-link parse, AASA route 404-without-env / JSON-with-env).
- `cd apps/mobile && pnpm exec expo-doctor` → clean; `EAS_PROJECT_ID=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 npx expo config --type public | grep -E 'bundleIdentifier|usesNonExemptEncryption|associatedDomains'` → bundle id, `false`, and (with `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL` set) the applinks entry (plugin purpose strings such as `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription` are plugin props, not public config — the prebuild grep in Build 5 covers them; optionally `npx expo config --type introspect | grep -c expo-image-picker`); `npx expo export --platform ios` and `npx expo export --platform android` → clean.
- Prebuild proof: the grep commands from Build 5 print `audio`, the purpose strings and `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption` false; afterwards `git status` shows no `ios/` or `android/` directory.
- `git ls-files | grep -Ei '\.p8$|\.mobileprovision$|\.p12$'` → no output; `pnpm --filter web build` → green; `curl -s http://localhost:3000/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` → 404 without `APPLE_TEAM_ID`, JSON with it (local dev server).
- Founder-side (not you): `npx eas-cli build -p ios --profile production` succeeds, `npx eas-cli submit -p ios --profile production --latest` lands the build in TestFlight, the device checklist passes; you record the pasted results.

## Finish
- Update `HANDOFF.md` (State checklist: 6.4 "iOS-ready + docs" after the first pass, "TestFlight live" after the second; feature table row "iOS build"; the "iOS / TestFlight" block and ledger; `docs/ENV.md` variable `APPLE_TEAM_ID` in the env list; founder to-dos; "Deviations from plan" incl. the lock-screen metadata status), after the first pass leave the 6.4 checkbox in `docs/TODO.md` unticked and add the line `6.4 first pass done <date> — waiting for founder TestFlight results` under HANDOFF State; tick the checkbox only in the second pass; write `session_log.md`, commit `feat(mobile): iOS readiness — config, PDF/push/audio branches, AASA route, App Store privacy worksheet` for the first pass and `fix(mobile): TestFlight findings` for the second, push `main` (or the branch I named). If something in the plan turns out impossible or wrong, do the closest correct thing, record the deviation in HANDOFF.md under "Deviations from plan", and report it in the final message.
steps.founder_checklist:
## 6.4 — iOS / TestFlight (founder, 2–3 hours of clicking plus Apple's enrolment and processing waits; an iPhone is required, a Mac is NOT)

Run the agent prompt's first pass first, `git pull`, then follow this list; the long form is `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` → "iOS (step 6.4)". Never put a `.p8` key, certificate, provisioning profile, Apple password or app-specific password into git, a prompt or chat — EAS stores them; copies go to the vault from 0.1.

**Before you start (must already be true)**
1. HANDOFF "Applied migrations" lists every file under `supabase/migrations/` as pasted (9999, and 9998/9997 if they exist — otherwise the production build talks to a database without the join-code or survey RPCs). 6.6 is done (`https://<DOMAIN>/privacy` live, no banner); 4.5 is done (EAS project `anacast`, `EAS_PROJECT_ID` in `apps/mobile/.env`); the EAS **production** environment variables exist (created in 6.5 item 13 — if 6.5 has not run, create them now exactly as 4.5 step B but for the environment `production`: `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL` = `https://<DOMAIN>`, `EAS_PROJECT_ID`; the `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON` file variable is Android-only and harmless here). The reviewer/demo account from 6.5 item 3 exists (create it if not: demo church in `/admin`, `/o/<demo-slug>/users` → Create account → temporary password to the vault).
2. `cd apps/mobile && npx expo config --type public | grep -E 'bundleIdentifier|package'` → both print `com.anacast.app` (orchestrator decision 18); write it down. It is immutable once App Store Connect has the app.

**A. Apple Developer Program (start early — approval takes 1–2 days for individuals, longer for organisations)**
3. developer.apple.com → Account → sign in with an Apple ID using `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` and two-factor authentication → Join the Apple Developer Program → Enrol → choose Individual (your own name is the seller name shown in the App Store) or Organization (needs a D-U-N-S number and a legal entity — the one recorded in HANDOFF "Legal entity" by 6.6) → pay 99 USD per year → wait for the "Welcome" email. Then developer.apple.com → Account → Membership details → copy the **Team ID** (10 characters, not secret) into HANDOFF.md → "iOS / TestFlight" and into Vercel → Settings → Environment Variables as `APPLE_TEAM_ID` (Production) → Redeploy (this turns on the Universal Links file).

**B. Credentials and first build (EAS does the certificate work)**
4. `cd apps/mobile && npx eas-cli build -p ios --profile production` → "Do you want to log in to your Apple account?" **Yes** → Apple ID + password + the 2FA code (EAS uses the session once; nothing is stored in the repo) → let EAS **register the bundle identifier**, **generate a new Apple Distribution Certificate**, **create the provisioning profile**, and answer **Yes** to setting up **Push Notifications** (EAS creates the APNs key `AuthKey_….p8` in your developer account and keeps it) → the build queues (15–40 minutes on the free tier). If the Apple login fails, run `npx eas-cli credentials -p ios` → production → set up each item there, then rebuild.
5. When the build finishes, note the build id and the iOS build number from the build page in HANDOFF.

**C. App Store Connect record**
6. appstoreconnect.apple.com → My Apps → **+** → New App → Platforms iOS → Name `Anacast` → Primary language → Bundle ID: pick the one EAS registered → SKU `anacast` → User access Full → Create. Note the Apple ID number of the app ("App Information → General → Apple ID") in HANDOFF as the ASC app id.
7. App Information → Privacy Policy URL `https://<DOMAIN>/privacy`; Category Primary "Lifestyle" (secondary optional); Content Rights → does not contain third-party content. Save.
8. App Privacy → Get started → answer from `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md` (collects data: Yes; Contact Info, Identifiers, User Content; each "linked to identity: Yes", "used for tracking: No", purpose "App Functionality"; Diagnostics only if error reporting is on) → Publish.
9. Age Rating → questionnaire with the answers from `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md` (all "None"; result 4+) → Done.
9b. App Store → 1.0 Prepare for Submission → upload the screenshot sets listed in `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md` → "Assets" (6.7" and 6.5" iPhone, at least 3 each, taken from the TestFlight build in step 14 — the app's real palette, no mock-ups); the 1024×1024 icon is taken from the build automatically. Not needed for internal TestFlight testers, but required before external testers or review.
10. TestFlight tab → Test Information → Beta App Description (one paragraph), Feedback email `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`, Privacy Policy URL again; Sign-in required → **Yes** → the reviewer account email + password from item 1; Review notes: "Church members are invited by their church; use the password, ignore the one-time code option. Account deletion: More → Delete account (30-day grace) or https://<DOMAIN>/account/delete". (Needed only when you later add external testers, but fill it now.)

**D. Upload to TestFlight**
11. `npx eas-cli submit -p ios --profile production --latest` → log in with the Apple ID again, or — recommended for repeat use — first create an App Store Connect API key: App Store Connect → Users and Access → Integrations → App Store Connect API → Team Keys → **+** → name `eas-submit`, access **App Manager** → Download the `.p8` ONCE → `npx eas-cli credentials -p ios` → production → **App Store Connect API Key** → Upload → provide the `.p8`, Key ID and Issuer ID → then move the `.p8` to the vault and delete the download. Submit again with `--latest`.
12. App Store Connect → TestFlight → iOS builds: the build shows "Processing" (10–30 minutes), then "Ready to Test" (no "Missing Compliance" prompt thanks to the agent's `usesNonExemptEncryption: false`; if it appears anyway, answer "None of the algorithms mentioned above" / "No").
13. TestFlight → Internal Testing → **+** → group "Church leaders" → add testers: Users and Access → **+** → invite yourself and up to 100 App Store Connect users with the role Developer or Marketing (internal testers must be ASC users; no Beta App Review is needed). Enable automatic distribution → the build appears in the group.

**E. Device checklist (iPhone with the TestFlight app from the App Store)**
14. Open the TestFlight email/invite → Accept → Install Anacast → open it → sign in with a 6-digit code (or password) as an active member of the first church (4.5 item 2 — Invite + accept on the web, not Create account, if you use your super-admin email).
15. Accept the push explainer → iOS permission prompt "Anacast Would Like to Send You Notifications" → Allow → in Supabase SQL Editor `select platform, device_name from public.push_devices;` shows an `ios` row.
16. On the web publish an announcement with push on → the notification arrives on the locked iPhone → tapping opens the announcement; upload a bulletin → its push arrives; turn the Bulletins preference off in the app → the next bulletin push is suppressed.
17. Play an uploaded mp3 sermon → lock the phone → audio continues → the lock screen shows play/pause (and title/speaker if the agent could set them); play a YouTube-linked sermon → inline, stops when backgrounded (expected); a Drive-linked sermon → opens the in-app Safari view.
18. Open a bulletin PDF → renders in the in-app Safari view with the share icon → "Share" → Save to Files works; an image bulletin renders inline.
19. More tab: Privacy Policy / Terms open in Safari view; Deactivate account and Delete account rows exist and show their explanations (do not confirm them on your real account); Sign out → the `push_devices` row is gone; reopen → sign in again keeps working. If the directory (5.2b) exists: pick a household photo → the photo-library permission prompt shows the Anacast purpose sentence.
19b. If surveys (6.1c) exist: open a survey push → answer a `date` and a `multi_choice` question → "Answer saved"; as head of house answer for a child without an account.
19c. If events (5.3b) exist: submit an event → it shows as pending.
19d. Tap an invite link `https://<DOMAIN>/invite/<token>` from Mail → opens in Anacast (Universal Links; falls back to Safari when `APPLE_TEAM_ID` is unset — note which happened).
19e. With a throwaway account: More → Deactivate account → signed out → sign in again → "Restore my account" → the account and its church are back.
20. Note keyboard/safe-area problems (field hidden by the keyboard, content under the notch, tab bar under the home indicator).

**F. Hand back**
21. Paste into the agent prompt's second pass: pass/fail per item 14–20, iPhone model + iOS version, build number, any `eas build` error excerpt, any email from Apple (ITMS codes). Record in HANDOFF → "iOS / TestFlight": Team ID, bundle id, ASC app id, build number, EAS build id, TestFlight date, tester count, results.

**Done when**: the Apple Developer Program membership is active and the Team ID is in HANDOFF and Vercel; EAS holds the distribution certificate, profile and APNs key; the Anacast app exists in App Store Connect with the privacy URL and App Privacy published; a production build is "Ready to Test" in TestFlight and installed on an iPhone; items 14–20 (incl. 19b–19e where the feature exists) pass or the agent's second pass fixed them; HANDOFF's iOS block is filled.

## Goal
Turn my TestFlight results and Apple's messages into fixes or exact instructions, and fill the HANDOFF TestFlight ledger.

## Inputs / prior state

- `eas build`/`eas submit` error excerpt (`npx eas-cli build:view <id>` or the build page log): <PASTE or "none">

## Build
1. Triage each item to its layer: EAS credentials (founder: `npx eas-cli credentials -p ios` → production → the missing item; a push token failure with `APNs` in `last_error` means the push key is missing there), App Store Connect configuration (tell me the exact menu), web (`APPLE_TEAM_ID` unset → AASA 404 → Universal Links silently fall back to Safari; privacy URL), or app code (fix with a `Platform.OS === 'ios'` guard where Android would otherwise change; add a unit test where one can catch it). 3. Fill the HANDOFF "iOS / TestFlight" block from my ledger facts; set the State checklist 6.4 to done when a build is "Ready to Test" on my iPhone and the device list passes or the remaining failures are recorded as known.

## Constraints
No new native packages; no Mac-only steps; no secrets in the repo; do not touch Android behaviour or migrations; do not start another step.

## Verify
`pnpm turbo lint typecheck test`, `pnpm --filter mobile exec expo-doctor`, `npx expo export --platform ios`, `npx expo export --platform android` green; each fix has a test or a manual check I can run on the next TestFlight build.

## Finish
Update HANDOFF.md (iOS block, Deviations from plan, feature table row 'iOS build'), tick 6.4 in `docs/TODO.md`, write `session_log.md`, commit `fix(mobile): TestFlight findings`, push.

steps.notes: Revised after critique: bundle id is `com.anacast.app` with no case caveat (decision 18); iOS icon/splash/screenshots come from the decision-17 palette via `theme.ts`; `pickOpener(mimeType, platform)` keeps 4.2a's signature; the public-config grep no longer looks for plugin purpose strings; first-pass Finish leaves the checkbox unticked with a HANDOFF State line; the founder checklist checks the migration ledger first and exercises surveys, events, Universal Links and deactivate/restore on iOS. steps.founder_checklist:
## 6.5 — Google Play Console: internal testing (founder, 2–4 hours of clicking spread over several days of Google verification; agent first pass before, agent second pass after)

Run the agent prompt's first pass (Build 1–6) first, `git pull`, then follow this list. Follow `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` → "Google Play (step 6.5)" for the long form. Never put a key file, `google-services.json` or the Play service-account JSON into git, a prompt or chat; they go to the vault from 0.1.

**Before you start (must already be true)**
1. HANDOFF "Applied migrations" lists every file under `supabase/migrations/` as pasted (9999, and 9998/9997 if they exist — otherwise the production build talks to a database without the join-code or survey RPCs). 6.6 is done: `https://<DOMAIN>/privacy` shows the approved policy without a banner and `https://<DOMAIN>/account/delete` redirects a signed-out visitor to sign-in (Google's reviewer opens both). 4.5 is done: the `preview` APK runs on your phone and pushes arrive. `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` is open next to you.
2. Print the package id — `cd apps/mobile && npx expo config --type public | grep '"package"'` — and write it on paper; it is immutable from the first upload.
3. Create a demo church in `/admin` holding only fictional data, and in it a reviewer account via `/o/<demo-slug>/users` → Create account (temporary password shown once — put it in the vault). Sign in with it once in the Android app to confirm the password path works.

**A. Developer account (start early — identity verification takes 1–7 days)**
4. play.google.com/console → Create developer account → choose Personal or Organization (an organization account needs a D-U-N-S number; a personal account created after November 2023 must run a closed test with 20 testers for 14 days before it may publish to production — internal testing, which is all this step needs, is not gated). Pay the one-time 25 USD, complete identity verification, turn on 2-step verification on the Google account. Record the developer account name and date in HANDOFF.md → "Google Play".

**B. Create the app**
5. All apps → Create app → App name `Anacast` → Default language → App: "App" → Free (irreversible; keep Free) → accept the declarations → Create app. Note the Play app id from the URL (`…/app/<id>/…`) in HANDOFF.

**C. App content (Dashboard → "Set up your app" → each task, in this order)**
6. Privacy policy → `https://<DOMAIN>/privacy` → Save.
7. App access → "All or some functionality is restricted" → Add instructions → name "Reviewer account", the demo email + temporary password from item 3, note "Sign in with email and password; ignore the one-time code option" → Save.
8. Ads → "No, my app does not contain ads" → Save.
9. Content rating → Start questionnaire → email `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` → category "All other app types" → answer No to every violence/sexual/drugs/gambling item; "Does the app allow users to interact or exchange content" → Yes (announcements, surveys, directory within a closed church group); "Does the app share user-provided personal information" → Yes, with other users within the church (as the questionnaire words it) → Save → Submit. Expected rating: Everyone / PEGI 3 or Teen — either is fine.
10. Target audience and content → age groups "18 and over" only (children have no accounts) → "Could your app unintentionally appeal to children" → No → Save.
11. News apps → No. COVID-19 contact tracing and status apps → No. Government apps → No. Financial features → "My app doesn't provide any financial features" (churches pay on the web through Stripe; the app never takes payments). Health → none.
12. Data safety → Start → copy each answer from `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` (collection & security: yes collects, encrypted in transit, provides a way to request deletion → the URL `https://<DOMAIN>/account/delete`; data types per the worksheet table; purposes "App functionality" and "Account management"; no sharing with third parties except service providers; no ads/analytics). The **Account deletion** question: choose "Provides a way for users to request that their account is deleted" → URL `https://<DOMAIN>/account/delete` → in the free-text, state the 30-day window and that deactivation is separate. Save → review summary → Submit.

**D. Production build and first upload (by hand)**
13. expo.dev → project → Environment variables → environment **production** → create the same variables as 4.5 step B (`EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL` = `https://<DOMAIN>`, `EAS_PROJECT_ID`, and the secret **File** variable `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON` from the same `google-services.json`).
14. `cd apps/mobile && npx eas-cli build -p android --profile production` → reuse the keystore EAS created in 4.5 → wait → Download the `.aab` from the build page. Record the EAS build id and version code (shown on the build page) in HANDOFF.
15. Play Console → Testing → Internal testing → Create new release → if asked, "Use Google-generated key" for Play App Signing (Google keeps the signing key; your EAS keystore becomes the upload key) → upload the `.aab` → Release name (prefilled) → Release notes "First internal build" → Next → fix any listed error (agent second pass if it is not a form) → Save → Go to Testers.
16. Testers → Create email list "Church testers" → add your email and a few members' Google-account emails (≤ 100) → Save → copy the **opt-in link** → Save release → Review release → Start rollout to Internal testing. Internal testing needs no Google review.
17. On your phone (signed into a Google account on the tester list): open the opt-in link → Become a tester → Download it on Google Play → install → sign in → run the 4.5 Checkpoint C device list once more (OTP sign-in, a push from a web announcement, background audio, bulletin PDF, Deactivate and Delete rows present on More). Then the production-only checks: if 5.7 built App Links — Play Console → Setup → App integrity → copy the **App signing key certificate** SHA-256 and paste it into the agent's second-pass prompt (Play re-signs the bundle, so the preview keystore's fingerprint in `assetlinks.json` no longer matches); after the agent redeploys, tap `https://<DOMAIN>/invite/<token>` from Gmail → opens in Anacast. If surveys (6.1c) exist: answer one from a push. If the directory (5.2b) exists: pick a household photo → the permission prompt appears. Uninstall the sideloaded preview APK first if the install fails with "package conflicts".

**E. Later uploads by command (optional but recommended)**
18. Google Cloud console (the project Play created, or Firebase's) → IAM & Admin → Service accounts → Create → name `eas-submit` → Keys → Add key → JSON → download. Play Console → Users and permissions → Invite new users → the service account's email → App permissions → Anacast → "Release to testing tracks", "Manage testing tracks" → Invite. Then `cd apps/mobile && npx eas-cli credentials -p android` → select the production profile → Google Service Account → the **Play Store submissions** entry (not the FCM push key) → upload the JSON. Move the JSON to the vault and delete the download. From now on: `npx eas-cli build -p android --profile production` then `npx eas-cli submit -p android --profile production --latest`.

**F. Pre-launch report and hand-back**
19. Play Console → Testing → Pre-launch report (appears ~30 minutes after the upload) → copy the summary (crashes, accessibility, security, performance) and any policy email you receive, plus your device results from item 17, and paste them into the agent prompt's second pass. Record in HANDOFF → "Google Play": app id, package id, track "internal", version name/code, build id, upload date, opt-in link, number of testers.

**Done when**: the developer account is verified; the Anacast app exists with the package id from `app.config.ts`; App content is complete (green ticks) including Data safety with the deletion URL; a production `.aab` is on the Internal testing track and installed from the opt-in link on at least one phone; the pre-launch report has no crash or the agent fixed it; HANDOFF has the Play block filled in.

Typical cases: an app crash on a specific Android version → reproduce from the stack, fix, bump nothing by hand (remote versioning), tell me to run `npx eas-cli build -p android --profile production` and `npx eas-cli submit -p android --profile production --latest`; accessibility warnings → `accessibilityLabel`/48 dp targets in the named component; "Account deletion" policy note → confirm the URL works signed-out and the in-app path on More; "App access" → the reviewer account (archived accounts fail — check `/admin` users list); "Data safety mismatch" → correct `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` from the schema and tell me which form rows to change.
2. Fill the HANDOFF "Google Play" block from the ledger facts; mark the State checklist 6.5 done when the internal release is available and installed.

Native versions only via `npx expo install`; never change `android.package`; no secrets in the repo; no EAS commands in CI; do not start 6.4.

## Finish

steps.goal: The draft privacy policy and terms of service that step 6.3a generated from the schema become the real, founder-approved documents: the founder records the legal entity, postal address, governing state and privacy contact in HANDOFF.md, decides how the final text is produced (the 6.3a draft reviewed by a lawyer, a policy generator, or both), checks that the text covers what Anacast actually does (Supabase hosting in US East, Stripe billing for churches, push tokens, directory data shared inside the congregation and optionally with the fellowship, the Deactivate-vs-Delete paths and the 30-day window from orchestrator decision 15, no ads, no analytics SDK, error monitoring only if 6.3b's Sentry is enabled), approves the text and its effective date, and hands it to the agent. steps.prompt:
You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is step 6.6 "Privacy policy and terms of service — founder-approved text goes live" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `docs/PLAN.md` §8 (`/privacy`, `/terms`) and §11 (Phase 3 line), `docs/DESIGN.md` §5 (Account deletion paragraph), §9, §10 (More tab) and §13 risk 9, plus `HANDOFF.md` ("Legal entity" block written by the founder in this step's checklist, "Decisions", "Still open for the founder") before writing code. Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one.

## Goal
Publish the founder-approved privacy policy and terms of service. When you are done `/privacy` and `/terms` render the approved text with no draft banner and no `<…>` placeholder, show "Last updated <effective date>", the deletion/deactivation paragraph is identical to the copy both apps show on their account screens (proved by a test), the mobile sign-in screen, the More tab and the web footer link to the live pages, `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` names the live privacy-policy and account-deletion URLs, the Playwright smoke suite fails if a draft marker ever comes back, and HANDOFF.md records the effective date and the URLs. This step ships no migration and no schema change.

## Inputs / prior state
- The founder's checklist for this step (docs/TODO.md 6.6) must be complete before you start. Confirm in `HANDOFF.md` that the "Legal entity" block exists with `<LEGAL_ENTITY_NAME>`, `<POSTAL_ADDRESS>`, `<STATE>` and `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` replaced by real values, that the production domain `<DOMAIN>` is recorded (it may still be the Vercel domain `<VERCEL_URL>` — see Build 8), and that the approved text is available. The founder hands you the text in ONE of two ways: (a) files `docs/legal/privacy-approved.md` and `docs/legal/terms-approved.md` committed or placed in the working tree, or (b) pasted below this prompt under the headings `### APPROVED PRIVACY POLICY` and `### APPROVED TERMS OF SERVICE`, followed by a line `Effective date: YYYY-MM-DD`. If neither is present, stop and ask for them; do not invent legal text and do not flip `LEGAL_IS_DRAFT` on your own.
- `docs/legal/privacy-policy.md` — the placeholder privacy policy (orchestrator decision 19) that 6.3a copied verbatim into `legal.ts`; its *For counsel* notes explain each section's factual basis and are the document the lawyer starts from. Step 6.3a produced: `apps/web/src/content/legal.ts` exporting `LEGAL = { entityName, contactEmail, postalAddress, governingLaw, effectiveDate, domain }`, `LEGAL_IS_DRAFT = true`, `privacySections` and `termsSections` (arrays of `{ id, heading, paragraphs: string[] }`); `apps/web/src/features/legal/LegalPage.tsx` (h1, "Effective <date>", table of contents, the yellow "Draft for review — not yet published" banner while `LEGAL_IS_DRAFT` or any `<…>` value remains); `app/(public)/privacy/page.tsx` and `app/(public)/terms/page.tsx`; the shared copy module `apps/web/src/features/account/deletion-copy.ts`, mirrored by 6.3c's `apps/mobile/src/features/account/deletion-copy.ts` (identical strings, duplicated on purpose — never import across apps); 6.3c's `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` with the URLs `https://<DOMAIN>/privacy` and `https://<DOMAIN>/account/delete`; a smoke test asserting the pages return 200 with one h1 and the h2s "Your choices" and "Contact". Read all of these first.
- Orchestrator decision 15 (founder, 2026-09-07) shapes the copy: the self-service action "Deactivate account" archives the account (reversible; super admins restore it from `/admin`, and the recommended default lets the user restore by signing in and confirming "Restore my account"); "Delete account" stays in-app and on the web because Google Play requires it, archives immediately and schedules the real deletion `ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS = 30` days later unless the user (sign in → "Keep my account") or a super admin cancels. The approved privacy text MUST describe both paths and the window; if it does not, stop and tell the founder which sentence is missing rather than adding it yourself.
- Step 6.3b (if it ran) changed the privacy page's "Service providers" paragraph to name an error-reporting service when enabled and made `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md`'s crash-logs row conditional. Read `HANDOFF.md` to learn whether error reporting is enabled on the hosted deployment (a DSN set in Vercel/EAS) and check the approved text says the right thing.
- Mobile (4.1b, 4.3, 6.3c): `apps/mobile/app/(auth)/sign-in.tsx`, `app/(app)/(tabs)/more.tsx` (already has privacy/terms rows from 4.3 — verify), `src/lib/env.ts` `publicEnv()` exposing `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL`, `expo-web-browser` already installed. Web (2.1a, 3.8): the public layout `apps/web/app/(public)/layout.tsx` and whatever footer component exists (grep for "Privacy" in `apps/web/src/components` and `apps/web/app/(public)`).

## Build
1. **Approved text into `apps/web/src/content/legal.ts`.** Replace the draft `privacySections` and `termsSections` with the approved text, one `{ id, heading, paragraphs }` entry per heading, preserving the founder's headings and paragraph order exactly (do not edit wording, fix typos, or "improve" sentences; markdown emphasis in the source becomes plain text). Fill `LEGAL` from the HANDOFF "Legal entity" block: `entityName`, `contactEmail` (the privacy contact the founder recorded — keep it a plain string in the file; it is public information that the page must show), `postalAddress`, `governingLaw`, `effectiveDate` (ISO date from the founder's "Effective date" line), `domain` (keep reading `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`). Set `LEGAL_IS_DRAFT = false`. After the approved text is in `legal.ts`, replace `docs/legal/privacy-policy.md` with a two-line stub ("Superseded on <date> by the approved policy in `docs/legal/privacy-approved.md` and `apps/web/src/content/legal.ts`") so no placeholder text remains in the repo looking authoritative — or delete it if the founder pasted the text instead of committing a file, in which case commit the pasted text as `docs/legal/privacy-approved.md` / `terms-approved.md` yourself. Remove every `<…>` placeholder including `<PRICE>` in the terms — the founder's approved terms state the price in words (founder decision 7: flat $50 per month per church, 30-day trial, only `suspended` blocks writes; if the approved terms describe billing differently, use the founder's wording — the founder wins over the plan).
2. **`LegalPage.tsx`.** Change the "Effective <date>" line to "Last updated <date>" (formatted in the church-neutral form `Month D, YYYY` from `LEGAL.effectiveDate`), keep the table of contents, and make the draft banner impossible to show silently: keep the `LEGAL_IS_DRAFT || hasPlaceholders(sections)` check, but when it is true in a production build (`process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'`) render the banner AND log a server-side warning once, so a regression is visible in Vercel logs. Add `export const metadata` on both pages with titles "Privacy Policy — Anacast" and "Terms of Service — Anacast" and `robots: { index: true }` (these are the one public pair of pages that should be indexed; the share pages stay noindex).
3. **Deletion/deactivation paragraph in sync (both apps).** The privacy policy's deletion section must contain, word for word, the strings exported by `apps/web/src/features/account/deletion-copy.ts` (the "what deletion does", "what it does not do", "when" strings and, after decision 15, the Deactivate sentence "Deactivate account — hides you from your church and signs you out; your data is kept so an administrator can restore you later" and the Delete sentence "Delete account — permanently deletes your account and data after 30 days unless you cancel"). If the approved text phrases them differently, the founder's approved wording wins: update `deletion-copy.ts` on web AND the mobile mirror `apps/mobile/src/features/account/deletion-copy.ts` to the approved sentences (same strings, no cross-app import), and re-run both apps' existing account tests. Then add `apps/web/src/content/legal.test.ts` (Vitest): (a) every string in `DELETION_COPY` (6.3a named it `DELETION_POLICY_COPY` — the privacy-§5 sentences; `ACCOUNT_ACTION_COPY` holds the two button sentences, which the terms' Termination section must also contain verbatim) appears verbatim in the joined paragraphs of the privacy section whose `id` is the deletion section (section 5 'Your choices' in the placeholder; the approved text may renumber it — locate it by content); (b) read `../../../mobile/src/features/account/deletion-copy.ts` from disk with `node:fs` relative to the test file (use `path.resolve(__dirname, …)`; the monorepo layout is fixed) and assert each web string appears verbatim in that file's source; (c) `LEGAL_IS_DRAFT === false` and no paragraph or `LEGAL` value matches `/<[A-Z_]+>/`; (d) `LEGAL.effectiveDate` parses as a date not in the future. Test (b) is a source-text comparison, not an import — keep it that way so `apps/web` never depends on `mobile`.
4. **Links from the apps.** Web: the public footer (create `apps/web/src/components/SiteFooter.tsx` if no footer component exists yet and render it from `app/(public)/layout.tsx`, the `(auth)` layout and the `(account)` layout) shows "Privacy Policy" → `/privacy` and "Terms of Service" → `/terms` plus "© <year> <LEGAL.entityName>". Do not add the footer to the `(org)` and `(super)` shells' main content areas if they already have their own — add the two links to their existing footer or user menu instead. Also add a one-line footer with the two links to the public share page `app/(public)/s/[token]/page.tsx` (including its 404 view; keep its `noindex`/no-referrer/`X-Frame-Options` headers unchanged — it is the one page anonymous members of the public reach and the policy describes its hashed-IP records) and plain links to `${NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL}/privacy` and `/terms` at the bottom of the invitation email template in `src/lib/email/resend.ts` (3.2). Mobile: 4.1b already renders the sign-in caption "By signing in you agree to the Terms and Privacy Policy" linking to `${webUrl}/terms` and `/privacy`, and 4.3 added Privacy/Terms rows on More — refactor both to call one helper `openLegalPage(kind: 'privacy' | 'terms')` in `src/features/legal/openLegalPage.ts` (`WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync(`${publicEnv().webUrl}/${kind}`)`; `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL` is the web origin — never hard-code the domain in the app; the same URL the store listings use); add a caption only if 4.1b's is missing, never a second one. Do not add `react-native-webview` legal screens — the system browser is enough and Apple/Google accept it.
5. **`docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md`.** Replace `https://<DOMAIN>/privacy` and `https://<DOMAIN>/account/delete` with the live URLs from HANDOFF, add a line "Privacy policy effective <date>; text lives in `apps/web/src/content/legal.ts`", and confirm every row still matches the approved text (in particular the Deactivate/Delete description and the 30-day window, the "no ads, no analytics SDK" line, and the crash-logs row's conditional wording from 6.3b). If the approved text and the worksheet disagree, the approved text wins and you correct the worksheet; list every correction in your final message.
6. **Smoke test.** Extend the Playwright smoke suite (3.7a; `pnpm --filter web test:e2e:smoke`, mock env) with `apps/web/e2e/legal.smoke.spec.ts`: `/privacy` and `/terms` → status 200, exactly one `h1`, no text matching `/draft for review|placeholder|<[A-Z_]+>/i`, a "Last updated" line, links from `/` (footer) to both pages resolve, `/s/unknown` (404) still renders the two footer links, and each page contains the entity name. Keep the 6.3a assertions ("Your choices", "Contact") only if the approved headings still contain them; otherwise replace them with two headings the approved text does have and say so in the final message.
7. **Docs.** `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md`: add a "Legal pages" line (open both pages, no banner, footer links). `README.md`: one line naming where the legal text lives and that changing it requires a founder-approved effective date bump. `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md`: add "Store listings use `https://<DOMAIN>/privacy`; the app links to it from Sign in and More" under the Play (6.5) and iOS (6.4) prerequisites if those sections exist, else under a new "Store prerequisites" heading.
8. **Domain caveat.** If HANDOFF records that the production domain is still the Vercel domain, the live URLs use `https://<VERCEL_URL>`; write a HANDOFF to-do "When the custom domain is live: update Play Console privacy-policy URL, App Store Connect privacy URL, `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md`, `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md` (6.4) and EAS `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL`; the pages themselves need no change". The app never embeds the domain (it reads `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL`), so a domain change is a rebuild, not a code change.

## Constraints
- Do not write, rewrite or "tidy" legal wording. The only text in `legal.ts` is what the founder approved; if something in it contradicts what the product does (for example it promises immediate deletion while decision 15 gives a 30-day window, or it names a service provider the app does not use), stop and report the contradiction to the founder before publishing — never publish a policy that misdescribes the product.
- Never write a real email address into a prompt, commit message or `prompt_history.txt` other than the privacy contact the founder deliberately chose for the public page; keys and tokens never.
- No migration, no schema change, no new dependency on web; on mobile no new package (`expo-web-browser` is already installed; if for some reason it is missing, install it only with `npx expo install expo-web-browser`).
- Do not touch `/account/*` behaviour, the deletion RPCs, 6.3b's monitoring code, or the share pages' `noindex` headers. Keep `apps/web` free of any import from `apps/mobile` (source-text test only).
- Do not change `deletion-copy.ts` unless the approved text differs; when you do, change both copies in the same commit.

## Verify
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → green, including the new `legal.test.ts`.
- `pnpm --filter web build` → green; `pnpm --filter web test:e2e:smoke` → green including `legal.smoke.spec.ts`.
- `grep -rn "LEGAL_IS_DRAFT = true\|<LEGAL_ENTITY_NAME>\|<FOUNDER_EMAIL>\|<POSTAL_ADDRESS>\|<STATE>\|<PRICE>\|Draft for review" apps/web/src/content apps/web/app/\(public\)` → no output.
- `grep -rn "<DOMAIN>" docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` → no output; `grep -rn "<[A-Z_]\+>\|For counsel" docs/legal` → no output (the placeholder file is stubbed or deleted, the approved files carry no placeholders); `grep -c "Last updated" apps/web/src/features/legal/LegalPage.tsx` → ≥ 1.
- `cd apps/mobile && pnpm exec expo-doctor` → clean; `npx expo export --platform android` → clean; `grep -rn "openLegalPage" apps/mobile/app/(auth)/sign-in.tsx apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/more.tsx` → both hit.
- Manual (local dev server, mock env): open `/privacy` and `/terms` — no banner, "Last updated <date>", table of contents, footer links on `/`; open `/o/<slug>/dashboard` and `/admin` — the two links are reachable from their footer or user menu.
- After the founder deploys (Vercel auto-deploys `main`): `curl -sI https://<VERCEL_URL>/privacy | head -1` → `HTTP/2 200`; `curl -s https://<VERCEL_URL>/privacy | grep -ci "draft for review"` → `0`. Include both commands in your final message for the founder to run if you cannot reach the deployment.

## Finish
- Update `HANDOFF.md`: State checklist (6.6 done), the "Legal" block gains "Privacy policy and terms effective <date>; live at `https://<DOMAIN>/privacy` and `/terms`; text in `apps/web/src/content/legal.ts`; any change needs a new founder-approved effective date", the founder to-dos (domain caveat from Build 8; 6.4/6.5 may now fill in store forms), and "Deviations from plan" for anything that differed (for example changed deletion-copy strings). Remove the 6.3a to-do "fill `legal.ts` placeholders and flip `LEGAL_IS_DRAFT`".
- Tick step 6.6 in `docs/TODO.md`; write `session_log.md`; commit `feat(web): publish approved privacy policy and terms; legal links in both apps` (plus the harness attribution trailers); push `main` (or the branch I named).
- If something in the plan turns out impossible or wrong, do the closest correct thing, record the deviation in HANDOFF.md under "Deviations from plan", and report it in the final message together with the list of corrections you made to `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md`.
steps.founder_checklist:
## 6.6 — Privacy policy and terms of service (founder part first, then the agent prompt; allow 1–3 weeks if a lawyer reviews)

Both app stores refuse a listing without a live privacy-policy URL (Play Console "App content → Privacy policy"; App Store Connect "App Information → Privacy Policy URL"), and Google's reviewers read the account-deletion paragraph. Do the founder part before running the agent prompt; do not run 6.4 or 6.5 before this step is done.

**A. Record the legal facts (HANDOFF.md → new "Legal entity" block; none of this is secret)**
1. Decide who publishes Anacast: you personally (sole proprietor) or a company/non-profit. Write into `HANDOFF.md` under a heading `## Legal entity`: `Legal entity name: <LEGAL_ENTITY_NAME>` (exact registered name), `Postal address: <POSTAL_ADDRESS>` (a real mailing address is required by both stores and by most privacy laws), `Governing state: <STATE>`, `Privacy contact: <FOUNDER_EMAIL>` (an address you will read; it is printed on the public page — a role address such as privacy@ on your domain is better than a personal one), `Production domain: <DOMAIN>` (or `<VERCEL_URL>` if the custom domain from "Still open for the founder" item 2 is not live yet — see F).
2. Confirm in HANDOFF that error reporting (6.3b) is either OFF on the hosted deployment (no `SENTRY_DSN` / `EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` set) or ON; the policy's "Service providers" paragraph must match.

**B. Decide how the final text is produced**
3. Read the drafts: the privacy placeholder is `docs/legal/privacy-policy.md` in the repo (orchestrator decision 19 — step 6.3a copied it verbatim into `legal.ts`; the markdown file carries *For counsel* notes and `<…>` placeholders, so hand your lawyer or generator THAT file, not the rendered page), and the terms draft that 6.3a wrote is in `apps/web/src/content/legal.ts` (`termsSections`). The rendered pages are at `https://<VERCEL_URL>/privacy` and `/terms`. Neither is legal advice.
4. Choose one: (a) send the draft to a lawyer for review; (b) run a privacy-policy/terms generator and merge its output with the draft's factual sections; (c) both. Record the choice and the date in HANDOFF.

**C. Check the text covers what the app actually does (tick each; ask the reviewer/generator to keep every item)**
5. Hosting: data is stored with Supabase in the United States (US East) and served by Vercel; email sent by Supabase/Resend when configured.
6. Billing: churches (not members) pay a flat monthly subscription through Stripe; Stripe receives the church's payment details, Anacast never stores card numbers; 30-day trial.
7. Push notifications: an Expo push token per device is stored (`push_devices`) and deleted on sign-out, deactivation or deletion.
8. ## 6.7 — Paste the Phase 3 migrations into the hosted Supabase project and record the ledger (founder, about 20 minutes; no code)

Every migration file is re-runnable: pasting a file twice is harmless, so when in doubt paste again. Keep `docs/MIGRATIONS.md` and `supabase/README.md` (paste order) open beside this list; where they differ from it, the documents (written by the agents that wrote the files) win.

**Before you start (must already be true)**
1. `HANDOFF.md` → "Applied migrations (hosted Supabase)" lists `9999_init.sql` with a date (if it does not, finish step 2.4 first — nothing below works without the base schema). **A. Paste `9997_surveys_head_of_house.sql` (about 5 minutes)**
5. Supabase dashboard → your project → **SQL Editor** → "New query" (blank, not a template). Open `supabase/migrations/9997_surveys_head_of_house.sql` in your editor → select all → copy → paste → **Run** (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter). Expected: "Success. No rows returned" (the file's own `raise notice` lines may appear under Results/Messages). **B. Paste `9996_account_archival.sql` (only if the file exists — 6.3a case B; about 5 minutes)**

The file adds orchestrator decision 15's archival objects: columns `profiles.archived_at`, `profiles.archived_by`, `profiles.archive_reason` and `account_deletion_requests.scheduled_for`, client RPCs `deactivate_account`, `restore_my_account` and the changed `request_account_deletion`, service RPCs `srv_archive_account`, `srv_restore_account` and the changed `srv_process_account_deletions`, the `ca_profiles_*` / `ca_account_deletion_requests_*` policies and grants. Errors: item 7.
9. Paste any other unlisted file from item 3 the same way (Run, Run again, no error), highest number first.

**C. Verify (SQL Editor, new query — read-only)**
10. Run:
    ```sql
    select proname from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace
    where n.nspname = 'public' and proname in ('submit_survey_response_for','list_survey_proxy_targets') order by 1;   -- 2 rows
    select proname from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace

    select column_name from information_schema.columns
    where table_schema = 'public' and table_name = 'survey_responses' and column_name = 'answered_on_behalf';          -- 1 row

    select column_name from information_schema.columns
    where table_schema = 'public' and table_name = 'profiles' and column_name in ('archived_at','archived_by','archive_reason');  -- 3 rows
    ```
