steps.title: Production release: Play closed test → production, App Store review submission (FOUNDER+AGENT)
steps.goal: Anacast is publicly installable: on Google Play the internal build is promoted through a closed test (the minimum opted-in tester count Google shows — 20 at the rule's launch, lowered to 12 in 2025 — for 14 consecutive days when the developer account is personal and created after November 2023), production access is applied for, the store listing is published and the app is released to the chosen countries; on the App Store the TestFlight build is submitted for App Store review with the screenshots, description, keywords and review notes prepared in `docs/PLAY_STORE_LISTING.md` / `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md` and released. The agent's first pass writes the release runbook `docs/RELEASE.md` (release checklist, closed-test rule and tester invitation, production-access questionnaire answers, App Store fields, rejection playbook), adds store badges to the invite page, landing page and invitation email behind `NEXT_PUBLIC_PLAY_STORE_URL` / `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_STORE_URL`, and confirms the mobile version fields; the second pass fixes review rejections (metadata, guideline 2.1/3.1.3(b)/5.1.1(v)/1.2 questions, crashes) with tests, drafts the reviewer replies, and records the public listing URLs and the 'Store releases' ledger in HANDOFF.md.
steps.prompt:
You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is step 6.8 "Production release: Play closed test → production, App Store review submission" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `docs/PLAN.md` §7–§9 (env vars, web routes, mobile build profiles) and `docs/DESIGN.md` §10 (EAS profiles), §11 "Phase 3" (acceptance stops at a Play internal-testing build and a TestFlight build — this step closes the gap to public installs) and §13, then `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` ("Google Play (step 6.5)" and "iOS (step 6.4)"), `docs/PLAY_STORE_LISTING.md`, `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md`, `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` and the HANDOFF blocks "Google Play", "iOS / TestFlight" and "Legal entity" before writing anything. Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one.

## Goal
Anacast becomes publicly installable and the repository knows how to ship every later release. Your first pass (Build 1–6, before the founder touches the consoles) writes `docs/RELEASE.md` — the release runbook — with the release notes, the Play closed-test invitation text, the production-access questionnaire answers, the App Store listing fields and the final review notes; adds the store links to the web (`/invite/[token]` "Open in app" block, the public landing page and the invitation email) behind two new public env vars so nothing shows until the listings exist; and confirms the mobile version fields are release-ready. Your second pass (Build 7, one session per store answer) fixes whatever the reviewers, the pre-launch report or the closed testers report, drafts the reviewer replies, and finally records the public listing URLs and release ledger in `HANDOFF.md`. The founder's part is the checklist in `docs/TODO.md` 6.8; it is interleaved: first pass → founder → second pass (possibly several times) → release mode.

## Inputs / prior state
- 4.1a: `apps/mobile/app.config.ts` (dynamic config; `name: 'Anacast'`, `slug: 'anacast'`, `scheme: 'anacast'`, `version` semver, `android.package: 'com.anacast.app'` — orchestrator decision 18, `ios.bundleIdentifier` the same, `extra.eas.projectId: process.env.EAS_PROJECT_ID`); `apps/mobile/eas.json` with `cli.appVersionSource: 'remote'`, `build.production` (`autoIncrement: true`, `environment: 'production'`, Android `app-bundle`), `submit.production.android = { track: 'internal', releaseStatus: 'completed', changesNotSentForReview: false }` (6.5) and `submit.production.ios: {}` (6.4). Remote versioning means `versionCode` / `buildNumber` are bumped by EAS; only `version` lives in the repo.
- 6.5: `docs/PLAY_STORE_LISTING.md` (listing text within Play's limits, category, contact block, asset sizes, reviewer test-account block), `apps/mobile/store-assets/` (512 × 512 icon, 1024 × 500 feature graphic generated from `theme.ts` — decision 17, `scripts/assets/`), the HANDOFF "Google Play" block (app id, package id, track, version code, opt-in link, tester count). 6.4: `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md` (App Privacy data types, age rating answers, review notes: reviewer account convention, account deletion with the 30-day window, no in-app purchase per guideline 3.1.3(b), no Sign in with Apple per 4.8), the HANDOFF "iOS / TestFlight" block (Team ID, ASC app id, build number). 6.6: `apps/web/src/content/legal.ts` live, HANDOFF "Legal entity" (`<LEGAL_ENTITY_NAME>`, privacy contact, `<DOMAIN>` or `<VERCEL_URL>`), `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` naming the live URLs. 6.7: every migration in the ledger.
- Web: `apps/web/app/(auth)/invite/[token]/page.tsx` with its "Open in app" block (2.1a; deep link `anacast://` / `https://<DOMAIN>/invite/<token>` via 5.7a App Links and 6.4 Universal Links), the `(public)` landing page `/` (2.1a), the invitation email template in `apps/web/src/lib/email/resend.ts` (3.2, only sends when `RESEND_API_KEY` is set), the constants file `apps/web/src/lib/mobile-app.ts` (6.4/5.7: `ANDROID_PACKAGE`, `IOS_BUNDLE_ID`) — if 5.7a/6.4 named it differently, reuse theirs. `docs/ENV.md` and `apps/web/.env.example` list every env var (1.1, 3.8).
- Mobile: `app/(app)/(tabs)/more.tsx` (4.3; Privacy/Terms rows via `src/features/legal/openLegalPage.ts` from 6.6, Deactivate/Delete rows from 6.3c). Event submissions from members are `pending` until a leader approves them (5.3a/5.3b; `events_require_approval`); announcements, bulletins, sermons, documents and surveys are published only by permission holders — this is the factual basis for any user-generated-content answer to Apple guideline 1.2.
- The founder pastes, on the line after this prompt, the mode and its input: `first-pass` (nothing else), `review` (the full text of an Apple App Review message or Google Play policy email, or a pre-launch-report / tester observation list, plus the platform and build number), or `release` (the public Play and App Store URLs, release dates, version name/code, countries, staged percentage).

## Build
1. **`docs/RELEASE.md` (new, the runbook; first pass).** Sections, in this order: (a) *Release checklist* — `git pull`, `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test`, `pnpm --filter mobile exec expo-doctor`, `npx expo export --platform android` and `--platform ios`, bump `version` in `app.config.ts` (semver; the first public release is `1.0.0`; patch for fixes, minor for features), commit `chore(mobile): release vX.Y.Z`, `npx eas-cli build -p android --profile production` and `-p ios --profile production`, `npx eas-cli submit -p android --profile production --latest` (lands on Internal testing) and `-p ios --profile production --latest` (TestFlight), promote in the Play Console (Internal → Closed → Production; `.aab`s move between tracks without a rebuild) and create the App Store version in App Store Connect, tag `git tag mobile-vX.Y.Z && git push origin --tags`, ledger row in HANDOFF "Store releases". (b) *Google Play: the 14-day closed-test rule* — personal developer accounts created after 13 November 2023 must run a closed test with the minimum opted-in tester count Google currently shows (20 at launch, lowered to 12 in 2025 — tell the founder to read the number in the Console) for 14 consecutive days before applying for production access; organization accounts are exempt; testers must be Google accounts on the track's email list, opted in through the opt-in link and keep the app installed; a new build does not reset the clock. (c) *Closed test invitation* (plain text the founder sends to members: what Anacast is, the opt-in link placeholder `<OPT_IN_LINK>`, "keep it installed for two weeks", how to sign in with the code, whom to email problems — `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`). (d) *Production access questionnaire* — factual suggested answers (how testers were recruited: church members invited through the web; feedback channels; what changed; readiness: pre-launch report clean, Data safety and privacy policy live); mark them "edit to match what actually happened". (e) *Google Play production release* — Countries/regions, managed publishing, staged rollout and raising it, release notes template (`<en-US>` block, ≤ 500 characters) with the 1.0.0 text: sermons, announcements with notifications, bulletins, and Phase 2 features only if they shipped (check `docs/TODO.md` ticks). (f) *App Store submission* — every field of "Prepare for Submission" with its length limit and the value or the file that holds it; the final **Review notes** text (copy the base from `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md` and add: content is published by church leaders to their own congregation, members can only submit events that leaders approve before publication, leaders can remove any content; no in-app purchase because churches buy the subscription on the web and the app never links to checkout; account deletion path and the 30-day window; the reviewer account instructions); Version Release manual vs automatic; export compliance. (g) *Handling rejections* — a table of the likely guidelines (Apple 2.1, 2.3.3, 3.1.1 / 3.1.3(b), 4.2, 4.8, 5.1.1(v), 5.1.2, 1.2; Google: account deletion, Data safety mismatch, metadata, login credentials) with the prepared reply outline for each and whether it is metadata-only, a reply, or a code change; the rule "never claim a feature the app does not have — if a store requires one (for example an in-app report path for guideline 1.2), build the minimum in the second pass and record it as a deviation". (h) *Every release afterwards* — hotfix flow, Play staged rollout halt, App Store "Developer Removed from Sale" as the emergency brake, and the reminder that both stores need the privacy URL updated plus a rebuild if `<DOMAIN>` changes. Link `docs/RELEASE.md` from `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` (one line under both store sections) and from `README.md`.
2. **Store links on the web (first pass).** Add to `docs/ENV.md` and `apps/web/.env.example` two optional public variables: `NEXT_PUBLIC_PLAY_STORE_URL` (the founder sets `https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.anacast.app` once the listing is live) and `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_STORE_URL` (`https://apps.apple.com/app/id<ASC_APP_ID>`). In `apps/web/src/lib/mobile-app.ts` export `getStoreLinks(): { play?: string; appStore?: string }` that reads both, validates each with the `URL` constructor and the hosts `play.google.com` / `apps.apple.com` (anything else → ignored, so a typo cannot inject a foreign link), and returns only the valid ones; unit-test it in `mobile-app.test.ts` (unset, one set, invalid host, trailing whitespace). Create `apps/web/src/components/StoreBadges.tsx` — accessible links ("Get it on Google Play", "Download on the App Store") rendered as text-and-icon buttons in the decision-17 palette (no downloaded badge images — Google's and Apple's official badge artwork has its own usage terms; use inline SVG store glyphs you draw or plain text buttons; note this in `docs/RELEASE.md`), rendering nothing when both links are absent. Show `<StoreBadges />` (a) in the `/invite/[token]` "Open in app" block under the deep-link button, with the caption "Don't have Anacast yet? Install it, then come back to this link"; (b) on the public landing page `/` below the sign-in call to action; (c) in the invitation email template in `src/lib/email/resend.ts` as plain text lines "Android: <url>" / "iPhone: <url>" when the links exist (email clients — no component). Extend the existing invite Playwright smoke (or `apps/web/e2e/invite.smoke.spec.ts` if none covers the page) with one case: with `NEXT_PUBLIC_PLAY_STORE_URL` set in the mock env the badge link is present and points at `play.google.com`; without it nothing renders.
3. **Mobile release readiness (first pass).** Confirm `apps/mobile/app.config.ts` has `version: '1.0.0'` (set it if lower; never add `android.versionCode` or `ios.buildNumber` — remote versioning owns them) and that `eas.json` `submit.production.android.track` stays `internal` (promotion happens in the Console — do not point `eas submit` at `production`, so a mistaken `submit --latest` can never publish). Add a tiny Vitest in `apps/mobile` (or extend 4.1a's config test) asserting `version` matches `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$` and neither version-code field exists. Add the app's public store URLs to the More tab only if a "Rate / Share Anacast" row already exists — otherwise do nothing on mobile (no scope creep).
4. **CI (first pass).** Extend the mobile job of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with the `version` regex assertion from Build 3 and an assertion that `docs/RELEASE.md` exists and names the current `version`. CI stays non-blocking and runs no EAS command.
5. **Listing text review (first pass).** Read `docs/PLAY_STORE_LISTING.md` and `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md` against the shipped feature set (`docs/TODO.md` ticks, HANDOFF feature table): remove any sentence about a feature that did not ship (directory, events, surveys, documents if untick), keep every length limit (Play short 80 / full 4000 / release notes 500; Apple promotional 170 / description 4000 / keywords 100 / what's new 4000), add the "Closed test invitation" and "App Store listing" (keywords, promotional text, support URL) subsections the checklist refers to, and make sure no sentence promises moderation, analytics or features the app lacks.
6. **First-pass Finish.** Run Verify, update `HANDOFF.md` (State: 6.8 "runbook + store links, awaiting founder release"; "Store releases" heading created with an empty ledger table `| platform | version | build | date | countries | URL | notes |`; founder to-dos: set the two Vercel env vars after release, redeploy), do NOT tick 6.8, write `session_log.md`, commit, push, and tell the founder to start the checklist at item 1.
7. **Second pass — `review` mode (repeatable).** Read the pasted text. Classify each point as metadata (console edit only — write the exact new text), reply (draft the reviewer reply in a code block, factual, referencing the demo account and the docs; never promise what the app cannot do), or code. For code: reproduce where possible (unit test for a logic bug; `npx expo export` for a bundling error; the pre-launch report's stack trace mapped to the source), fix with a regression test, run the full Verify list, bump `version` (patch) and tell the founder the exact build/submit commands from `docs/RELEASE.md`. Known shapes: Apple 2.1 sign-in failure → check the reviewer notes and the demo account instructions, and that the sign-in screen's password path is discoverable (4.1b); 5.1.1(v) → verify More → Delete account copy states the 30-day window (6.3c `deletion-copy.ts`) and the web URL is in the notes; 1.2 → if Apple requires an in-app report path, add a "Report a problem" row to the More tab that opens the system mail composer to the church's contact (`organizations`/settings contact if present, else the platform privacy contact from `legal.ts`) via `expo-linking` `mailto:` — no new native dependency — and record the deviation; 3.1.1 → the reply explains the church-pays-on-the-web model (no code); Google Data safety mismatch → fix the form, not the app, unless the app really collects more than declared. Record every rejection and its resolution under HANDOFF "Store releases" → "Review log" (date, store, guideline, resolution, build). Still no tick.
8. **Second pass — `release` mode (once).** Fill the "Store releases" ledger rows for both platforms from the pasted values, add the two public URLs to HANDOFF "Decisions" (they are permanent identifiers), write the founder to-do for the two Vercel env vars if not yet set, update the HANDOFF feature table ("iOS build" → released; mobile rows → "in stores"), tick 6.8 in `docs/TODO.md`, and write the final `session_log.md`.

## Constraints
- Never write an Apple password, App Store Connect API key, Play service-account JSON, keystore, opt-in link with a personal email, tester emails or the reviewer account's password into the repo, a prompt or chat; the reviewer account's *convention* is documented, its password lives in the founder's vault.
- No new native dependencies (`npx expo install` only if unavoidable in Build 7 — prefer `expo-linking`, already installed); mobile changes limited to Build 3 and Build 7; no restyling of the invite page or landing page beyond adding the badges; the badges render nothing without the env vars, so the deployed site is unchanged until the founder sets them.
- Do not change `submit.production.android.track` to `production`; do not add `android.versionCode` / `ios.buildNumber`; do not touch `app.config.ts` identity fields (`android.package`, `ios.bundleIdentifier`, `scheme`, `slug`).
- Do not write legal wording (6.6 owns `legal.ts`); do not edit `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` except to fix a factual mismatch a store reported (then also HANDOFF "Deviations from plan").
- Store-console menu labels and policy numbers (tester count, 14 days, review durations) are as known when this prompt was written; where the founder's screen differs, keep the documented flow and note the new label in `docs/RELEASE.md`. Never `supabase db push` / `db reset`; no migration is expected in this step.

## Verify
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → green (`mobile-app.test.ts` store-link cases, the mobile version test, everything else unchanged).
- `pnpm --filter web build` → green; `pnpm --filter web test:e2e:smoke` → the invite badge case passes with and without the env var.
- `pnpm --filter mobile exec expo-doctor` → no issues; `npx expo export --platform android` and `npx expo export --platform ios` (in `apps/mobile`) → both succeed.
- `cd apps/mobile && npx expo config --type public | grep -E '"version"|versionCode|buildNumber'` → `"version": "1.0.0"` (or the bumped value) and no versionCode/buildNumber lines; `node -e "const e=require('./eas.json');if(e.submit.production.android.track!=='internal')process.exit(1)"` → exit 0.
- `git grep -n -i -E 'sk_live|AuthKey_|service-account.*\.json' -- ':!docs' ':!*.md'` → no key material; `git ls-files | grep -E '\.p8$|\.jks$|\.keystore$|service-account'` → empty.
- Manual (after the founder sets the env vars and redeploys): `curl -s https://<DOMAIN>/ | grep -c 'play.google.com'` → 1 or more; a fresh invitation email contains both store lines.

## Finish
- First pass: update `HANDOFF.md` (State checklist line for 6.8 without a tick, "Store releases" heading and empty ledger, founder to-dos for the Vercel variables, "Deviations from plan" if any), leave `docs/TODO.md` 6.8 unticked, write `session_log.md`, commit `feat(release): store links, release runbook and store-review fixes (step 6.8)`, push `main` (or the branch I named). Review passes: same, with the review log rows and `fix(mobile): <what> — store review <guideline>` commits and a `version` bump. Release mode: fill the ledger, tick 6.8 in `docs/TODO.md`, final `session_log.md`, commit `docs: store release ledger — Anacast 1.0.0 live (step 6.8)`, push. If anything in the plan turns out impossible (for example a store demands a feature the app lacks), do the closest correct thing, record it under HANDOFF "Deviations from plan", and report it in the final message.
steps.founder_checklist:
## 6.8 — Production release: Play closed test → production, App Store review (founder, about 3 hours of clicking spread over 3–5 weeks of waiting; agent first pass before, agent second pass after each store answer)

Run the agent prompt's first pass (Build 1–6) first, `git pull`, then follow this list. The long form is `docs/RELEASE.md` (written by the first pass); where it differs from this list, the document wins. Never put an Apple password, App Store Connect API key, Play service-account JSON or keystore into git, a prompt or chat — EAS holds them, copies live in the vault from 0.1. The two stores run in parallel: start the Play closed test on day 1 because its 14-day clock is the long pole, and submit to Apple the same week.

**Before you start (must already be true)**
1. 6.4 (a production iOS build is "Ready to Test" in TestFlight, App Privacy and age rating published), 6.5 (a production `.aab` is on the Internal testing track, all App content tasks green, Data safety submitted) and 6.7 (every migration in the HANDOFF ledger) are ticked. 6.6 is done and the privacy-policy URL in BOTH stores is the URL that will stay: if the custom domain `<DOMAIN>` went live after 6.4/6.5 were filled with `<VERCEL_URL>`, first update Play Console → App content → Privacy policy and App Store Connect → App Information → Privacy Policy URL, set the EAS `production` environment variable `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL` to `https://<DOMAIN>`, and rebuild both platforms (`npx eas-cli build -p android --profile production` / `-p ios`) before you release anything — the store builds bake the URL in.
2. The demo church from 6.5 item 3 has content the reviewers can see: at least one published sermon (a linked YouTube video is fine), one announcement, one bulletin, and the reviewer account's password still works in the Android app AND on the TestFlight build. Reviewers reject empty apps (Apple guideline 2.1 "App completeness").
3. `HANDOFF.md` "Google Play" and "iOS / TestFlight" blocks are filled (app ids, version code/build number of the builds you will release). Decide and write into HANDOFF → "Store releases": the countries/regions (recommended: United States and Canada — the fellowship's congregations; you can add countries later without a review), the version name `1.0.0`, and the release notes text the agent drafted in `docs/RELEASE.md`.

**A. Google Play — find out whether the 14-day closed test applies (5 minutes)**
4. play.google.com/console → Anacast → Dashboard. If the dashboard shows the task **"Apply for production access"** (personal developer accounts created after 13 November 2023), the closed-test rule applies: Google requires a closed test with a minimum number of opted-in testers (20 when the rule launched; Google lowered it to 12 in 2025 — the Console shows the current number) kept for **14 consecutive days** before you may apply. Organization accounts and older personal accounts skip A–C and go to D. Record which case you are in HANDOFF.

**B. Google Play — closed test (day 1; then wait 14 days)**
5. Testing → **Closed testing** → the default track "Alpha" (or Create track → name `Closed test`) → Manage track → Testers → Create email list `Closed testers` → add at least the required number of Google-account emails of members who own Android phones (recruit 20 to be safe: a tester who uninstalls or opts out stops counting; the agent's tester invitation text is in `docs/PLAY_STORE_LISTING.md` → "Closed test invitation"; Anacast members must also be invited to the first church through `/o/<slug>/users` so they can sign in). Save → copy the **opt-in link** (a `play.google.com/apps/testing/com.anacast.app` URL) into HANDOFF.
6. Releases → **Create new release** → **Add from library** → pick the `.aab` already on the Internal testing track (the same version code — Play promotes bundles between tracks without a rebuild; alternatively Internal testing → Releases → **Promote release** → Closed testing) → Release name prefilled → Release notes: the `<en-US>` text from `docs/RELEASE.md` → Next → resolve every error the pre-rollout page lists (warnings about missing tablet screenshots are fine) → **Save** → **Review release** → **Start rollout to Closed testing**. The first closed-test release goes through Google's review (hours to 7 days); the track page shows "In review" then "Available to testers".
7. Send the opt-in link and the invitation text to the testers. Each tester: opens the link signed into the Google account you listed → "Become a tester" → installs from Play → signs in to Anacast (OTP or password) at least once. Ask them to keep the app installed for the whole 14 days. The Console → Closed testing → Testers tab shows the opted-in count; the 14-day clock starts when the required number is reached, so check the count on day 1 and day 2.
8. During the 14 days: read Testing → Pre-launch report for the closed-test build and any tester email; paste crashes or feedback into the agent prompt's second pass. If the agent ships a fix, `npx eas-cli build -p android --profile production` then `npx eas-cli submit -p android --profile production --latest` (lands on Internal testing) → Promote release → Closed testing. A new build does not reset the 14-day clock.

**C. Google Play — apply for production access (day 15; then wait up to 7 days)**
9. Dashboard → **Apply for production access** → the questionnaire asks about your closed test (how you recruited testers, what feedback you got, what you changed, how the app is ready for production) — answer in your own words; the agent's suggested answers are in `docs/RELEASE.md` → "Production access questionnaire" (facts only; do not overstate). Submit. Google answers by email within about 7 days; if declined, the email names the reason (usually "not enough engagement" or "testing period too short") — paste it into the agent second pass, act on it, and reapply.

**D. Google Play — store listing and production release (about 45 minutes; needs production access)**
10. Grow → Store presence → **Main store listing**: App name `Anacast`; Short description (≤ 80 characters) and Full description (≤ 4000) from `docs/PLAY_STORE_LISTING.md`; App icon 512 × 512 and Feature graphic 1024 × 500 from `apps/mobile/store-assets/` (6.5); Phone screenshots: at least 4 of the ones you captured on the production build (portrait, 1080 × 1920 or the phone's native size; no device frames required) — Home, a sermon playing, an announcement, a bulletin, plus directory/survey if built; 7-inch and 10-inch tablet screenshots optional. Save.
11. Store settings → App category **Lifestyle** (or the category recorded in `docs/PLAY_STORE_LISTING.md`), Tags optional; Store listing contact details: email `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` (the privacy contact from HANDOFF "Legal entity" is best), website `https://<DOMAIN>`, phone optional. Google shows your developer name and contact email on the listing (organization accounts also show the address; check Account details → what appears publicly). Save.
12. Publishing overview → **Managed publishing** → Turn on (changes are reviewed but go live only when you click Publish — so the listing and the release appear together).
13. Release → **Production** → Countries/regions → Add countries → the list from item 3 → Save. Create new release → Add from library → the closed-test `.aab` (or the latest fixed build) → Release notes → Next → Save → Review release → **Start rollout to Production** (choose a staged rollout of 20 % if you prefer to watch crashes first; raise to 100 % later — Production → Releases → Manage rollout). Then Publishing overview → **Publish changes**. Google reviews production releases (hours to 7 days; the Dashboard shows "In review", then "Available on Google Play"). Policy emails from Google go to the developer account email — paste any into the agent second pass.
14. When live: open `https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.anacast.app` in a browser (not signed in as a tester) → the listing shows; install on a phone that was never a tester → sign in → a push from a web announcement arrives. Record in HANDOFF → "Store releases": date, version name/code, countries, staged percentage, the listing URL.

**E. App Store — prepare the version (day 1, in parallel with B; about 45 minutes)**
15. appstoreconnect.apple.com → My Apps → Anacast → App Store tab → **1.0 Prepare for Submission**. Version Information: screenshots for 6.7" and 6.5" iPhones (from 6.4 item 9b; at least 3 each, same screens as item 10; iPad screenshots are not needed unless the app supports iPad — 6.4 set `ios.supportsTablet` false); Promotional text (optional, ≤ 170), Description (≤ 4000) and Keywords (≤ 100 characters, comma-separated — the drafts are in `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md` → "App Store listing"); Support URL `https://<DOMAIN>` (a page with a way to contact you — the footer's privacy contact suffices); Marketing URL optional; Version `1.0.0`; Copyright `<YEAR> <LEGAL_ENTITY_NAME>`.
16. **Build** → **+** → select the TestFlight build from 6.4 (or the latest fixed one) → Done. If asked about export compliance, answer "No" / "None of the algorithms" (6.4 set `usesNonExemptEncryption: false`, so the question should not appear).
17. **App Review Information**: Sign-in required → **Yes** → the reviewer account email + password from 6.5 item 3; Contact information: your first/last name, phone number with country code, `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`; Notes: paste the final review notes from `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md` → "Review notes" (church members are invited by their church; use the password, ignore the one-time code option; churches pay on the web through Stripe and the app sells nothing — no in-app purchase; account deletion: More → Delete account, 30-day grace, also at `https://<DOMAIN>/account/delete`; content is published by church leaders to their own congregation, members can only submit events for leader approval). Attach nothing.
18. **Version Release**: choose **Manually release this version** (so you can publish the same day as Play) or "Automatically release". Pricing and Availability (left menu) → Price **Free** (USD 0) → Availability → the same countries as item 3 (or all) → Save. App Information → confirm the Privacy Policy URL, Category Lifestyle, Content Rights "does not contain, show or access third-party content" (the church's own sermons and documents are its own content). Age Rating shows 4+ from 6.4.
19. Top right → **Add for Review** → the summary page lists anything missing (red) → fix → **Submit to App Review**. Status: "Waiting for Review" (typically 1–2 days) → "In Review" (hours) → "Pending Developer Release" (manual) / "Ready for Sale", or **"Rejected"** with a message in App Store Connect → App Review → Messages (also emailed).

**F. Handling a rejection (either store; repeat until approved)**
20. Copy the full message (Apple: guideline number + text + any screenshot description; Google: the policy email) into the agent prompt's second pass. Do not argue in the reviewer thread before the agent has read it. Three outcomes: (a) a metadata fix (screenshots, description, notes) — you edit in the console and resubmit, no build; (b) a code fix — the agent commits, you rebuild (`npx eas-cli build -p ios --profile production` then `npx eas-cli submit -p ios --profile production --latest`; Android as item 8), select the new build in the version and resubmit; (c) a clarification — you paste the agent's drafted reply into App Review → Messages → Reply (Apple) or the Play policy appeal form and resubmit. Typical Apple questions and the answers the agent prepares: 2.1 the reviewer could not sign in or saw an empty app (check the demo church and password); 5.1.1(v) account deletion (point to More → Delete account and the web URL, with the 30-day window explained); 3.1.1/3.1.3(b) payments (churches, not users, pay on the web; the app never links to checkout); 1.2 user-generated content (leaders publish; member event submissions are approved before anyone sees them; leaders can remove anything; if Apple insists on an in-app report path the agent adds one — see the prompt); 4.2 minimum functionality (the app is for church members; the reviewer sees the demo church). Log every rejection and its resolution in HANDOFF → "Store releases".

**G. Go live and record (both stores)**
21. Apple: when the status is "Pending Developer Release", App Store → 1.0 → **Release This Version** (same day as the Play publish if you chose manual). Within 24 hours the app appears at `https://apps.apple.com/app/id<ASC_APP_ID>` (the Apple ID number from HANDOFF "iOS / TestFlight"). Install it from the App Store on an iPhone that never had the TestFlight build (or delete TestFlight's copy first) → sign in → push arrives.
22. Paste both public URLs into the agent prompt's second pass in **release** mode so it records the "Store releases" ledger, sets the Vercel env vars `NEXT_PUBLIC_PLAY_STORE_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_STORE_URL` instructions for you, and ticks the step. Then: Vercel → Settings → Environment Variables → add both URLs (Production) → Redeploy → open `https://<DOMAIN>/invite/<token>` for a fresh invitation: the "Open in app" block now shows the Google Play and App Store badges; send yourself an invitation email → the store links are in it.
23. Tell the churches: the invitation email is the onboarding path (leaders invite members from `/o/<slug>/users`; members install from the store link in the email and sign in with the code). Keep the internal/closed tracks and the TestFlight group: future builds land there first (`docs/RELEASE.md` → "Every release").

**Done when**: Play Console shows a Production release "Available on Google Play" with the store listing published (or, if the closed test is still running, the 14-day requirement is met, production access is granted and the production release is in review — record the date); App Store Connect shows "Ready for Sale"; both public URLs open the listings and a phone that was never a tester can install and sign in; every rejection is recorded with its resolution in HANDOFF "Store releases"; the Vercel store-URL variables are set and the invite page and email show the badges; docs/TODO.md 6.8 is ticked.
done_when: `docs/RELEASE.md` exists with the release checklist (version bump, build, submit, promote, tag, ledger), the Play closed-test rule and tester invitation text, the production-access questionnaire answers, the App Store submission fields with limits, the final review notes, the rejection playbook and the post-release flow; `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` and `README.md` link to it; `docs/PLAY_STORE_LISTING.md` / `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md` mention no unshipped feature and carry the 'Closed test invitation' and 'App Store listing' subsections.

`NEXT_PUBLIC_PLAY_STORE_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_STORE_URL` are in `docs/ENV.md` and `.env.example`; `getStoreLinks()` in `apps/web/src/lib/mobile-app.ts` accepts only `play.google.com` / `apps.apple.com` URLs (unit-tested); `StoreBadges` renders on `/invite/[token]` and `/` and the invitation email lists the store URLs only when set; the invite smoke case passes with and without the variable; `app.config.ts` has `version` `1.0.0` (or higher semver) and no `versionCode`/`buildNumber`; `eas.json` keeps `submit.production.android.track` = `internal`; CI asserts both.

Play Console shows a Production release 'Available on Google Play' with the store listing, screenshots and Data safety published — or, while Google's clock is still running, the closed test has the required opted-in testers for 14 days, production access is granted and the production release is in review with the date recorded in HANDOFF.

App Store Connect shows the app 'Ready for Sale' after App Store review, with screenshots, description, keywords, support URL, App Privacy and the reviewer account instructions in place; the release was triggered manually or automatically as recorded.

Every review rejection or policy email was classified and resolved — metadata edited, a reply drafted and sent, or code fixed by the agent with a regression test and a rebuilt/resubmitted build — and logged with date, store, guideline and resolution under HANDOFF 'Store releases' → 'Review log'; any store-required feature the plan lacked is recorded under 'Deviations from plan'.

HANDOFF.md 'Store releases' records both public URLs, version name/code, build ids, dates, countries and staged percentage; the two Vercel env vars are set and redeployed so `/invite/[token]`, `/` and the invitation email show the store links; a phone that was never a tester installs from each store, signs in and receives a push; `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test`, `pnpm --filter web build`, `expo-doctor` and both `expo export` platforms are green; docs/TODO.md 6.8 is ticked.
steps.commit_message: feat(release): store links, release runbook and store-review fixes (step 6.8)
reads: docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md (Google Play step 6.5 and iOS step 6.4 sections)
docs/PLAY_STORE_LISTING.md, docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md, docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md
HANDOFF.md — 'Google Play', 'iOS / TestFlight', 'Legal entity', feature table
docs/PLAN.md §7–§9 (env vars, web routes incl. /invite/[token], EAS profiles); docs/DESIGN.md §10, §11 Phase 3 acceptance, §13
docs/TODO.md steps 6.4, 6.5, 6.6 (the checklists this one continues) and 3.2 (invitation email), 2.1a (invite page 'Open in app')
steps.notes: Adopted by orchestrator decision 24 (2026-09-08) from G14's proposal; the brief there is the goal, done_when 1–4 of the sketch survive in the list above. Founder-heavy: about 3 hours of console work but 3–5 weeks of calendar time because of Google's 14-day closed test (personal accounts created after 13 Nov 2023), Google's production-access decision (≤ 7 days) and store reviews; the checklist runs both stores in parallel from day 1. Agent sessions: one first pass (M) and one short session per review answer, then a release-mode session; `estimated_session` covers the first pass. Policy facts the founder should re-check on the day (recorded as known when drafted, unverified offline): the closed-test minimum tester count (20 at launch; Google announced a reduction to 12 in 2025 — the Console shows the current number), the 14 consecutive days, organization accounts exempt, first closed-test release reviewed by Google, `.aab` promotion between tracks without a rebuild, managed publishing, Apple review typically 24–48 h, Apple's 'Manually release this version' option. Names chosen because the docs stop at 'Play internal-testing build; TestFlight build': `docs/RELEASE.md`, env vars `NEXT_PUBLIC_PLAY_STORE_URL` / `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_STORE_URL` (full URLs, host-validated, both optional; an alternative would derive the Play URL from `ANDROID_PACKAGE` and take only the ASC id — rejected to keep one mechanism), `getStoreLinks()` in `apps/web/src/lib/mobile-app.ts` (6.4's constants file; reuse 5.7a's if named differently), `apps/web/src/components/StoreBadges.tsx`, `apps/web/e2e/invite.smoke.spec.ts` only if no invite smoke exists, HANDOFF headings 'Store releases' and 'Review log', git tags `mobile-vX.Y.Z`, the closed-test track name and tester list name. Store badge artwork is deliberately NOT downloaded (Google Play and App Store badge images carry their own brand-usage terms); the component uses text buttons or hand-drawn inline SVG in the decision-17 palette — the founder may later add the official badges after reading the terms. Countries are a founder decision (recommendation United States + Canada, extendable without review). Guideline 1.2 (user-generated content): the app's content is published by permission holders and member event submissions are approved before publication, so the prepared reply is factual; if Apple still demands an in-app report path, the second pass adds a mailto 'Report a problem' row to More (no native dependency) and records a deviation — the plan has no such feature. `eas.json` keeps `submit.production.android.track: internal` on purpose so `eas submit --latest` can never publish; promotion is a Console action. The demo church for reviewers (6.5 item 3) must hold real-looking fictional content, or Apple rejects under 2.1. If the custom domain replaces the Vercel URL after 6.4/6.5, both stores' privacy URL and `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL` must change and both platforms must be rebuilt before release (checklist item 1).

proposed_additional_steps.title: Web member survey responder (optional)
proposed_additional_steps.goal: Members and leaders without the app can answer surveys on the web at `/o/[orgSlug]/surveys/[surveyId]/answer` (and the head of house for family members without accounts), reusing 6.1a's RPCs and `validateSurveyAnswers`; the survey push email/link (if Resend is configured) can point there. Optional per DESIGN §11 ('member web is optional').
done_when: `/o/[orgSlug]/surveys/[surveyId]/answer` renders the seven question kinds for any active member in the audience and submits through `submit_survey_response`.
The head of house can answer for household members without accounts through `submit_survey_response_for` on the same page.
Members without `announcements.*` permissions can reach the page (the Surveys nav entry gains a member-facing list) without seeing management controls.
Playwright smoke covers the page; `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` and `pnpm --filter web build` stay green.
reads: docs/DESIGN.md §9, §11 (member web optional)
6.1a/6.1b outputs
proposed_additional_steps.notes: Only if the founder wants web answering; not implied by the plan.
proposed_additional_steps.reason: DESIGN §10 puts survey answering in the mobile app and §11 calls a member web view optional; some congregations have members without smartphones (one shared household email, DESIGN §5), so a web responder may be wanted. Drafted as a proposal so the orchestrator/founder can decide.
proposed_additional_steps.decision: REJECTED (orchestrator decision 24, 2026-09-08): the mobile app is the survey responder for Phase 3; a web responder is a post-launch idea.

proposed_additional_steps.title: Super admin operations view (cron health, failed pushes, storage-deletion backlog)
proposed_additional_steps.goal: `/admin/ops` shows the super admin the platform's maintenance health in one place: last cron tick per phase (from a small `cron_runs` table or the Vercel Cron logs link), `notifications` counts by status across churches, failed pushes with Retry, the `storage_deletions` backlog (`processed_at is null`, `attempts >= 10`), pending `account_deletion_requests`, and paused-project hints for the Supabase Free plan. Reads via the service client in `app/(super)` Server Actions after `requireSuperAdmin()` (the tables are super-only in RLS, so the user client also works for most of them).
done_when: `/admin/ops` renders for a super admin and redirects anonymous callers to `/login?next=...`.
The page lists `notifications` counts by status for the last 7 days across all churches and links failed rows to the church's `/o/<slug>/notifications/<id>` detail page.
The `storage_deletions` backlog and `account_deletion_requests` pending counts are shown with the age of the oldest row.
`pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` and `pnpm --filter web build` stay green; the Playwright smoke covers the redirect.
reads: docs/PLAN.md §7 (Cron row)
docs/DESIGN.md §6 (super-only rows), §8
3.6b tick report shape, 6.2b notification pages
proposed_additional_steps.notes: Optional; 6.3's Sentry covers errors but not 'did the cron run'. A `cron_runs` table would need a `9996_*` migration — the step can start with the Vercel Cron logs link and in-memory phase results. Renumbered from 6.6 (see reason).
proposed_additional_steps.reason: The skeleton gives the super admin only `/admin/audit` in Phase 3; once the cron, push and storage drains exist (3.6b) the founder has no single page that says whether they are running. 6.2b builds the per-church view; a cross-church ops view is a small follow-up the orchestrator/founder may adopt or fold into 6.3's monitoring. RENUMBERED 6.6 → 6.7 on 2026-09-07: 6.6 is now the adopted privacy-policy step (orchestrator decision 16).
proposed_additional_steps.decision: REJECTED (orchestrator decision 24, 2026-09-08): post-launch; the fixer adds a "cron health / failed pushes / storage backlog" row to 6.3b's monitoring runbook instead. Id freed for the founder paste step.

open_issues: Split (orchestrator decision 13): skeleton 6.1 → 6.1a (migration `9997_surveys_head_of_house.sql` + RLS tests + `@church/domain`/`@church/db`), 6.1b (web builder, open/close with push, results, CSV), 6.1c (mobile responder + head-of-house 'answer for' + push target). Chain: 5.2b + 5.5 → 6.1a → 6.1b → 6.1c (6.1c's code needs only 6.1a; its device checklist uses 6.1b). The skeleton's `depends_on: 5.2` is repointed to `5.2b` per G12; `5.5` is kept as written because G13 is not drafted yet — the assembler should repoint it if G13 splits 5.5.

Names chosen because the docs only say 'allow head of house to submit per_person responses … adjust stamp_response_scope + policies': RPCs `submit_survey_response_for(uuid, uuid, jsonb)` and `list_survey_proxy_targets(uuid)`, helper `app.can_answer_for(uuid)` (and `app.validate_survey_answers` only if 1.3b did not factor the answer validation), column `survey_responses.answered_on_behalf`, transaction-local setting `app.answer_for`, error keys `survey_proxy_not_allowed` (42501, `detail` ∈ not_head_of_house / different_household / person_has_account / person_not_active), `survey_not_per_person` (22023), `survey_not_found` (P0002), test file `supabase/tests/rls/10_surveys_head_of_house.sql`. A new RPC was preferred over a third parameter on `submit_survey_response` because G2's 1.3b froze the client RPC signatures and PostgREST overload resolution on jsonb arguments is fragile. G2/G3 revisers should not rename the survey error keys these prompts assert on.

Founder decision 8's 'or an adult designated head when there is no father' is implemented purely through `household_role = 'head'`: only the head WITH an account can proxy. If the father has no account but the mother does, the household must make her `head` (5.2b picker, blocked for household adults until proposed 5.8's `set_head_of_house` is adopted; 5.1a's admin control works today). The founder should confirm this reading or ask for a broader rule (any household adult with an account may proxy) — that would be a one-line change in `app.can_answer_for` before 9997 is pasted.

Web has no member-facing survey responder (members answer in the app; DESIGN §11 calls a member web view optional). If leaders or members without phones must answer on the web, that is a new step after 6.1b (`/o/[slug]/surveys/[surveyId]/answer`).

The 9997 migration must be pasted into the hosted Supabase project by the founder before 6.1b/6.1c can be trialled on Vercel/Android; 6.1a adds the founder to-do and a 'ready to paste' ledger row but no founder step exists for it in the skeleton — the assembler may want a tiny FOUNDER checklist (paste 9998 if present, then 9997; record dates) or fold it into 6.3/6.4's founder items.

Push `data.url` for surveys is `/surveys/<id>` from `notificationTargetPath` (G9 3.6a, G11 4.3); 6.1c flips G11's `not_built` ignore to navigate. G9's `PushStatusBadge` retry permission map needs a `survey → announcements.edit` entry (6.1b adds it additively); G9 revisers may include it upfront.

Split (orchestrator decision 13): skeleton 6.2 → 6.2a (audit UI: `/o/[orgSlug]/audit`, `/admin/audit`, CSV export, `@church/db` `queries/audit.ts`) and 6.2b (scheduled announcements polish + `/o/[orgSlug]/notifications` delivery status). Chain: 3.6b → 6.2a → 6.2b. The skeleton's `depends_on: 3.6` is repointed to `3.6b` per G9's note; the assembler should place both after 6.1c in the M6 order (6.2b links to 5.3a's `/events` and 6.1b's `/surveys/[surveyId]` when present, and the prompts tell the agent to check the repo).

Names chosen for 6.2a because the docs stop at `/audit` and `/admin/audit`: export routes `/o/[orgSlug]/audit/export` and `/admin/audit/export` (PLAN §8 lists neither), `packages/db/src/queries/audit.ts` (`listAuditLog`, `listAuditActors`, `countAuditSince`, `AUDITED_TABLES`, `AUDIT_ACTIONS`), feature dir `apps/web/src/features/audit/`, a base64url keyset cursor (shared codec `packages/db/src/cursor.ts` from 6.2b onward), UI deny-list `NEVER_RENDER_KEYS`, and a 7-day default range on `/admin/audit` because `audit_log` has only the `(org_id, created_at desc)` index. A cross-org `audit_log (created_at desc)` index would need a `9996_*` migration — flagged, not added (founder/assembler may fold it into 6.3 or a later hardening step).

Names chosen for 6.2b because the docs do not name a delivery status page: routes `/o/[orgSlug]/notifications` and `/o/[orgSlug]/notifications/[notificationId]`, `src/features/notifications/`, helpers `listNotifications`, `countNotificationsByStatus`, `rescheduleQueuedNotification` (service), `listDeliveriesForNotification` (service), `getNotificationForOrg`, Server Actions `rescheduleAnnouncementAction`, `publishAnnouncementNowAction`, `listDeliveriesAction`; `queryKeys.notifications.list/detail` are added to 1.7a's key factory (1.7a only had `.notifications.preferences`).

6.2b widens visibility of `notification_deliveries` (super-only in RLS) to `announcements.*` holders through an org-checked Server Action with the service client, showing recipient display names and device platforms (never emails or tokens). This is a product decision the docs do not settle — recorded in the prompt's HANDOFF Decisions for the founder to veto; if vetoed, the detail page keeps only the aggregate counts 3.6a already exposes.

6.2b's `rescheduleQueuedNotification` is a service-client WRITE to `notifications` from a Server Action (after the user-client `publish_at` update). It closes the gap G9 documented (a push moved earlier waited for the old `scheduled_for`). G9 revisers may prefer to move it into 3.5a/3.6a; if so, 6.2b's Build item 2 shrinks to the UI actions. The prompt already tells the agent to reuse rather than duplicate.

6.2b's 'Coming up' strip and dashboard counts rely on 3.5a's `deriveAnnouncementState`; 6.2a's dashboard tile and 6.2b's tile both touch `src/features/org/Dashboard.tsx` additively — the assembler need not reorder anything, but critics should check the two prompts do not restyle the dashboard.

Split (orchestrator decision 13): skeleton 6.3 → 6.3a (schema proof for both decision-15 cases, `@church/domain`/`@church/db`, web `/account/*` deactivate/delete/restore, sign-in detection, super-admin `/admin/users`, privacy text copied verbatim from `docs/legal/privacy-policy.md` per decision 19 + agent-drafted terms, docs), 6.3c (mobile Deactivate/Delete/Restore screens, More rows, `deletion-copy.ts` mirror, `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md`, device checklist) and 6.3b (Sentry web + mobile behind env, `docs/MONITORING.md`, `scripts/db/security-audit.sh` SEC-01…SEC-13 + `CHECKLIST_SECURITY.md` run-through). Chain: 3.6b + 3.8 → 6.3a → 6.3c (+ 4.3) → 6.3b → 6.6 → 6.4 / 6.5. Decisions 15/16/19 say '6.3a' for legal.ts and the UI — legal.ts and the web UI stay in 6.3a; only the mobile screens and the worksheet moved to 6.3c, so the assembler should read '6.3a' in those decisions as '6.3a (web) / 6.3c (mobile, worksheet)'.

Names chosen for 6.3a/6.3c because PLAN §8 has no account routes and decision 15 gives only defaults: per-user table `profiles` (DESIGN §4.2) carries `archived_at timestamptz`, `archived_by uuid`, `archive_reason text` (`'user' | 'deletion_request' | 'admin'`); `account_deletion_requests.scheduled_for`; client RPCs `deactivate_account()`, `request_account_deletion()` (now archives + schedules), `restore_my_account()` (self-restore for reasons `user`/`deletion_request`; refuses `admin` with new error `account_archived_by_admin` 42501); service RPCs `srv_archive_account(user_id, reason)` / `srv_restore_account(user_id)`; web route group `(account)` with `/account`, `/account/deactivate`, `/account/delete`, `/account/restore` and `(public)` `/account/deactivated`, `/account/deleted`; super-admin page `/admin/users` (PLAN §8 lists no users page under `/admin`); `ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS` in `packages/domain/src/limits.ts`; `queries/account.ts` (`getMyAccountState`, service-only `listArchivedAccounts`), `queryKeys.account.state()`; `deletion-copy.ts` exports `ACCOUNT_ACTION_COPY` / `DELETION_POLICY_COPY` / `whatTheChurchKeeps` / `DELETE_CONFIRMATION_WORD`; mobile routes `app/account/{deactivate,delete,restore}.tsx`, pure router `routeForAccountState`; tests `11_account_deletion.sql`, `tick.concurrency.test.ts`, `legal.source.test.ts`, `deletion-copy.test.ts`. The G2/G3 fixers must use these names (or 6.3a adapts to theirs — the prompt says to read HANDOFF Decisions and 9999).

Names chosen for 6.3b because the docs only say 'Sentry (web + mobile) behind env': env vars `SENTRY_DSN`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`, `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`; `apps/web/src/lib/monitoring/{index,scrub}.ts`, `apps/mobile/src/lib/monitoring.ts`, `docs/MONITORING.md`, `supabase/tests/security/audit.sql`, `scripts/db/security-audit.sh`, check ids `SEC-01`…`SEC-12`. SDK versions are deliberately not pinned in the prompt: `@sentry/nextjs` must be checked against Next 16's peer range at build time (fallback: DSN-less shim, recorded in HANDOFF) and `@sentry/react-native` comes only from `npx expo install`. If the founder does not want a third-party error service at all, 6.3b shrinks to the audit script + checklist run-through (Build items 5–7) — a one-line instruction at session start.

6.3b's audit check `SEC-09` (column revokes) and `SEC-03` (anon table privileges) depend on the exact lists 1.4b chose; the prompt tells the agent to read `docs/RLS.md`, but G3 revisers may want to record those lists in a machine-readable place (e.g. a comment block in `9999_init.sql` section (9)) so the audit can cite them.
